title: God’s warning to Cain about sin
paragraphs: Study 7: God’s warning to Cain about sin
Related indexed requirements: C0008. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Connection to Christ: Romans commands resistance to sin; its teaching does not erase the difference between the Hebrew and Greek readings of Cain’s warning.
Christian response today: Resist sin through God’s grace and compare the wording before drawing a conclusion from Genesis 4:7.
Saints Translation — Law: Genesis 4:6–7 Christ and the apostles: Romans 6:12–14
Text and setting: Textual distinction
Torah: Genesis 4:6–7

In the Hebrew reading, God warns Cain about sin’s desire and his responsibility to rule over it. The Septuagint wording differs substantially, referring to offering and dividing rightly; the Saints parallel text should be compared rather than treated as identical. Romans independently commands believers not to let sin reign and locates freedom from sin in grace.
Read with Christ and the apostles: Romans 6:12–14
Connection and evidence: Related New Testament teaching. Romans commands resistance to sin; its teaching does not erase the difference between the Hebrew and Greek readings of Cain’s warning.

paragraphs: Study 10: Abraham’s call to walk faithfully before God

Jesus likewise calls His disciples to the Father’s perfection, while Paul describes continuing growth. Christian obedience is a response to grace, not proof of personal sinlessness.

title: Rejecting images as objects of worship
paragraphs: Study 20: Rejecting images as objects of worship
Related indexed requirements: C0147, C0148, C0149, C0256, C0258, C0259. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Connection to Christ: Acts and First John reject idolatry; Christian traditions distinguish images and their religious use differently.
Christian response today: Reject worship of created substitutes for God and examine the distinction between art, veneration and worship.
Saints Translation — Law: Exodus 20:4–6 · Exodus 25:18–22 Christ and the apostles: Acts 17:29 · 1 John 5:21
Text and setting: Moral teaching
Torah: Exodus 20:4–6 · Exodus 25:18–22

The prohibition joins making images with bowing to and serving them. The same Torah also commands cherubim in the sanctuary, so the passages require more care than a blanket ban on every work of art. Christian traditions differ over religious images; all must reckon with the rejection of idolatry and created substitutes for God.
Read with Christ and the apostles: Acts 17:29 · 1 John 5:21
Connection and evidence: Explicit New Testament treatment. Acts and First John reject idolatry; Christian traditions distinguish images and their religious use differently.

title: Rejecting divination and occult direction
paragraphs: Study 85: Rejecting divination and occult direction

Related indexed requirements: C0033, C0241, C0590, C0628, C0629, C0630, C1071, C1072, C1073, C1074, C1075, C1076. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Connection to Christ: Acts describes converts renouncing magic, and Galatians condemns sorcery.
Christian response today: Seek God’s guidance and renounce occult practices without labeling unfamiliar people or ordinary care as sorcery without evidence.
Saints Translation — Law: Leviticus 19:26 · Deuteronomy 18:9–14 Christ and the apostles: Acts 19:18–20 · Galatians 5:19–21
Text and setting: Moral teaching
Torah: Leviticus 19:26 · Deuteronomy 18:9–14

The Torah prohibits divination and related practices that seek guidance or power apart from the Lord. The instruction concerns the practices named; unfamiliar cultures or ordinary medical treatments should not be labeled sorcery without evidence.

verses.text: And when Abram was ninety-nine years old, the Lord appeared to Abram and said to him, “I am your God; be pleasing before Me, and be blameless.
And I will set My covenant between Me and you, and will multiply you exceedingly.”
And Abram fell upon his face; and God spoke to him, saying,
“As for Me, behold, My covenant is with you, and you shall be a father of a multitude of nations.
And your name shall no longer be called Abram, but your name shall be Abraham; for I have made you a father of many nations.
And I will increase you exceedingly, exceedingly, and will make nations of you; and kings shall come from you.
And I will establish My covenant between Me and you and your seed after you throughout their generations, as an everlasting covenant, to be your God and the God of your seed after you.
And I will give to you, and to your seed after you, the land where you live as a stranger, all the land of Canaan, as an everlasting possession; and I will be their God.”
And God said to Abraham, “And you shall keep My covenant, you and your seed after you throughout their generations.
And this is the covenant that you shall keep, between Me and you, and your seed after you throughout their generations: every male among you shall be circumcised.
And you shall be circumcised in the flesh of your foreskin; and it shall be a sign of the covenant between Me and you.

And every male child among you, eight days old, shall be circumcised throughout your generations, the slave born in your house, and the slave bought with silver from any foreigner who is not of your seed.
The slave born in your house, and the slave bought with silver, shall surely be circumcised; and My covenant shall be upon your flesh as an everlasting covenant.
And the uncircumcised male who is not circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin on the eighth day, that soul shall be destroyed from his kindred; for he has broken My covenant.”
And God said to Abraham, “Sara your wife shall no longer be called Sara, but Sarah shall be her name.
And I will bless her, and will give you a child by her; and I will bless him, and he shall become nations, and kings of nations shall come from him.”
And Abraham fell upon his face and laughed, and said in his mind, “Shall a child be born to a man a hundred years old? And shall Sarah, who is ninety years old, bear a child?”
And Abraham said to God, “Let this Ishmael live before Thee.”

And God said to Abraham, “Yes; behold, Sarah your wife shall bear you a son, and you shall call his name Isaac. And I will establish My covenant with him as an everlasting covenant, and with his seed after him.
And concerning Ishmael, behold, I have heard you. Behold, I have blessed him, and I will increase him and multiply him exceedingly; he shall beget twelve nations, and I will make him a great nation.

title: Leviticus 19:1–37 · Parents, Sabbath, idols, offerings, gleaning, honesty, wages, disability, justice, speech, love, mixtures, fruit, occult practices, elders and weights

Leviticus 19:1 — And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Leviticus 19:2 — Speak unto the congregation of the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: You shall be holy, for I am holy, the Lord your God.
Leviticus 19:3 — Each shall revere his father and his mother, and you shall keep My Sabbaths. I am the Lord your God.
Leviticus 19:4 — You shall not follow idols, neither shall you make cast gods for yourselves; I am the Lord your God.
Leviticus 19:5 — And if you sacrifice a sacrifice of deliverance unto the Lord, you shall sacrifice it so that it is acceptable for you.
Leviticus 19:6 — It shall be eaten on the day when you sacrifice it and on the morrow; and if any remains until the third day, it shall be burned with fire.
Leviticus 19:7 — If it is eaten at all on the third day, it is unfit for sacrifice; it shall not be accepted.
Leviticus 19:8 — But he that eats it shall bear sin, for he has profaned the holy things of the Lord; and the souls that eat shall be destroyed from among their people.
Leviticus 19:9 — And when you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not wholly reap the harvest of your field; and you shall not gather what falls from your harvest,
Leviticus 19:10 — neither shall you glean your vineyard again, nor gather the grapes of your vineyard; you shall leave them for the poor and the resident foreigner; I am the Lord your God.
Leviticus 19:11 — You shall not steal. You shall not lie. No one shall defraud his neighbour.
Leviticus 19:12 — And you shall not swear by My name for an unjust cause, and you shall not profane the name of your God. I am the Lord your God.
Leviticus 19:13 — You shall not wrong your neighbour, neither shall you rob; and the wages of the hired worker shall in no wise remain with you overnight until morning.
Leviticus 19:14 — You shall not speak evil of the deaf, neither shall you put a stumbling block before the blind; and you shall fear the Lord your God; I am the Lord your God.

Leviticus 19:15 — You shall do no injustice in judgment; you shall not favour the person of the poor, neither shall you admire the person of the mighty; you shall judge your neighbour in righteousness.
Leviticus 19:16 — You shall not go about deceitfully among your nation; you shall not conspire against the blood of your neighbour; I am the Lord your God.
Leviticus 19:17 — You shall not hate your brother in your mind; you shall surely reprove your neighbour, and you shall not bear sin because of him.
Leviticus 19:18 — And your hand shall not take vengeance, neither shall you remain angry with the sons of your people; and you shall love your neighbour as yourself; I am the Lord.

Leviticus 19:19 — You shall keep My law; you shall not mate your livestock with a different stock, neither shall you sow your vineyard with a different kind, nor put upon yourself a spurious garment woven of two materials.

Leviticus 19:20 — And if anyone lies with a woman with an emission of semen, and she is a household slave reserved for a man but has not been ransomed or given freedom, there shall be an inquiry concerning them. They shall not die, because she has not been freed.
Leviticus 19:21 — And he shall bring his guilt offering unto the Lord beside the door of the Tent of Testimony, a ram for a guilt offering.
Leviticus 19:22 — And the priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering before the Lord for the sin he has committed, and the sin he has committed shall be forgiven him.

Leviticus 19:23 — But when you enter the land which the Lord your God gives unto you, and plant any tree for food, you shall purge its uncleanness; its fruit shall be unpurged unto you three years; it shall not be eaten.
Leviticus 19:24 — And in the fourth year all its fruit shall be holy, praiseworthy unto the Lord.
Leviticus 19:25 — But in the fifth year you shall eat the fruit; its produce shall be an increase unto you; I am the Lord your God.
Leviticus 19:26 — You shall not eat on the mountains. You shall not divine by omens or observe birds for divination.
Leviticus 19:27 — You shall not make a sisoe from the hair of your head or spoil the appearance of your beards.
Leviticus 19:28 — And you shall make no incisions in your body for a dead person, neither shall you put tattooed letters upon yourselves; I am the Lord your God.
Leviticus 19:29 — You shall not profane your daughter by making her a prostitute, lest the land prostitute itself and the land be filled with lawlessness.
Leviticus 19:30 — You shall keep My Sabbaths and revere My holy things. I am the Lord.
Leviticus 19:31 — You shall not follow spirit mediums, neither shall you attach yourselves unto enchanters, to be defiled by them; I am the Lord your God.
Leviticus 19:32 — You shall rise before the face of the grey-haired, and honour the person of an elder, and fear your God; I am the Lord your God.
Leviticus 19:33 — If a resident foreigner comes to you in your land, you shall not oppress him.

Leviticus 19:34 — The resident foreigner who approaches you shall be as the native among you; and you shall love him as yourself, for you were resident foreigners in the land of Egypt; I am the Lord your God.
Leviticus 19:35 — You shall do no injustice in judgment, in measures, weights, or scales.
Leviticus 19:36 — You shall have just scales, just weights, and a just chous. I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.
Leviticus 19:37 — And you shall keep all My law and all My ordinances, and do them; I am the Lord your God.

title: Leviticus 26:1–46 · No idols; Sabbath and sanctuary reverence; obedience, blessings, discipline, confession and covenant remembrance
paragraphs: Passage group: No idols; Sabbath and sanctuary reverence; obedience, blessings, discipline, confession and covenant remembrance. Setting: Covenant obligations and sanctions.
Requirements appearing in this passage: C0129, C0147, C0636, C0738, C0739. A mixed passage can link to more than one topic or classification.

Leviticus 26:1 — You shall not make for yourselves images made by hand, neither carved images, nor shall you set up a pillar for yourselves, nor place a conspicuous stone in your land to bow down unto it; I am the Lord your God.
Leviticus 26:2 — You shall keep My Sabbaths and revere My holy things. I am the Lord.
Leviticus 26:3 — If you walk in My ordinances, keep My commandments, and do them,
Leviticus 26:4 — then I will give you rain in its season. The land shall yield its produce, and the trees of the fields shall yield their fruit.
Leviticus 26:5 — And your threshing shall reach the grape harvest, and the grape harvest shall reach the sowing. You shall eat your bread to satisfaction and dwell securely in your land.
Leviticus 26:6 — And war shall not pass through your land. I will give peace in your land. You shall lie down, with no one to frighten you, and I will destroy harmful animals from your land.
Leviticus 26:7 — And you shall pursue your enemies, and they shall fall before you in slaughter.
Leviticus 26:8 — And five of you shall pursue a hundred, and a hundred of you shall pursue tens of thousands; and your enemies shall fall before you by the sword.
Leviticus 26:9 — And I will look upon you, increase you, multiply you, and establish My covenant with you.
Leviticus 26:10 — And you shall eat old stores and old stores of old stores, and clear out the old before the new.
Leviticus 26:11 — And I will place My covenant among you, and My soul shall not abhor you;
Leviticus 26:12 — and I will walk among you and be your God, and you shall be My people.
Leviticus 26:13 — I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt while you were slaves. I shattered the bond of your yoke and led you with boldness.
Leviticus 26:14 — But if you do not obey Me and do not do these ordinances of Mine,
Leviticus 26:15 — but disobey them, and your soul is indignant at My judgments, so that you do not do all My commandments, so as to dissolve My covenant,

Leviticus 26:16 — then I will do this to you: I will bring distress upon you, scab and jaundice that waste your eyes and melt away your life. You shall sow your seeds in vain, and your adversaries shall eat them.
Leviticus 26:17 — And I will set My face against you, and you shall fall before your enemies. Those who hate you shall pursue you, and you shall flee when no one pursues you.
Leviticus 26:18 — And if up to this point you do not obey Me, I will discipline you seven times more for your sins.
Leviticus 26:19 — And I will shatter the arrogance of your pride, and make your heaven iron, and your land as bronze;
Leviticus 26:20 — and your strength shall be in vain. Your land shall not yield its seed, and the tree of your field shall not yield its fruit.
Leviticus 26:21 — And if after these things you walk crookedly and will not obey Me, I will add seven blows upon you according to your sins.
Leviticus 26:22 — And I will send the wild animals of the land against you. They shall devour you, consume your livestock, and make you few, so that your roads become desolate.
Leviticus 26:23 — And if by these things you are not disciplined, but walk crookedly toward Me,
Leviticus 26:24 — then I too will walk with you in contrary anger, and I too will strike you seven times in return for your sins.
Leviticus 26:25 — And I will bring upon you a sword exacting the penalty of the covenant. You shall flee into your cities, and I will send death among you; you shall be handed into enemies’ hands.
Leviticus 26:26 — When I afflict you with a scarcity of bread, ten women shall bake your bread in one oven and give back your bread by weight. You shall eat and in no wise be filled.
Leviticus 26:27 — If after these things you do not obey Me, but walk crookedly toward Me,
Leviticus 26:28 — then I Myself will walk with you in contrary anger, and I will discipline you seven times according to your sins.
Leviticus 26:29 — And you shall eat the flesh of your sons, and the flesh of your daughters you shall eat.
Leviticus 26:30 — And I will lay waste your pillars, and destroy your wooden images made by hand, and place your limbs upon the limbs of your idols; and My soul shall be indignant with you;
Leviticus 26:31 — and I will make your cities desolate, and lay waste your holy places; and I will in no wise smell the savour of your sacrifices;
Leviticus 26:32 — and I Myself will desolate your land, and your enemies who dwell in it shall marvel at it.
Leviticus 26:33 — And I will scatter you among the nations, and the advancing sword shall consume you. Your land shall become desolate, and your cities shall be desolate.
Leviticus 26:34 — Then the land shall welcome its Sabbaths and all the days of its desolation, and you shall be in your enemies’ land. Then the land shall keep Sabbath and welcome its Sabbaths.
Leviticus 26:35 — All the days of its desolation it shall keep Sabbath for the Sabbaths it did not keep during your Sabbaths when you inhabited it.

Leviticus 26:36 — And upon those who remain of you I will bring cowardice into their heart in the land of their enemies; and the sound of a leaf borne along shall pursue them; and they shall flee as those fleeing from war, and fall when none pursues;
Leviticus 26:37 — and brother shall disregard brother as in war, though no one runs after them. You shall not be able to withstand your enemies.
Leviticus 26:38 — And you shall perish among the nations, and your enemies’ land shall devour you.
Leviticus 26:39 — And those who remain of you shall be ruined because of your sins; they shall waste away in the land of their enemies.
Leviticus 26:40 — And they shall confess their sins and their fathers’ sins, because they transgressed and disregarded Me, and because they walked crookedly before Me.
Leviticus 26:41 — And I too walked with them in contrary anger, and I will destroy them in their enemies’ land. Then their uncircumcised heart will feel shame, and then they will accept their sins.

verses.text: You shall not make for yourselves images made by hand, neither carved images, nor shall you set up a pillar for yourselves, nor place a conspicuous stone in your land to bow down unto it; I am the Lord your God.
You shall keep My Sabbaths and revere My holy things. I am the Lord.
If you walk in My ordinances, keep My commandments, and do them,
then I will give you rain in its season. The land shall yield its produce, and the trees of the fields shall yield their fruit.
And your threshing shall reach the grape harvest, and the grape harvest shall reach the sowing. You shall eat your bread to satisfaction and dwell securely in your land.
And war shall not pass through your land. I will give peace in your land. You shall lie down, with no one to frighten you, and I will destroy harmful animals from your land.
And you shall pursue your enemies, and they shall fall before you in slaughter.
And five of you shall pursue a hundred, and a hundred of you shall pursue tens of thousands; and your enemies shall fall before you by the sword.
And I will look upon you, increase you, multiply you, and establish My covenant with you.
And you shall eat old stores and old stores of old stores, and clear out the old before the new.
And I will place My covenant among you, and My soul shall not abhor you;
and I will walk among you and be your God, and you shall be My people.
I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt while you were slaves. I shattered the bond of your yoke and led you with boldness.
But if you do not obey Me and do not do these ordinances of Mine,
but disobey them, and your soul is indignant at My judgments, so that you do not do all My commandments, so as to dissolve My covenant,
then I will do this to you: I will bring distress upon you, scab and jaundice that waste your eyes and melt away your life. You shall sow your seeds in vain, and your adversaries shall eat them.
And I will set My face against you, and you shall fall before your enemies. Those who hate you shall pursue you, and you shall flee when no one pursues you.
And if up to this point you do not obey Me, I will discipline you seven times more for your sins.
And I will shatter the arrogance of your pride, and make your heaven iron, and your land as bronze;
and your strength shall be in vain. Your land shall not yield its seed, and the tree of your field shall not yield its fruit.
And if after these things you walk crookedly and will not obey Me, I will add seven blows upon you according to your sins.
And I will send the wild animals of the land against you. They shall devour you, consume your livestock, and make you few, so that your roads become desolate.
And if by these things you are not disciplined, but walk crookedly toward Me,
then I too will walk with you in contrary anger, and I too will strike you seven times in return for your sins.
And I will bring upon you a sword exacting the penalty of the covenant. You shall flee into your cities, and I will send death among you; you shall be handed into enemies’ hands.
When I afflict you with a scarcity of bread, ten women shall bake your bread in one oven and give back your bread by weight. You shall eat and in no wise be filled.
If after these things you do not obey Me, but walk crookedly toward Me,
then I Myself will walk with you in contrary anger, and I will discipline you seven times according to your sins.
And you shall eat the flesh of your sons, and the flesh of your daughters you shall eat.
And I will lay waste your pillars, and destroy your wooden images made by hand, and place your limbs upon the limbs of your idols; and My soul shall be indignant with you;
and I will make your cities desolate, and lay waste your holy places; and I will in no wise smell the savour of your sacrifices;
and I Myself will desolate your land, and your enemies who dwell in it shall marvel at it.
And I will scatter you among the nations, and the advancing sword shall consume you. Your land shall become desolate, and your cities shall be desolate.
Then the land shall welcome its Sabbaths and all the days of its desolation, and you shall be in your enemies’ land. Then the land shall keep Sabbath and welcome its Sabbaths.
All the days of its desolation it shall keep Sabbath for the Sabbaths it did not keep during your Sabbaths when you inhabited it.

And upon those who remain of you I will bring cowardice into their heart in the land of their enemies; and the sound of a leaf borne along shall pursue them; and they shall flee as those fleeing from war, and fall when none pursues;
and brother shall disregard brother as in war, though no one runs after them. You shall not be able to withstand your enemies.
And you shall perish among the nations, and your enemies’ land shall devour you.
And those who remain of you shall be ruined because of your sins; they shall waste away in the land of their enemies.
And they shall confess their sins and their fathers’ sins, because they transgressed and disregarded Me, and because they walked crookedly before Me.
And I too walked with them in contrary anger, and I will destroy them in their enemies’ land. Then their uncircumcised heart will feel shame, and then they will accept their sins.
And I will remember the covenant of Jacob and the covenant of Isaac, and the covenant of Abraham I will remember; and I will remember the land.

And the land shall be abandoned by them. Then the land shall receive its Sabbaths when it is desolated because of them, and they shall accept their lawless deeds, because they disregarded My judgments and were indignant at My ordinances in their soul.
And yet even so, while they were in their enemies’ land, I did not disregard them or become indignant with them so as to consume them and dissolve My covenant with them, for I am the Lord their God.
And I will remember for them the former covenant, when I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of a house of slavery, before the nations to be their God. I am the Lord.
These are the judgments and the ordinances and the law which the Lord gave between Himself and the sons of Israel on Mount Sinai by the hand of Moses.

and you shall destroy all who inhabit the land before you, remove their lookout places, destroy all their cast idols, and remove all their pillars.

Deuteronomy 5:28 — And the Lord heard the voice of your words as you spoke unto me; and the Lord said unto me: I have heard the voice of the words of this people, which they have spoken unto you; all that they have spoken is right.

You shall not bow down unto them, neither shall you serve them; for I am the Lord your God, a jealous God, repaying the sins of fathers upon children, unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate Me,

verses.text: At that time the Lord said unto me: Hew for yourself two tablets of stone like unto the first, and come up unto Me into the mountain; and you shall make for yourself an ark of wood.
And I will write upon the tablets the words which were upon the first tablets, which you broke; and you shall put them in the ark.
And I made an ark of decay-resistant wood, and hewed two tablets of stone like unto the first; and I went up into the mountain, with the two tablets in my hands.
And He wrote upon the tablets, according to the first writing, the ten words which the Lord spoke unto you in the mountain out of the midst of the fire; and the Lord gave them unto me.
And I turned and came down from the mountain, and put the tablets into the ark which I had made; and they were there, as the Lord commanded me.
And the sons of Israel set out from Beeroth of the sons of Iakim to Misadai. Aaron died there and was buried there, and his son Eleazar served as priest in his place.
From there they set out to Gadgad, and from Gadgad to Jotbathah, a land of flowing torrents.
At that time the Lord set apart the tribe of Levi, to bear the ark of the covenant of the Lord, to stand before the Lord to minister, and to bless in His name, unto this day.
Therefore the Levites have no portion or inheritance among their brethren; the Lord Himself is his inheritance, as He spoke unto him.
And I abode in the mountain forty days and forty nights; and the Lord hearkened unto me at that time also, and the Lord would not destroy you.
And the Lord said unto me: Go, set forth before this people, and let them enter and inherit the land which I sware unto their fathers to give them.

And now, O Israel, what does the Lord your God require of you, but to fear the Lord your God, to walk in all His ways, and to love Him, and to serve the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul,
to keep the commandments of the Lord your God, and His ordinances which I command you this day, that it may be well with you?
Behold, unto the Lord your God belong heaven and the heaven of heaven, the earth and all that is therein.
Yet the Lord preferred your fathers, to love them, and chose their seed after them, even you, above all the nations, as at this day.
And you shall circumcise your hardness of heart, and shall stiffen your neck no more.
For the Lord your God, He is God of gods and Lord of lords, the great and mighty and fearful God, who shows no partiality, neither takes a bribe;
who executes judgment for the sojourner, and the orphan, and the widow, and loves the sojourner, to give him bread and clothing.
And you shall love the sojourner, for you were sojourners in the land of Egypt.
You shall fear the Lord your God, and you shall serve Him, and you shall cleave unto Him, and you shall swear by His name.
He is your boast, and He is your God, who has done among you these great and glorious things which your eyes have seen.
Your fathers went down into Egypt with seventy souls; but now the Lord your God has made you as the stars of heaven in multitude.

And if a Levite comes from any of your cities, from among all the sons of Israel where he sojourns, according to the desire of his soul, unto the place which the Lord shall choose,
then he shall minister in the name of the Lord his God, as do all his brethren the Levites who stand there before the Lord.
He shall eat an allotted portion, apart from the sale according to his ancestral family.
And when you enter the land which the Lord your God gives you, you shall not learn to do after the abominations of those nations.
There shall not be found among you one who purifies his son or his daughter by fire, or practises divination, or interprets spoken omens, or observes auguries, or works sorcery,
or chants spells, or is a medium, or observes portents, or inquires of the dead.
For everyone who does these things is an abomination unto the Lord your God; for because of these abominations the Lord shall destroy them from before you.
You shall be perfect before the Lord your God.
For these nations whose possession you inherit hearken unto omens and divinations; but the Lord your God has not granted you so to do.
The Lord your God shall raise up unto you a prophet from among your brethren, like unto me; you shall hearken unto him,

according to all that you asked of the Lord your God in Horeb, in the day of the assembly, saying: We will no more hear the voice of the Lord our God, neither will we see this great fire any more, lest we die.
And the Lord said unto me: All that they have spoken is right.
I will raise up for them a prophet from among their brethren, like unto you, and will put My word in his mouth; and he shall speak unto them all that I command him.
And the man who will not hearken unto whatsoever the prophet shall speak in My name, I will exact retribution from him.
But the prophet who shall act ungodly, speaking in My name a word which I commanded him not to speak, or who shall speak in the name of other gods, that prophet shall die.
And if you say in your heart: How shall we know the word which the Lord has not spoken?

Whatsoever the prophet speaks in the name of the Lord, if the word does not come to pass, nor is fulfilled, that is the word which the Lord has not spoken. That prophet has spoken in ungodliness; you shall not spare him.

Deuteronomy 29:1 — And Moses called all the sons of Israel, and said unto them, You have seen all that the Lord did in the land of Egypt before you unto Pharaoh, and unto his servants, and unto all his land:
Deuteronomy 29:2 — the great trials which your eyes have seen, the signs, and those great wonders.
Deuteronomy 29:3 — And the Lord God has not given you a heart to know, and eyes to see, and ears to hear, unto this day.
Deuteronomy 29:4 — And He led you forty years in the wilderness; your garments did not grow old, and your sandals did not wear away from your feet.
Deuteronomy 29:5 — You ate no bread, and drank no wine or strong drink, that you might know that He is the Lord your God.
Deuteronomy 29:6 — And you came unto this place; and Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan came out to meet us in battle, and we smote them.
Deuteronomy 29:7 — And we took their land, and I gave it as an inheritance unto Reuben, and unto Gad, and unto the half tribe of Manasseh.
Deuteronomy 29:8 — And you shall take heed to do all the words of this covenant, that you may understand all that you shall do.
Deuteronomy 29:9 — You stand all this day before the Lord your God: your tribal chiefs, and your elders, and your judges, and your recording officers, every man of Israel,
Deuteronomy 29:10 — your wives, and your children, and the sojourner who is in the midst of your camp, from your woodcutter unto your water carrier,
Deuteronomy 29:11 — that you may enter into the covenant of the Lord your God, and into His curses, which the Lord your God covenants with you this day;
Deuteronomy 29:12 — that He may establish you unto Himself for a people, and He shall be your God, as He said unto you, and as He sware unto your fathers, Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob.
Deuteronomy 29:13 — And not with you alone do I make this covenant and this curse,
Deuteronomy 29:14 — but also with those who are here with us this day before the Lord your God, and with those who are not here with us this day.
Deuteronomy 29:15 — For you know how we dwelt in the land of Egypt, and how we passed through the midst of the nations through which you passed.
Deuteronomy 29:16 — And you saw their abominations and their idols, wood and stone, silver and gold, which are among them.

Deuteronomy 29:17 — Is there among you a man, or woman, or family, or tribe, whose mind has turned aside from the Lord your God, to go and serve the gods of those nations? Is there among you a root springing up in gall and bitterness?

Deuteronomy 29:18 — And it shall be, if he hears the words of this curse and pronounces a blessing in his heart, saying, May it be well with me, though I walk in the wandering of my heart—so that the sinner may not destroy the guiltless with him—

Deuteronomy 29:20 — And the Lord shall set him apart for evils from all the sons of Israel, according to all the curses of the covenant which are written in this book of the law.

Deuteronomy 29:24 — And they shall say, Because they forsook the covenant of the Lord, the God of their fathers, which He made with their fathers when He brought them forth out of the land of Egypt;
Deuteronomy 29:25 — and they went and served other gods, and bowed down unto them, whom they did not know, and whom He had not allotted unto them.
Deuteronomy 29:26 — And the Lord was kindled in wrath against that land, to bring upon it all the curses which are written in this book of the law.
Deuteronomy 29:27 — And the Lord removed them from their land in wrath, and anger, and exceeding great indignation, and cast them into another land, as it is now.
Deuteronomy 29:28 — The hidden things belong unto the Lord our God; but the things revealed belong unto us and unto our children for ever, that we may do all the words of this law.

Is there among you a man, or woman, or family, or tribe, whose mind has turned aside from the Lord your God, to go and serve the gods of those nations? Is there among you a root springing up in gall and bitterness?

And it shall be, if he hears the words of this curse and pronounces a blessing in his heart, saying, May it be well with me, though I walk in the wandering of my heart—so that the sinner may not destroy the guiltless with him—

God will in no wise be willing to be merciful unto him; but then the anger of the Lord and His jealousy shall blaze against that man, and all the curses of this covenant which are written in this book of the law shall cleave unto him, and the Lord shall blot out his name from under heaven.
And the Lord shall set him apart for evils from all the sons of Israel, according to all the curses of the covenant which are written in this book of the law.

And the generation to come, your sons who shall arise after you, and the foreigner who shall come from a far land, shall speak; and they shall see the plagues of that land and its diseases, which the Lord has sent upon it—

sulfur and salt, burned over; all its land shall neither be sown nor sprout, neither shall any green thing grow upon it, as at the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, which the Lord overthrew in wrath and anger—
and all the nations shall say, Why has the Lord done thus unto this land? What does this great heat of anger mean?
And they shall say, Because they forsook the covenant of the Lord, the God of their fathers, which He made with their fathers when He brought them forth out of the land of Egypt;
and they went and served other gods, and bowed down unto them, whom they did not know, and whom He had not allotted unto them.
And the Lord was kindled in wrath against that land, to bring upon it all the curses which are written in this book of the law.
And the Lord removed them from their land in wrath, and anger, and exceeding great indignation, and cast them into another land, as it is now.
The hidden things belong unto the Lord our God; but the things revealed belong unto us and unto our children for ever, that we may do all the words of this law.

category: Marriage, family and care for parents
title: Marriage and the one-flesh union
paragraphs: Study 6: Marriage and the one-flesh union
This study preserves narrative teaching, a promise or a permission without adding a new item to the individual-command total.
Connection to Christ: Jesus expressly appeals to the one-flesh union when teaching about marriage.
Christian response today: Honor marital fidelity while respecting the New Testament’s recognition of singleness.
Saints Translation — Law: Genesis 2:24 Christ and the apostles: Matthew 19:4–6 · 1 Corinthians 7:7
Text and setting: Creation
Torah: Genesis 2:24

Genesis describes a man leaving his parents and being joined to his wife. Jesus expressly uses this passage when teaching about marriage and fidelity. It supports the marriage bond; it does not command everyone to establish a separate household or marry. Paul’s recognition of singleness remains part of the same biblical witness.
Read with Christ and the apostles: Matthew 19:4–6 · 1 Corinthians 7:7
Connection and evidence: Explicit New Testament treatment. Jesus expressly appeals to the one-flesh union when teaching about marriage.

paragraphs: Study 13: Teaching the household God’s way
Related indexed requirements: C0978, C0989, C0990. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Connection to Christ: Ephesians and Second Timothy carry household instruction into Christian nurture and learning.
Christian response today: Teach children Scripture patiently, including its meaning, setting and practical demands.
Saints Translation — Law: Genesis 18:19 · Deuteronomy 6:6–7 Christ and the apostles: Ephesians 6:4 · 2 Timothy 3:14–15
Text and setting: Command and narrative
Torah: Genesis 18:19 · Deuteronomy 6:6–7

God’s statement about Abraham concerns instructing his household in righteousness and justice. Deuteronomy gives Israel an explicit responsibility to teach its children. Christian parents likewise receive a duty of nurturing instruction. Teaching should include the meaning and setting of a passage, rather than presenting every ancient law as an identical rule for every child today.
Read with Christ and the apostles: Ephesians 6:4 · 2 Timothy 3:14–15
Connection and evidence: Explicit New Testament treatment. Ephesians and Second Timothy carry household instruction into Christian nurture and learning.

Christian response today: Honor marital fidelity and do not infer a general permission for multiple spouses from a narrowly stated prohibition.

Text and setting: Family law

The verse prohibits taking a woman as a rival to her sister during the sister’s lifetime. The lifetime qualification must not be omitted. The provision addresses an ancient marriage situation; Christian teaching about marriage must also include Jesus’ appeal to the one-flesh union rather than infer general approval of multiple wives from this restriction.

paragraphs: Study 149: Divorce regulation and Jesus’ teaching
Related indexed requirements: C1166. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Connection to Christ: Jesus expressly distinguishes the Mosaic divorce concession from the creation ideal; Paul addresses further circumstances.
Christian response today: Take fidelity and Jesus’ teaching seriously, and seek careful pastoral guidance where Christian applications differ.

Torah: Deuteronomy 24:1–4

Deuteronomy regulates a case involving divorce, remarriage and return to the first husband; it is not a command to divorce. Jesus explicitly distinguishes Mosaic concession from the creation ideal. Paul addresses further pastoral circumstances. Christian traditions differ over some applications, so the study should present these texts together rather than manufacture one unrestricted rule.
Read with Christ and the apostles: Matthew 19:3–9 · Mark 10:2–12 · 1 Corinthians 7:10–16

verses.text: And if there is a dispute between men, and they come unto judgment, and the judges judge them, and justify the righteous, and condemn the ungodly,
then it shall be, if the ungodly man is worthy of stripes, that you shall seat him before the judges, and they shall scourge him before them, by number according to his ungodliness.
They shall give him forty stripes, and shall not add thereto; lest, if they add more stripes beyond these, your brother be dishonoured before you.
You shall not muzzle an ox when it treads out the grain.

And if brethren dwell together, and one of them dies, and has no seed, the wife of the dead shall not be married outside unto a man who is not near of kin. Her husband’s brother shall go in unto her, and take her unto himself for a wife, and dwell with her as husband.
And it shall be, that the child whom she bears shall be established in the name of the dead, and his name shall not be blotted out of Israel.

And if the man will not take his brother’s wife, the woman shall go up unto the gate, unto the elders, and say: My husband’s brother will not raise up his brother’s name in Israel; my husband’s brother has refused.
And the elders of his city shall call him, and speak unto him; and if he stands and says: I will not take her,

then his brother’s wife shall draw near before the elders, and loose one sandal from his foot, and spit in his face, and answer and say: Thus shall they do unto the man who will not build up his brother’s house.
And his name shall be called in Israel: The House of Him Whose Sandal Was Loosed.
And if men strive together, a man with his brother, and the wife of one draws near to deliver her husband out of the hand of him that strikes him, and puts forth her hand, and seizes his testicles,
you shall cut off her hand; your eye shall not spare her.
You shall not have in your pouch differing weights, a great and a small.
You shall not have in your house differing measures, a great and a small.
You shall have a true and just weight, and you shall have a true and just measure, that your days may be long upon the land which the Lord your God gives you for a possession.
For everyone who does these things, everyone who does injustice, is an abomination unto the Lord your God.
Remember what Amalek did unto you in the way, when you came forth out of Egypt,
how he withstood you in the way, and smote your rear, those who were weary behind you, when you were hungry and weary; and he did not fear God.

And it shall be, when the Lord your God gives you rest from all your enemies round about you, in the land which the Lord your God gives you for a possession to inherit, that you shall blot out the name of Amalek from under heaven. You shall not forget.

title: Justice in cases of violence, theft and loss
paragraphs: Study 32: Justice in cases of violence, theft and loss

Related indexed requirements: C0020, C0173, C0174, C0175, C0176, C0177, C0178, C0179, C0180, C0181, C0182, C0183, C0184, C0185, C0186, C0187, C0188, C0189, C0190, C0191, C0192, C0193, C0194, C0195, C0196, C0197, C0198, C0199. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Connection to Christ: Romans distinguishes public authority from private vengeance, providing guidance for reading Israel’s judicial cases.
Christian response today: Seek lawful justice and protection for the injured; do not impose ancient penalties on your own authority.
Saints Translation — Law: Exodus 21:12–36 (KJV 21:12–36) · Exodus 22:1–16 (KJV 22:2–17) Christ and the apostles: Romans 12:19 · Romans 13:1–4
Text and setting: Civil law

The guide’s broad heading about offenders is treated here as a study of several judicial cases, not a single all-purpose rule. Exodus distinguishes intention, negligence, evidence and restitution. These were Israel’s civil ordinances. Christian readers must distinguish lawful public justice from private vengeance and must not reenact ancient penalties on their own authority.
Read with Christ and the apostles: Romans 12:19 · Romans 13:1–4
Connection and evidence: Related New Testament teaching. Romans distinguishes public authority from private vengeance, providing guidance for reading Israel’s judicial cases.

Numbers 35:7 — All the towns you shall give the Levites shall be forty-eight towns, together with their outlying lands.

Numbers 35:8 — And for the towns that you shall give from the possession of the sons of Israel, take many from those with much and fewer from those with less. Each shall give towns to the Levites according to the inheritance he receives.
Numbers 35:9 — And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:

Numbers 35:11 — and you shall set apart towns for yourselves. They shall be refuges for the killer to flee there, anyone who has struck a person unintentionally.
Numbers 35:12 — And the towns shall be refuges for you from the kinsman who avenges blood, so that the killer shall in no wise die before standing before the congregation for judgment.
Numbers 35:13 — And the towns you shall provide, the six towns, shall be refuges for you.
Numbers 35:14 — You shall provide three towns across the Jordan, and you shall provide three towns in the land of Canaan.

Numbers 35:15 — There shall be a refuge for the sons of Israel; for the sojourner and the resident stranger among you, these towns shall also be refuges, so that anyone who strikes a person unintentionally may flee there.
Numbers 35:16 — But if he strikes someone with an iron object and that person dies, he is a murderer. Let the murderer surely be put to death.
Numbers 35:17 — If he strikes someone with a stone from his hand capable of causing death and that person dies, he is a murderer. Let the murderer surely be put to death.
Numbers 35:18 — If he strikes someone with a wooden object from his hand capable of causing death and that person dies, he is a murderer. Let the murderer surely be put to death.
Numbers 35:19 — The kinsman who avenges blood shall himself kill the murderer. When he encounters him, he shall kill him.

Numbers 35:23 — or, without his knowing, a stone capable of causing death falls upon him and he dies, though he was not his enemy and was not seeking to harm him,
Numbers 35:24 — And then the congregation shall judge between the one who struck him and the kinsman who avenges blood according to these judgments.

Numbers 35:28 — For he must live in the city of refuge until the high priest dies. After the death of the high priest, the killer may return to the land of his possession.
Numbers 35:29 — And these shall be an ordinance of judgment for you throughout your generations in all your settlements.
Numbers 35:30 — In every case of a person being struck down, you shall put the killer to death through witnesses. A single witness shall not testify against a person so as to cause his death.

Numbers 35:32 — You shall not accept a ransom concerning flight to a city of refuge, allowing him to live in the land again before the high priest dies.

Numbers 35:34 — And you shall not defile the land in which you dwell, in which I will dwell among you, for I am the Lord, dwelling among the sons of Israel.

verses.text: These are the words which Moses spoke unto all Israel beyond the Jordan, in the wilderness toward the west, near the Red Sea, between Paran, Tophel, Laban, Aulon, and Katachrysea.
It is a journey of eleven days from Horeb by the way of Mount Seir unto Kadesh-barnea.

And it came to pass in the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, that Moses spoke unto all the sons of Israel, according to all that the Lord had commanded him concerning them.
After he had smitten Sihon king of the Amorites, who dwelt in Heshbon, and Og king of Bashan, who dwelt in Ashtaroth and in Edrei,
beyond the Jordan, in the land of Moab, Moses began to make this law plain, saying:
The Lord our God spoke unto us in Horeb, saying: Let it suffice you to have dwelt in this mountain.

Turn and set forth, and enter the hill country of the Amorites and all the neighbouring places of Arabah, the hill country and the plain, the southwest and the seacoast, the land of the Canaanites and Anti-Lebanon, as far as the great river Euphrates.
Behold, I have delivered the land before you. Enter and inherit the land which I sware unto your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, to give unto them and unto their seed after them.
And I spoke unto you at that time, saying: I shall not be able to bear you alone.
The Lord your God has multiplied you, and behold, you are this day as the stars of heaven in multitude.
The Lord, the God of your fathers, make you a thousand times as many as you are, and bless you, as He has spoken unto you.
How shall I alone be able to bear your trouble, and your resistance, and your disputes?
Choose for yourselves wise men, men of knowledge and understanding, for your tribes, and I will appoint them to rule over you.
And you answered me and said: The thing which you have spoken is good to do.

And I took from among you wise men, men of knowledge and understanding, and appointed them to rule over you, captains of thousands, and captains of hundreds, and captains of fifties, and captains of tens, and recording officers for your judges.
And I commanded your judges at that time, saying: Hear the matters between your brethren, and judge justly between a man and his brother and the sojourner with him.

You shall not show partiality in judgment; you shall judge the small and the great alike. You shall not shrink before the face of man, for judgment belongs unto God. And you shall bring unto me the matter which is too hard for you, and I will hear it.
And I commanded you at that time all the things which you should do.

And we departed from Horeb, and went through all that great and fearful wilderness which you saw, by the way of the hill country of the Amorite, as the Lord our God commanded us; and we came unto Kadesh-barnea.
And I said unto you: You have come unto the hill country of the Amorite, which the Lord our God gives you.
Behold, the Lord your God has delivered the land before you. Go up and inherit it, as the Lord, the God of your fathers, has spoken unto you; fear not, neither be dismayed.

And you all came unto me, and said: Let us send men before us, and let them search out the land for us, and bring us word of the way by which we shall go up, and of the cities into which we shall enter.
And the saying pleased me; and I took twelve men from among you, one man from each tribe.
And they turned and went up into the hill country, and came unto the Valley of the Cluster, and searched it out.
And they took of the fruit of the land in their hands, and brought it down unto us, and said: The land which the Lord our God gives us is good.
And you would not go up, but disobeyed the word of the Lord your God.
And you murmured in your tents, and said: Because the Lord hates us, He brought us forth out of the land of Egypt, to deliver us into the hands of the Amorites, to destroy us.

Whither do we go up? Your brethren have made your heart fail, saying: The nation is great and numerous and mightier than we; and the cities are great and walled up to heaven. Moreover, we have seen sons of giants there.
And I said unto you: Neither cower nor fear them.
The Lord your God, who goes before you, shall Himself fight against them with you, according to all that He did for you in the land of Egypt,
and in this wilderness which you saw, how the Lord your God nurtured you as a man nurtures his son, in all the way which you went, until you came unto this place.
And in this matter you did not trust the Lord your God,
who goes before you in the way to choose a place for you, guiding you in fire by night, to show you the way wherein you should go, and in a cloud by day.
And the Lord heard the voice of your words, and, being provoked to anger, sware, saying:
Surely none of these men shall see this good land which I sware unto their fathers,
save Caleb son of Jephunneh. He shall see it, and I will give unto him and unto his sons the land whereon he trod, because he cleaved unto the things of the Lord.
And the Lord was angry with me also for your sakes, saying: You shall not enter there either.
Joshua son of Nun, who stands beside you, he shall enter there. Strengthen him, for he shall cause Israel to inherit it.
And every young child who this day knows neither good nor evil shall enter there; and I will give it unto them, and they shall inherit it.
But you, turn and encamp in the wilderness by the way of the Red Sea.

And you answered me and said: We have sinned before the Lord our God. We will go up and fight, according to all that the Lord our God commanded us. And you took up, every man, his weapons of war, and gathered yourselves together, and went up into the hill country.
And the Lord said unto me: Say unto them, You shall not go up, neither shall you fight, for I am not with you; and you shall not be crushed before your enemies.
And I spoke unto you, but you did not hearken unto me; and you transgressed the word of the Lord, and forced your way up into the hill country.
And the Amorites who dwelt in that hill country came out to meet you, and pursued you as bees do, and wounded you from Seir unto Hormah.
And you sat down and wept before the Lord; but the Lord did not hearken unto your voice, neither gave He heed unto you.
And you dwelt in Kadesh many days, as many days as you dwelt there.

verses.text: And when the Lord your God destroys the nations whose land your God gives you, and you inherit their possession, and dwell in their cities and in their houses,
you shall set apart three cities for yourself in the midst of your land which the Lord your God gives you.
Mark out the way for yourself, and divide into three parts the territory of your land which the Lord your God apportions unto you; and there shall be a refuge there for every slayer.
And this shall be the ordinance for the slayer who shall flee thither and live: whosoever strikes his neighbour unintentionally, having borne him no hatred aforetime,

as when a man goes with his neighbour into the forest to gather wood, and his hand is jolted with the axe as he cuts the wood, and the iron slips from the wood and strikes his neighbour, so that he dies, he shall flee unto one of these cities and live;

lest the kinsman who avenges blood pursue the slayer while his heart is hot, and overtake him, if the way is long, and strike him mortally, so that he dies, though no sentence of death is due unto him, for he bore his neighbour no hatred aforetime.
Therefore I command you this thing, saying: You shall set apart three cities for yourself.
And if the Lord your God enlarges your borders, as He sware unto your fathers, and the Lord gives you all the land which He promised to give unto your fathers,
if you hearken to do all these commandments which I command you this day, to love the Lord your God, and to walk in all His ways all your days, then you shall add three cities more unto these three,
that innocent blood may not be shed in your land which the Lord your God gives you for a possession, and that there may be none guilty of blood among you.
But if a man hates his neighbour, and lies in wait for him, and rises up against him, and strikes him mortally, so that he dies, and flees unto one of these cities,
then the elders of his city shall send and take him thence, and deliver him into the hands of the kinsman who avenges blood, and he shall die.
Your eye shall not spare him; and you shall cleanse the guilt of innocent blood from Israel, and it shall be well with you.
You shall not remove your neighbour’s boundaries, which your fathers set in your inheritance, which was allotted unto you in the land which the Lord your God gives you for a possession.

One witness shall not suffice to testify against a man concerning any injustice, or any trespass, or any sin which he sins. At the mouth of two witnesses, and at the mouth of three witnesses, shall every matter be established.
And if an unrighteous witness rises up against a man, accusing him of ungodliness,
then the two men between whom is the dispute shall stand before the Lord, and before the priests, and before the judges who shall be in those days.
And the judges shall inquire diligently; and behold, if the unrighteous witness has testified falsely, and has stood against his brother,
then you shall do unto him as he wickedly purposed to do unto his brother; and you shall remove the evil one from among yourselves.
And those who remain shall hear and fear, and shall no more do such an evil thing among you.
Your eye shall not spare him: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.

title: The prohibition of murder
paragraphs: Study 24: The prohibition of murder
Related indexed requirements: C0156. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Connection to Christ: Jesus carries the prohibition of murder into anger and the need for reconciliation.
Christian response today: Protect life, address destructive anger and seek reconciliation; do not read fulfillment as permission to harm.
Saints Translation — Law: Exodus 20:15 (KJV 20:13) Christ and the apostles: Matthew 5:21–24 · Romans 13:9–10
Text and setting: Moral teaching
Torah: Exodus 20:15 (KJV 20:13)

The command prohibits murder or wrongful killing; “do not kill” can obscure its legal context when taken to prohibit every taking of life without distinction. Jesus addresses anger and reconciliation at the command’s root. This entry does not resolve all Christian disagreements about war, self-defense or capital punishment.
Read with Christ and the apostles: Matthew 5:21–24 · Romans 13:9–10

Numbering note: The Saints Translation follows the Greek order: adultery at 20:13, theft at 20:14 and murder at 20:15. Each link now opens the matching command in the Saints chapter. The corresponding KJV number is shown separately.
Connection and evidence: Explicit New Testament treatment. Jesus carries the prohibition of murder into anger and the need for reconciliation.

Where interpretations differ: War, self-defense and capital punishment; the rejection of murder itself is not being set aside. Read the biblical passages together and distinguish a tradition’s conclusion from the wording of the text. Compare interpretive approaches.

title: Exodus 21:1–11 · Hebrew servants, release, households, female servants and protected marital provisions
paragraphs: Passage group: Hebrew servants, release, households, female servants and protected marital provisions. Setting: Civil law.
Requirements appearing in this passage: C0164, C0165, C0166, C0167, C0168, C0169, C0170, C0171, C0172. A mixed passage can link to more than one topic or classification.
Exodus 21:1 — “And these are the ordinances which you shall set before them.
Exodus 21:2 — If you acquire a Hebrew slave, he shall serve you for six years; and in the seventh year he shall go out free, without payment.
Exodus 21:3 — If he comes in alone, he shall go out alone; but if a wife comes in with him, his wife shall also go out with him.
Exodus 21:4 — But if his master gives him a wife, and she bears him sons or daughters, the wife and the children shall be his master’s, and he shall go out alone.
Exodus 21:5 — But if the slave answers and says, ‘I love my master, and my wife, and my children; I will not go out free,’
Exodus 21:6 — his master shall bring him before God’s tribunal, and then bring him to the door, to the doorpost. His master shall pierce his ear with an awl, and he shall serve him for ever.
Exodus 21:7 — And if a man sells his own daughter as a household slave, she shall not go out as the female slaves go out.
Exodus 21:8 — If she does not please her master, who pledged her to himself, he shall redeem her; he has no right to sell her to a foreign nation, because he has broken faith with her.
Exodus 21:9 — But if he pledges her to his son, he shall deal with her according to the ordinance for daughters.
Exodus 21:10 — And if he takes another wife to himself, he shall not deprive her of her necessities, her clothing, or her conjugal companionship.
Exodus 21:11 — But if he does not do these three things for her, she shall go out freely, without silver.

verses.text: “And these are the ordinances which you shall set before them.
If you acquire a Hebrew slave, he shall serve you for six years; and in the seventh year he shall go out free, without payment.
If he comes in alone, he shall go out alone; but if a wife comes in with him, his wife shall also go out with him.
But if his master gives him a wife, and she bears him sons or daughters, the wife and the children shall be his master’s, and he shall go out alone.
But if the slave answers and says, ‘I love my master, and my wife, and my children; I will not go out free,’
his master shall bring him before God’s tribunal, and then bring him to the door, to the doorpost. His master shall pierce his ear with an awl, and he shall serve him for ever.
And if a man sells his own daughter as a household slave, she shall not go out as the female slaves go out.
If she does not please her master, who pledged her to himself, he shall redeem her; he has no right to sell her to a foreign nation, because he has broken faith with her.
But if he pledges her to his son, he shall deal with her according to the ordinance for daughters.
And if he takes another wife to himself, he shall not deprive her of her necessities, her clothing, or her conjugal companionship.
But if he does not do these three things for her, she shall go out freely, without silver.

title: Lending without exploiting the needy
paragraphs: Study 36: Lending without exploiting the needy
Related indexed requirements: C0205, C0206. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Connection to Christ: Jesus teaches generous lending; applying Israel’s interest provisions to modern banking requires further interpretation.
Christian response today: Lend mercifully and refuse to profit by exploiting another person’s desperation.
Saints Translation — Law: Exodus 22:24 (KJV 22:25) · Deuteronomy 23:20–21 (KJV 23:19–20) Christ and the apostles: Luke 6:34–35
Text and setting: Economic law
Torah: Exodus 22:24 (KJV 22:25) · Deuteronomy 23:20–21 (KJV 23:19–20)

Exodus prohibits charging interest to the poor among God’s people; Deuteronomy distinguishes lending to an Israelite brother and to a foreigner. Those distinctions should be stated rather than omitted. Jesus teaches generosity in lending. Christian judgments about modern banking vary; the text clearly opposes exploiting need for personal advantage.
Read with Christ and the apostles: Luke 6:34–35
Connection and evidence: Related New Testament teaching. Jesus teaches generous lending; applying Israel’s interest provisions to modern banking requires further interpretation.
These passages support a related teaching or moral application. The connection is not presented as a direct quotation of this exact Torah rule.

Where interpretations differ: Interest, usury and applications to modern banking. Read the biblical passages together and distinguish a tradition’s conclusion from the wording of the text. Compare interpretive approaches.

title: Numbers 36:1–13 · Heiresses marry within their ancestral tribe; tribal allotments must not transfer
paragraphs: Passage group: Heiresses marry within their ancestral tribe; tribal allotments must not transfer. Setting: Inheritance law.
Requirements appearing in this passage: C0953, C0954. A mixed passage can link to more than one topic or classification.

Numbers 36:1 — And the rulers of the tribe of the descendants of Gilead son of Machir, son of Manasseh, from the tribe of Joseph’s descendants, approached and spoke before Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the rulers of the ancestral houses of the sons of Israel.

Numbers 36:2 — And they said: The Lord commanded our lord to distribute the inherited land by lot to the sons of Israel, and the Lord instructed the lord to give the inheritance of our brother Zelophehad to his daughters.

Numbers 36:3 — And if they become wives in one of the Israelite tribes, their allotment will be taken from our fathers’ possession and added to the inheritance of the tribe into which they marry. It will be taken from our inherited allotment.

Numbers 36:4 — If the release comes for the sons of Israel, their inheritance will be added to the inheritance of the tribe into which they marry, and their inheritance will be taken from the inheritance of our ancestral tribe.
Numbers 36:5 — And Moses commanded the sons of Israel by the Lord’s instruction, saying: Thus speaks the tribe of Joseph’s descendants.
Numbers 36:6 — This is the word that the Lord prescribed concerning Zelophehad’s daughters: Let them marry whom they please, but they shall marry from their father’s clan.
Numbers 36:7 — And no inheritance among the sons of Israel shall pass from tribe to tribe, for each Israelite shall hold fast to the inheritance of his ancestral tribe.

Numbers 36:8 — And every daughter who succeeds as next of kin to an inheritance among the Israelite tribes shall marry someone from her father’s clan, so that each Israelite may succeed as next of kin to his paternal inheritance.
Numbers 36:9 — And no allotment shall pass from one tribe to another; rather, the sons of Israel shall each hold fast to their own inheritance.
Numbers 36:10 — Zelophehad’s daughters did as the Lord had prescribed unto Moses.
Numbers 36:11 — And Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, Noah, and Mahlah, the daughters of Zelophehad, married their cousins.
Numbers 36:12 — They married within the clan of Manasseh, of Joseph’s descendants, and their inheritance remained with the tribe of their father’s clan.
Numbers 36:13 — These are the commandments, ordinances, and judgments that the Lord commanded through Moses on the western side of Moab, by the Jordan opposite Jericho.

verses.text: And the rulers of the tribe of the descendants of Gilead son of Machir, son of Manasseh, from the tribe of Joseph’s descendants, approached and spoke before Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the rulers of the ancestral houses of the sons of Israel.

And they said: The Lord commanded our lord to distribute the inherited land by lot to the sons of Israel, and the Lord instructed the lord to give the inheritance of our brother Zelophehad to his daughters.

And if they become wives in one of the Israelite tribes, their allotment will be taken from our fathers’ possession and added to the inheritance of the tribe into which they marry. It will be taken from our inherited allotment.

If the release comes for the sons of Israel, their inheritance will be added to the inheritance of the tribe into which they marry, and their inheritance will be taken from the inheritance of our ancestral tribe.
And Moses commanded the sons of Israel by the Lord’s instruction, saying: Thus speaks the tribe of Joseph’s descendants.
This is the word that the Lord prescribed concerning Zelophehad’s daughters: Let them marry whom they please, but they shall marry from their father’s clan.
And no inheritance among the sons of Israel shall pass from tribe to tribe, for each Israelite shall hold fast to the inheritance of his ancestral tribe.

And every daughter who succeeds as next of kin to an inheritance among the Israelite tribes shall marry someone from her father’s clan, so that each Israelite may succeed as next of kin to his paternal inheritance.
And no allotment shall pass from one tribe to another; rather, the sons of Israel shall each hold fast to their own inheritance.
Zelophehad’s daughters did as the Lord had prescribed unto Moses.
And Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, Noah, and Mahlah, the daughters of Zelophehad, married their cousins.
They married within the clan of Manasseh, of Joseph’s descendants, and their inheritance remained with the tribe of their father’s clan.
These are the commandments, ordinances, and judgments that the Lord commanded through Moses on the western side of Moab, by the Jordan opposite Jericho.

verses.text: At the end of seven years you shall make a release.

And this is the ordinance of the release: you shall release every debt of yours which your neighbour owes you; and you shall not exact it of your brother, for a release unto the Lord your God has been proclaimed.
Of a foreigner you may exact whatsoever he owes you; but you shall release your brother’s debt unto you.
For there shall be none in need among you; for the Lord your God shall surely bless you in the land which the Lord your God gives you for a possession, to inherit it,
if you diligently hearken unto the voice of the Lord your God, to keep and do all these commandments which I command you this day.

And if your brother, a Hebrew man or a Hebrew woman, is sold unto you, he shall serve you six years; and in the seventh year you shall send him forth free from you.
And when you send him forth free from you, you shall not send him away empty.

And you shall remember that you were a household slave in the land of Egypt, and the Lord your God redeemed you thence; therefore I command you to do this thing.
And if he says unto you: I will not go forth from you, because he loves you and your house, and because it is well with him beside you,
then you shall take an awl, and pierce his ear against the door, and he shall be your household slave for ever; and unto your female slave you shall do likewise.
It shall not seem hard unto you when they are sent forth free from you, for he served you six years for the yearly wage of a hired worker; and the Lord your God shall bless you in all that you do.

Deuteronomy 24:1 — And if a man takes a wife and dwells with her as husband, and she finds no favour in his sight, because he has found some unseemly thing in her, and he writes her a certificate of divorce, and gives it into her hands, and sends her forth out of his house,

Deuteronomy 24:17 — You shall not pervert the judgment of the sojourner, or of the orphan, or of the widow; neither shall you take a widow’s garment in pledge.
Deuteronomy 24:18 — And you shall remember that you were a household slave in the land of Egypt, and the Lord your God redeemed you thence; therefore I command you to do this thing.

Deuteronomy 24:22 — And you shall remember that you were a household slave in the land of Egypt; therefore I command you to do this thing.

title: Protecting foreigners, widows and orphans
paragraphs: Study 35: Protecting foreigners, widows and orphans
Related indexed requirements: C0203, C0204. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Connection to Christ: Jesus teaches practical welcome and mercy; James expressly calls for care of widows and orphans.
Christian response today: Protect vulnerable people through concrete help, fair treatment and hospitality.
Saints Translation — Law: Exodus 22:20–23 (KJV 22:21–24) Christ and the apostles: James 1:27 · Matthew 25:35–40
Text and setting: Moral teaching
Torah: Exodus 22:20–23 (KJV 22:21–24)

Israel must not mistreat resident foreigners, widows or fatherless children. The law recalls Israel’s own vulnerability in Egypt and God’s hearing of the oppressed. James calls care for widows and orphans a mark of faithful religion; Jesus identifies welcome and practical mercy as matters of serious spiritual concern.
Read with Christ and the apostles: James 1:27 · Matthew 25:35–40
Connection and evidence: Related New Testament teaching. Jesus teaches practical welcome and mercy; James expressly calls for care of widows and orphans.
These passages support a related teaching or moral application. The connection is not presented as a direct quotation of this exact Torah rule.

Jesus’ account of the merciful Samaritan challenges narrow definitions of neighbor, while Hebrews commends hospitality. Neither ethnic origin nor social vulnerability cancels a person’s claim to humane treatment.

paragraphs: Study 132: Opening the hand to a poor neighbor
Related indexed requirements: C0731, C1037, C1038, C1039, C1040, C1041. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Connection to Christ: First John and Second Corinthians call for practical, willing generosity toward those in need.
Christian response today: Respond to need with concrete help rather than finding religious or financial excuses to close your hand.
Saints Translation — Law: Deuteronomy 15:7–11 Christ and the apostles: 1 John 3:17–18 · 2 Corinthians 9:7
Text and setting: Moral teaching
Torah: Deuteronomy 15:7–11

Israel must not harden the heart or withhold assistance because the debt-release year is approaching. The passage exposes calculations that use the law as a reason to evade generosity. First John likewise asks how God’s love can remain in someone who sees a brother or sister’s need and refuses help.

Connection and evidence: Related New Testament teaching. First John and Second Corinthians call for practical, willing generosity toward those in need.
