Leviticus 25:1 — And the Lord spoke unto Moses on Mount Sinai, saying:
Leviticus 25:2 — Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: When you enter the land which I give unto you, the land which I give unto you shall rest, a Sabbath unto the Lord.
Leviticus 25:3 — For six years you shall sow your field, and for six years you shall prune your vine and gather its fruit.
Leviticus 25:4 — But in the seventh year the land shall have a Sabbath, a rest, a Sabbath unto the Lord. You shall not sow your field or prune your vine.
Leviticus 25:5 — And you shall not reap the things growing of themselves in your field or gather the grapes of your consecration. It shall be a year of rest for the land.
Leviticus 25:6 — And the land’s Sabbath produce shall be food for you, your male slave, your female slave, your hired worker, and the lodger attached to you.
Leviticus 25:7 — And all its produce shall also be food for your livestock and the wild animals in your land.
Leviticus 25:8 — And you shall count unto yourself seven rests of years, seven years seven times; and the seven weeks of years shall be unto you forty-nine years.

Leviticus 25:9 — And you shall make proclamation with a trumpet sound throughout your land in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month. On the Day of Atonement you shall make proclamation with a trumpet throughout your land.

Leviticus 25:10 — And you shall consecrate the fiftieth year, and proclaim release throughout the land unto all who dwell therein; this shall be a year of release, a signal unto you; and each one shall depart unto his possession, and each of you shall depart unto his ancestral homeland.
Leviticus 25:11 — This is a signal of release: the fiftieth year shall be a year for you. You shall not sow, reap what grows of itself, or gather its consecrated produce.
Leviticus 25:12 — For it is a signal of release; it shall be holy to you. You shall eat its produce from the fields.
Leviticus 25:13 — In the year of release, at its signal, each shall return to his possession.
Leviticus 25:14 — But if one sells property unto your neighbour, or you acquire it from your neighbour, let no man oppress his neighbour.
Leviticus 25:15 — According to the number of years after the signal you shall acquire from your neighbour; according to the number of harvest years he shall sell to you.
Leviticus 25:16 — As the years increase, you shall increase its purchase price; as the years decrease, you shall decrease its purchase price, for he is selling you a number of harvests.
Leviticus 25:17 — Let no man oppress his neighbour, and you shall fear the Lord your God; I am the Lord your God.
Leviticus 25:18 — And you shall do all My statutes and all My judgments, keep them, and do them; then you shall dwell confidently on the land.
Leviticus 25:19 — And the land shall yield its produce, and you shall eat to fullness and dwell confidently upon it.
Leviticus 25:20 — But if you say, “What shall we eat in this seventh year, if we neither sow nor gather our produce?”
Leviticus 25:21 — then I will send My blessing to you in the sixth year, and it shall produce its harvest for the three years.
Leviticus 25:22 — And you shall sow in the eighth year and eat old produce. Until the ninth year, until its produce comes in, you shall eat old stores from the old.
Leviticus 25:23 — And the land shall not be sold in perpetuity, for the land is Mine; for you are resident foreigners and lodgers before Me;
Leviticus 25:24 — and throughout all the land of your possession, you shall provide redemption for the land.
Leviticus 25:25 — But if your brother who is with you becomes poor, and sells some of his possession, and his nearest kinsman comes, he shall redeem that which his brother sold.
Leviticus 25:26 — If someone has no kinsman but prospers by his hand and enough is found for his redemption,
Leviticus 25:27 — then he shall calculate the years of his sale and repay the excess to the man to whom he sold himself; then he shall depart to his possession.

Leviticus 25:28 — If his hand does not prosper enough to repay him, the sale shall remain with the one who acquired it until the sixth year of release. It shall go out at the release, and he shall depart to his possession.
Leviticus 25:29 — But if anyone sells a dwelling house in a walled city, its redemption shall be possible until a year of days is fulfilled; that shall be its redemption period.

Leviticus 25:30 — If it is not redeemed before its whole year is complete, the house in the city that has a wall shall be confirmed permanently to its buyer throughout his generations. It shall not go out at the release.
Leviticus 25:31 — But houses in settlements that have no surrounding wall shall be reckoned with the field of the land. They shall always be redeemable and shall go out at the release.
Leviticus 25:32 — And the cities of the Levites—the houses in their cities of possession—shall always be redeemable by the Levites.

Leviticus 25:33 — And whosoever redeems from the Levites, the sale of their houses in the city of their possession shall go out at the release; for the houses in the cities of the Levites are their possession among the sons of Israel.
Leviticus 25:34 — And the fields set apart for their cities shall not be sold, for this is their everlasting possession.
Leviticus 25:35 — If your brother becomes poor and grows weak in his hands beside you, you shall support him as a resident foreigner and a lodger, and your brother shall live with you.
Leviticus 25:36 — You shall take no interest or increase from him, and you shall fear your God; I am the Lord; and your brother shall live with you.
Leviticus 25:37 — You shall not give him your silver at interest or give your food for an increase.
Leviticus 25:38 — I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan and to be your God.
Leviticus 25:39 — If your brother is brought low beside you and is sold to you, he shall not serve you with the service of a household slave.
Leviticus 25:40 — He shall be with you as a hired worker or a lodger; he shall work beside you until the year of release.
Leviticus 25:41 — And he shall go out at the release, and his children with him. He shall depart to his kin and return to his ancestral possession.
Leviticus 25:42 — For these are My household slaves, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt; one shall not be sold with the sale of a household slave.
Leviticus 25:43 — You shall not wear him down with toil, but you shall fear the Lord your God.
Leviticus 25:44 — And your male slave and your female slave, as many as you have from the nations which are round about you: from them you may acquire a male slave and a female slave.
Leviticus 25:45 — And you may also acquire from the sons of the lodgers among you and from their relatives who come to be in your land; they shall become your possession.

Leviticus 25:46 — And you shall distribute them to your children after you, and they shall be held by you permanently. But among your brethren, the sons of Israel, no one shall wear down his brother with toils.

Leviticus 25:47 — If the hand of the resident foreigner or lodger beside you gains means, and your brother becomes needy and is sold to the resident foreigner or lodger beside you, a foreigner by birth,
Leviticus 25:48 — after he is sold to him, he shall have a right of redemption. One of his brethren may redeem him,

Leviticus 25:49 — his father’s brother or the son of his father’s brother may redeem him, or one of his close kin from his tribe may redeem him; but if, having prospered by his hands, he redeems himself,

Leviticus 25:50 — then he shall calculate with the one who acquired him from the year he sold himself to him until the year of release. His sale price shall be like a hired worker’s pay; he shall be with him year by year.
Leviticus 25:51 — If many years remain for someone, he shall repay his redemption from his sale money in proportion to them.
Leviticus 25:52 — If few years remain until the year of release, he shall calculate with him according to his years and repay his redemption.
Leviticus 25:53 — He shall be with him as a hired worker year by year; you shall not wear him down with toil before you.
Leviticus 25:54 — If he is not redeemed by these means, he shall go out in the year of release, he and his children with him.
Leviticus 25:55 — For the sons of Israel are household slaves to Me; these are My servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.

title: Numbers 34:1–29 · Canaan's boundaries; tribal shares; Eleazar, Joshua and the appointed tribal leaders
paragraphs: Passage group: Canaan's boundaries; tribal shares; Eleazar, Joshua and the appointed tribal leaders. Setting: Land allocation instructions.
Requirements appearing in this passage: C0920, C0940, C0941. A mixed passage can link to more than one topic or classification.
Numbers 34:1 — And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Numbers 34:2 — Command the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: You are entering the land of Canaan; this shall be your inheritance, the land of Canaan with its boundaries.
Numbers 34:3 — And your southwestern side shall run from the wilderness of Sin to the territory adjoining Edom. Your southwestern boundary shall begin from the part of the Salt Sea toward the east.

Numbers 34:4 — And the boundary shall turn around you from the southwest toward the Ascent of Akrabin and pass through Senna. Its endpoint shall be southwest of Kadesh-barnea; it shall extend to the settlement of Arad and pass through Azmon.
Numbers 34:5 — And the boundary shall turn from Azmon to the Wadi of Egypt, and its endpoint shall be the sea.
Numbers 34:6 — And for your sea boundary, the Great Sea shall mark the limit. This shall be your sea boundary.
Numbers 34:7 — And this shall be your boundary toward the north: from the Great Sea you shall measure out for yourselves beside the mountain, the mountain;
Numbers 34:8 — and from the mountain, the mountain, you shall measure out for them toward the entrance into Hamath; and its endpoint shall be the boundaries of Sarada.
Numbers 34:9 — And the boundary shall extend to Dephrona, and its endpoint shall be Hazar-enan. This shall be your northern boundary.
Numbers 34:10 — And you shall measure out for yourselves the eastern boundary from Hazar-enan unto Shepham.
Numbers 34:11 — And the boundary shall descend from Shepham to Arbela, from the east toward the springs. The boundary shall descend to Bela, along the eastern ridge of the Sea of Chennara.
Numbers 34:12 — And the boundary shall descend to the Jordan, and its endpoint shall be the Salt Sea. This shall be your land and its surrounding boundaries.

Numbers 34:13 — And Moses commanded the sons of Israel, saying: This is the land that you shall inherit by lot, as the Lord prescribed unto Moses to give to the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
Numbers 34:14 — For the tribe of the sons of Reuben and the tribe of the sons of Gad according to their ancestral houses, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, have received their allotments.
Numbers 34:15 — The two tribes and the half-tribe have received their allotments across the Jordan opposite Jericho, from the south toward the east.
Numbers 34:16 — And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Numbers 34:17 — These are the names of the men who shall obtain the land as an inheritance for you: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun.
Numbers 34:18 — And you shall take one ruler from each tribe to allot the land unto you.
Numbers 34:19 — And these are the names of the men: from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
Numbers 34:20 — from the tribe of Simeon, Salamiel son of Ammihud;
Numbers 34:21 — from the tribe of Benjamin, Eldad son of Chislon;
Numbers 34:22 — from the tribe of Dan, the ruler Bakchir son of Egli;
Numbers 34:23 — from the descendants of Joseph, from the tribe of the sons of Manasseh, the ruler Hanniel son of Ouphi;
Numbers 34:24 — from the tribe of the sons of Ephraim, the ruler Kemuel son of Sabatha;
Numbers 34:25 — from the tribe of Zebulun, the ruler Elizaphan son of Parnach;
Numbers 34:26 — from the tribe of the sons of Issachar, the ruler Paltiel son of Oza;
Numbers 34:27 — from the tribe of the sons of Asher, the ruler Achior son of Shelomi;
Numbers 34:28 — from the tribe of Naphtali, the ruler Pedahel son of Benammihud.
Numbers 34:29 — These are the men whom the Lord commanded to distribute portions to the sons of Israel in the land of Canaan.

Deuteronomy 26:1 — And it shall be, when you enter the land which the Lord your God gives you for a possession, and inherit it, and dwell therein,

Deuteronomy 26:2 — that you shall take of the firstfruits of the produce of your land which the Lord your God gives you, and put it in a basket, and go unto the place which the Lord your God shall choose for His name to be called upon there.

Deuteronomy 26:3 — And you shall come unto the priest who shall be in those days, and say unto him: I declare this day unto the Lord my God, that I have come into the land which the Lord sware unto our fathers to give us.
Deuteronomy 26:4 — And the priest shall take the basket out of your hands, and set it before the altar of the Lord your God.

Deuteronomy 26:5 — And you shall answer and say before the Lord your God: My father forsook Syria, and went down into Egypt, and sojourned there, few in number; and there he became a great nation, and a multitude numerous and great.
Deuteronomy 26:6 — And the Egyptians afflicted us, and humbled us, and laid hard labours upon us.
Deuteronomy 26:7 — And we cried unto the Lord, the God of our fathers; and the Lord heard our voice, and saw our humiliation, and our toil, and our distress.
Deuteronomy 26:8 — And the Lord Himself brought us forth out of Egypt with great strength, and with a mighty hand, and with His uplifted arm, and with great visions, and with signs, and with wonders.
Deuteronomy 26:9 — And He brought us unto this place, and gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.

Deuteronomy 26:10 — And now, behold, I have brought the firstfruits of the produce of the land which Thou hast given me, O Lord, a land flowing with milk and honey. And you shall set them before the Lord your God, and bow down there before the Lord your God.
Deuteronomy 26:11 — And you shall rejoice in all the good things which the Lord your God has given unto you and unto your house, you, and the Levite, and the sojourner among you.

Deuteronomy 26:12 — And when you have finished tithing all the tithe of the produce of your land in the third year, you shall give the second tithe unto the Levite, and unto the sojourner, and unto the orphan, and unto the widow; and they shall eat within your cities and be filled.

Deuteronomy 26:13 — And you shall say before the Lord your God: I have cleared the holy things out of my house, and have given them unto the Levite, and unto the sojourner, and unto the orphan, and unto the widow, according to all Thy commandments which Thou hast commanded me. I have not transgressed Thy commandment, neither have I forgotten it.

Deuteronomy 26:14 — And I have not eaten thereof in my mourning, neither have I offered thereof for an unclean use, nor given thereof unto the dead. I have hearkened unto the voice of the Lord my God; I have done according to all that Thou hast commanded me.

Deuteronomy 26:15 — Look down from Thy holy house, from heaven, and bless Thy people Israel, and the land which Thou hast given them, as Thou didst swear unto our fathers to give us a land flowing with milk and honey.
Deuteronomy 26:16 — This day the Lord your God has commanded you to do all these ordinances and judgments; and you shall keep and do them with all your heart and with all your soul.
Deuteronomy 26:17 — You have chosen God this day to be your God, and to walk in His ways, and to keep His ordinances and His judgments, and to hearken unto His voice.
Deuteronomy 26:18 — And the Lord has chosen you this day to be unto Him a people for His own possession, as He has spoken unto you, to keep all His commandments,
Deuteronomy 26:19 — and to be above all the nations, as He has made you renowned, and a boast, and glorious, that you should be a holy people unto the Lord your God, as He has spoken.

verses.text: And it shall be, when you enter the land which the Lord your God gives you for a possession, and inherit it, and dwell therein,

that you shall take of the firstfruits of the produce of your land which the Lord your God gives you, and put it in a basket, and go unto the place which the Lord your God shall choose for His name to be called upon there.

And you shall come unto the priest who shall be in those days, and say unto him: I declare this day unto the Lord my God, that I have come into the land which the Lord sware unto our fathers to give us.
And the priest shall take the basket out of your hands, and set it before the altar of the Lord your God.

And you shall answer and say before the Lord your God: My father forsook Syria, and went down into Egypt, and sojourned there, few in number; and there he became a great nation, and a multitude numerous and great.
And the Egyptians afflicted us, and humbled us, and laid hard labours upon us.
And we cried unto the Lord, the God of our fathers; and the Lord heard our voice, and saw our humiliation, and our toil, and our distress.
And the Lord Himself brought us forth out of Egypt with great strength, and with a mighty hand, and with His uplifted arm, and with great visions, and with signs, and with wonders.
And He brought us unto this place, and gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.

And now, behold, I have brought the firstfruits of the produce of the land which Thou hast given me, O Lord, a land flowing with milk and honey. And you shall set them before the Lord your God, and bow down there before the Lord your God.
And you shall rejoice in all the good things which the Lord your God has given unto you and unto your house, you, and the Levite, and the sojourner among you.

And when you have finished tithing all the tithe of the produce of your land in the third year, you shall give the second tithe unto the Levite, and unto the sojourner, and unto the orphan, and unto the widow; and they shall eat within your cities and be filled.

And you shall say before the Lord your God: I have cleared the holy things out of my house, and have given them unto the Levite, and unto the sojourner, and unto the orphan, and unto the widow, according to all Thy commandments which Thou hast commanded me. I have not transgressed Thy commandment, neither have I forgotten it.

And I have not eaten thereof in my mourning, neither have I offered thereof for an unclean use, nor given thereof unto the dead. I have hearkened unto the voice of the Lord my God; I have done according to all that Thou hast commanded me.
Look down from Thy holy house, from heaven, and bless Thy people Israel, and the land which Thou hast given them, as Thou didst swear unto our fathers to give us a land flowing with milk and honey.
This day the Lord your God has commanded you to do all these ordinances and judgments; and you shall keep and do them with all your heart and with all your soul.
You have chosen God this day to be your God, and to walk in His ways, and to keep His ordinances and His judgments, and to hearken unto His voice.
And the Lord has chosen you this day to be unto Him a people for His own possession, as He has spoken unto you, to keep all His commandments,
and to be above all the nations, as He has made you renowned, and a boast, and glorious, that you should be a holy people unto the Lord your God, as He has spoken.

title: Passover and remembrance of deliverance
paragraphs: Study 15: Passover and remembrance of deliverance

Related indexed requirements: C0036, C0091, C0092, C0093, C0094, C0095, C0096, C0097, C0098, C0099, C0100, C0101, C0102, C0103, C0111, C0112, C0113, C0114. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Transformed — Passover remembrance in Christ
Connection to Christ: Paul explicitly identifies Christ as our Passover sacrifice; this mark concerns that identification, not the cancellation of every festival custom.
Christian response today: Remember Christ in the Lord’s Supper and live in sincerity and truth, with gratitude for the deliverance the exodus recounts.
Saints Translation — Law: Exodus 12:1–14 · Exodus 12:43–49 Christ and the apostles: Luke 22:14–20 · 1 Corinthians 5:7–8
Ancient covenant practice: Israel keeps Passover in remembrance of deliverance from Egypt, with its prescribed sacrifice and meal.

Development in Christ and the apostles: Paul identifies Christ as the Passover sacrifice. At the Passover meal Jesus gives the bread and cup in relation to his body, blood and the new covenant; Paul transmits remembrance of the Lord and proclamation of his death.
Saints Translation support: Luke 22:14–20 · 1 Corinthians 5:7–8 · 1 Corinthians 11:23–26
Basis and scope: Direct New Testament identification and institution; festival and sacramental applications differ.

Read carefully: The Fulfilled mark concerns the sacrifice; Transformed concerns Christian remembrance and participation. This does not declare every Passover custom forbidden or erase differences in Eucharistic understanding.
What Transformed means · Browse transformed practices

Passover commemorates Israel’s deliverance from Egypt and includes specific household, meal and covenant requirements. Jesus gives the bread and cup their significance in relation to His death; Paul calls Christ our Passover. Christian traditions differ in festival observance. Keep the exodus setting and the New Testament interpretation visible together.

title: The Festival of Unleavened Bread
paragraphs: Study 16: The Festival of Unleavened Bread

Related indexed requirements: C0088, C0103, C0104, C0105, C0106, C0107, C0108, C0109, C0116, C0117. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Transformed — unleavened bread and a life of sincerity
Connection to Christ: Paul uses unleavened bread to teach the removal of malice and wickedness from the Christian community.
Christian response today: Turn away from malice and live truthfully; let any festival observance serve Christ without becoming a test by which you condemn other believers.
Saints Translation — Law: Exodus 12:15–20 · Exodus 13:3–10 Christ and the apostles: 1 Corinthians 5:6–8 · Colossians 2:16–17
Ancient covenant practice: Israel removes leaven and keeps the feast as a memorial of the exodus.

Development in Christ and the apostles: Paul applies leaven to malice and wickedness and unleavened bread to sincerity and truth, grounding his exhortation in Christ our Passover. Colossians warns against judgment over festivals.
Saints Translation support: 1 Corinthians 5:6–8 · Colossians 2:16–17
Basis and scope: Direct apostolic use of the image; the conclusion about a binding calendar is a Christian interpretation.
Read carefully: Paul’s moral use does not erase the original literal feast. Christians differ on whether his language also calls for its continued calendar observance.
What Transformed means · Browse transformed practices

Israel is instructed to remove leaven and observe the festival as a memorial of the exodus. Paul draws a moral application concerning sincerity and truth. Colossians warns against judgment over festivals. The literal Israelite observance and Paul’s application are related but should not be collapsed into one undifferentiated Christian obligation.

title: Sabbath holiness and rest
paragraphs: Study 22: Sabbath holiness and rest
Related indexed requirements: C0116, C0129, C0151, C0152. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Connection to Christ: Jesus teaches the Sabbath’s human benefit and the lawfulness of doing good; this does not settle every later observance question.
Christian response today: Make room for worship, rest and mercy, and study the differing Christian understandings of the day and its obligation.
Saints Translation — Law: Exodus 20:8–11 · Deuteronomy 5:12–15 Christ and the apostles: Mark 2:27–28 · Matthew 12:9–12 · Romans 14:5–6 · Colossians 2:16–17
Text and setting: Covenant observance
Torah: Exodus 20:8–11 · Deuteronomy 5:12–15

The seventh-day Sabbath is commanded to Israel, with rest extending to workers, animals and resident foreigners. Jesus teaches its human benefit and the lawfulness of doing good. Christians differ about seventh-day observance, Sunday and the continuity of this command. Romans and Colossians must be included when discussing that application.
Read with Christ and the apostles: Mark 2:27–28 · Matthew 12:9–12 · Romans 14:5–6 · Colossians 2:16–17
Connection and evidence: Explicit New Testament treatment. Jesus teaches the Sabbath’s human benefit and the lawfulness of doing good; this does not settle every later observance question.

Where interpretations differ: Seventh-day observance, Sunday worship and the continuing form of the Sabbath command. Read the biblical passages together and distinguish a tradition’s conclusion from the wording of the text. Compare interpretive approaches.

title: Israel’s annual pilgrimage festivals
paragraphs: Study 50: Israel’s annual pilgrimage festivals
Related indexed requirements: C0104, C0230, C0231, C0232, C0233, C0234. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Transformed — festival pilgrimage and worship through Christ
Connection to Christ: Paul connects Passover with Christ and warns against judgment over festivals; he does not identify every calendar detail as completed.
Christian response today: Gather for worship, give thanks and encourage others through Christ; do not make travel to an ancient sanctuary a condition of Christian belonging.
Saints Translation — Law: Exodus 23:14–17 Christ and the apostles: Colossians 2:16–17 · 1 Corinthians 5:7–8
Ancient covenant practice: Israel’s three annual pilgrimage festivals belong to its agricultural year and sanctuary worship.

Development in Christ and the apostles: Jesus teaches worship of the Father in spirit and truth beyond the Jerusalem-versus-mountain question. Colossians places festivals in relation to Christ; Hebrews calls believers to draw near and assemble together.
Saints Translation support: John 4:21–24 · Colossians 2:16–17 · Hebrews 10:19–25
Basis and scope: Direct teaching on festivals and worship; its application to the pilgrimage requirement is interpretive.
Read carefully: This does not forbid pilgrimage or commemorating biblical festivals. Christians differ about calendar observance.
What Transformed means · Browse transformed practices

Exodus names Unleavened Bread, Harvest and Ingathering as annual festivals before the Lord. This entry overlaps the more detailed festival studies. Their place in Israel’s agricultural and sanctuary life matters. Christian observance should be discussed alongside the New Testament’s interpretation of Christ and its warning against judging others over festivals.

Saints Translation — Law: Leviticus 16:29–34 · Leviticus 23:26–32 Christ and the apostles: Hebrews 9:6–14 · Hebrews 10:1–14 · Hebrews 9:24–28 · Hebrews 10:19–25
Ancient covenant practice: An appointed high priest enters the sanctuary in the annual atonement rite, with sacrifices and Israel’s solemn observance.

Development in Christ and the apostles: Hebrews presents Christ’s decisive offering and heavenly entrance, then calls believers to approach God through him with faith, hope, love and mutual encouragement.
Saints Translation support: Hebrews 9:24–28 · Hebrews 10:19–25
Basis and scope: Direct New Testament account of the sanctuary rite and access through Christ.

Read carefully: Fulfilled identifies Christ’s offering; Transformed identifies the resulting access and response. This does not settle every question about commemorating the day or Eucharistic theology.
What Transformed means · Browse transformed practices

Israel is instructed to observe a solemn annual day of rest and self-affliction, with atonement performed by the priest. Hebrews interprets the sanctuary rites through Christ’s once-for-all offering. Christian traditions may commemorate the day differently, but no recurring ritual should be presented as completing an insufficiency in Christ’s sacrifice.

title: Firstfruits, the count and the Festival of Weeks
paragraphs: Study 95: Firstfruits, the count and the Festival of Weeks

Related indexed requirements: C0597, C0598, C0601, C0682, C0683, C0684, C0685, C0686, C0687, C0688, C0689, C0690, C1225, C1243. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Connection to Christ: Paul explicitly calls the risen Christ the firstfruits; Acts records the Spirit’s coming at Pentecost. This does not declare every festival detail completed.
Christian response today: Live in resurrection hope and respond to the Spirit; keep firstfruits, the count and Weeks distinct in the Torah calendar.
Saints Translation — Law: Leviticus 23:9–22 Christ and the apostles: Acts 2:1–4 · 1 Corinthians 15:20–23
Text and setting: Israel’s worship
Torah: Leviticus 23:9–22

Leviticus distinguishes the first sheaf, the counting of days and the later Festival of Weeks. Calling them one event erases that sequence. Acts places the Spirit’s coming at Pentecost, and Paul calls the risen Christ the firstfruits. These connections should accompany, rather than replace, the Torah’s actual calendar instructions.
Read with Christ and the apostles: Acts 2:1–4 · 1 Corinthians 15:20–23

Connection and evidence: Explicit New Testament treatment. Paul explicitly calls the risen Christ the firstfruits; Acts records the Spirit’s coming at Pentecost. This does not declare every festival detail completed.

Where interpretations differ: Festival observance; the firstfruits identification itself is explicit in Paul. Read the biblical passages together and distinguish a tradition’s conclusion from the wording of the text. Compare interpretive approaches.

title: The first day of the seventh month
paragraphs: Study 96: The first day of the seventh month
Related indexed requirements: C0691, C0692, C0693, C0694. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Transformed — festival observance in relation to Christ
Connection to Christ: Colossians relates festivals to Christ, but the New Testament does not explicitly identify this date with a completed trumpet event.
Christian response today: Let sacred-day observance lead to worship and gratitude in Christ, with humility toward believers who observe differently.
Saints Translation — Law: Leviticus 23:23–25 · Numbers 29:1 Christ and the apostles: Colossians 2:16–17
Ancient covenant practice: The first day of the seventh month is marked by rest, assembly and trumpet blasts or acclamation.

Development in Christ and the apostles: Colossians warns against judgment over a festival, new moon or Sabbaths and directs attention to Christ. This informs Christian calendar practice without naming a specific event that fulfills this date.
Saints Translation support: Colossians 2:16–17 · Romans 14:5–6
Basis and scope: Christian application of Colossians’ general festival teaching, not an identified fulfillment of this date.
Read carefully: This mark makes no prediction about the date of Christ’s return and does not resolve the separate debate about the weekly Sabbath.
What Transformed means · Browse transformed practices

The Torah calls for a sacred assembly, rest and a memorial of trumpet blasts or acclamation on this date. It does not in these verses name a New Testament event that must occur on the same calendar day. Christian festival practice and prophetic interpretations should be identified as interpretations, not added to the command.

title: Booths and the concluding assembly

Transformed — Booths, living water and Christian observance
Connection to Christ: John places Jesus’ teaching about living water at Booths; that connection is not an explicit declaration that every aspect of the festival is completed.
Christian response today: Come to Christ, receive the Spirit’s life and remember God’s provision; practice any festival commemoration without using it to condemn others.
Saints Translation — Law: Leviticus 23:33–43 Christ and the apostles: John 7:2 · John 7:37–39 · Colossians 2:16–17
Ancient covenant practice: Israel dwells in booths in remembrance of wilderness life and keeps the concluding assembly.

Development in Christ and the apostles: During this feast Jesus invites the thirsty to come to him; John explains the living water in relation to the Spirit. Colossians directs festival judgments toward Christ.
Saints Translation support: John 7:2 · John 7:37–39 · Colossians 2:16–17
Basis and scope: Direct Gospel festival setting and apostolic festival teaching; present observance remains an interpretive question.
Read carefully: John’s connection does not assign a separate completed prophecy to every booth, day or ritual detail. Christians differ in continuing festival practice.
What Transformed means · Browse transformed practices

Israel celebrates seven days, dwells in booths in remembrance of the wilderness, and observes an eighth-day assembly. John places Jesus’ teaching about living water at the festival. Christians differ about observance; keep the historical memorial, the eighth-day distinction and the Gospel connection clear.

title: Rejoicing before God with the household
paragraphs: Study 123: Rejoicing before God with the household
Related indexed requirements: C1012, C1013. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.

Israel is to rejoice at the place God chooses, sharing the celebration with household members, servants and the Levite. title: The month of Abib and Passover remembrance
paragraphs: Study 133: The month of Abib and Passover remembrance
Related indexed requirements: C0091, C0103. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Transformed — Passover remembrance and the Christian calendar
Connection to Christ: Luke records Jesus’ Passover meal; Colossians addresses festival judgments without settling every calendar calculation.
Christian response today: Remember Christ and God’s deliverance with thanksgiving, while treating differences in Christian calendar practice with humility.
Saints Translation — Law: Deuteronomy 16:1 · Exodus 12:1–2 Christ and the apostles: Luke 22:14–20 · Colossians 2:16–17
Ancient covenant practice: Israel observes Abib and Passover in remembrance of departure from Egypt.

Saints Translation support: Luke 22:14–20 · 1 Corinthians 11:23–26 · Colossians 2:16–17
Basis and scope: Direct connection with Jesus’ Passover meal; calendar application is interpretive.

What Transformed means · Browse transformed practices

Moses tells Israel to observe the month of Abib and celebrate Passover in remembrance of departure from Egypt. These verses do not settle every later dispute over calendar calculation. Christian commemoration should be discussed in relation to Jesus’ Passover meal and the New Testament’s treatment of festival judgments.

title: Three annual appearances before the Lord
paragraphs: Study 134: Three annual appearances before the Lord
Related indexed requirements: C0230, C0232, C1049. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Transformed — pilgrimage and gathered worship through Christ
Connection to Christ: John 4 addresses the place of worship, and Hebrews invites believers to draw near through Christ and continue meeting together.
Christian response today: Gather, worship, encourage one another and give generously; Christian access to God does not depend on making the three ancient sanctuary journeys.
Saints Translation — Law: Deuteronomy 16:16–17 Christ and the apostles: John 4:21–24 · Hebrews 10:19–25
Ancient covenant practice: Israelite males appear at the chosen sanctuary for the three festivals with gifts according to the blessing received.
Development in Christ and the apostles: Jesus teaches worship of the Father in spirit and truth; Hebrews calls believers to draw near through Christ and not neglect assembling together.
Saints Translation support: John 4:21–24 · Hebrews 10:19–25 · 2 Corinthians 9:7
Basis and scope: Direct teaching on access to God and worship location, applied to this pilgrimage law.
Read carefully: Voluntary pilgrimage may still serve devotion. The mark concerns a universal requirement to make these journeys, not a ban on travel or festivals.
What Transformed means · Browse transformed practices

Israelite males are instructed to appear at the chosen sanctuary for Unleavened Bread, Weeks and Booths, bringing gifts according to blessing received. This is a sanctuary pilgrimage law. Jesus’ teaching about worship and Hebrews’ invitation to approach God through Christ must be included before describing any Christian obligation to travel to a particular place.

Exodus 12:1 — The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying,
Exodus 12:2 — “This month shall be the beginning of months for you; it shall be the first month of the year for you.
Exodus 12:3 — Speak to the whole congregation of the sons of Israel, saying: On the tenth day of this month, each shall take a sheep for the ancestral households, one sheep for each household.

Exodus 12:4 — If those in the house are too few to be sufficient for a sheep, he shall join with his nearest neighbour. According to the number of persons, each person’s sufficient portion shall be reckoned for the sheep.
Exodus 12:5 — Your sheep shall be without blemish, a male a year old; you shall take it from the lambs and from the young goats.
Exodus 12:6 — And you shall keep it until the fourteenth day of this month; and the whole multitude of the congregation of the sons of Israel shall slaughter it toward evening.
Exodus 12:7 — They shall take some of the blood and put it on the two doorposts and the lintel of the houses in which they eat them.
Exodus 12:8 — They shall eat the meat that night, roasted over fire, and eat unleavened bread with bitter herbs.
Exodus 12:9 — You shall eat none of it raw, nor boiled in water, but roasted with fire, its head together with its feet and inward parts.
Exodus 12:10 — You shall leave none of it until morning, and you shall not break a bone of it. Whatever remains until morning you shall burn with fire.
Exodus 12:11 — And this is how you shall eat it: your loins girded, your sandals upon your feet, and your staffs in your hands; and you shall eat it in haste. It is a Passover to the Lord.

Exodus 12:12 — I will go through the land of Egypt that night and strike every firstborn in the land of Egypt, both human and animal. Against all the Egyptians’ gods I will execute vengeance. I am the Lord.

Exodus 12:13 — And the blood shall be a sign to you upon the houses in which you are; and I will see the blood, and shelter you; and no plague of destruction shall be among you when I strike the land of Egypt.
Exodus 12:14 — This day shall be a memorial for you. You shall celebrate it as a feast to the Lord throughout all your generations; you shall celebrate it as a perpetual statute.

Exodus 12:17 — You shall keep this commandment, for on this day I will bring your host out of the land of Egypt. You shall observe this day throughout your generations as a perpetual statute.
Exodus 12:18 — Beginning on the fourteenth day of the first month, from evening until the evening of the twenty-first day of the month, you shall eat unleavened bread.

Exodus 12:19 — For seven days no leaven shall be found in your houses; whoever eats anything leavened, that soul shall be destroyed from the congregation of Israel, whether a resident foreigner or a native of the land.
Exodus 12:20 — You shall eat nothing leavened. In all your dwellings you shall eat unleavened bread.”
Exodus 12:21 — Moses called the whole council of elders of the sons of Israel and said to them, “Go and take a sheep for your families, and slaughter the Passover.

Exodus 12:22 — Take a bunch of hyssop, dip it in the blood beside the door, and touch the lintel and both doorposts with the blood beside the door. None of you shall go out of the door of his house until morning.

Exodus 12:23 — The Lord will pass through to strike the Egyptians. He will see the blood on the lintel and both doorposts, and the Lord will pass by the doorway. He will not allow the destroyer to enter your houses to strike.
Exodus 12:24 — And you shall keep this word as a statute for yourself and for your sons for ever.
Exodus 12:25 — And when you enter into the land which the Lord shall give to you, as He has spoken, you shall keep this service.
Exodus 12:26 — When your sons say to you, ‘What is this service?’

Exodus 12:27 — you shall say to them, ‘This Passover is a sacrifice to the Lord, because He sheltered the houses of the sons of Israel in Egypt when He struck the Egyptians and delivered our houses.’” The people bowed down and worshipped.

you shall say to them, ‘This Passover is a sacrifice to the Lord, because He sheltered the houses of the sons of Israel in Egypt when He struck the Egyptians and delivered our houses.’” The people bowed down and worshipped.

title: Exodus 35:1–35 · Sabbath and fire; willing gifts, skilled workers and the specified sanctuary work

Exodus 35:2 — For six days you shall do work, but on the seventh day there shall be rest, a holy Sabbath, a rest to the Lord. Everyone who does work on it shall die.

title: Leviticus 23:1–44 · Sabbath, Passover, Unleavened Bread, first sheaf, Weeks, gleaning, trumpets, Atonement and Booths

Leviticus 23:1 — And the Lord said unto Moses, saying:
Leviticus 23:2 — Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: The feasts of the Lord, which you shall proclaim as holy convocations, these are My feasts.

Leviticus 23:4 — These are the feasts for the Lord, holy convocations, which you shall proclaim at their proper times.

Leviticus 23:6 — And on the fifteenth day of this month is the Feast of Unleavened Bread unto the Lord. You shall eat unleavened bread for seven days.
Leviticus 23:7 — And on the first day you shall have a holy convocation. You shall do no laborious work.
Leviticus 23:8 — And you shall bring whole burnt offerings unto the Lord for seven days. The seventh day shall be a holy convocation for you; you shall do no laborious work.
Leviticus 23:9 — And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:

Leviticus 23:10 — Say unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: When you enter the land which I give unto you, and reap its harvest, you shall bring a sheaf as the first portion of your harvest unto the priest;
Leviticus 23:11 — and he shall offer up the sheaf before the Lord, acceptable for you; the priest shall offer it up on the morrow after the first day.
Leviticus 23:12 — And on the day you bring the sheaf, you shall offer an unblemished year-old sheep as a whole burnt offering unto the Lord.

Leviticus 23:13 — And its sacrifice shall be two tenths of fine flour kneaded with oil, a sacrifice unto the Lord, a sweet savour unto the Lord. Its drink offering shall be a quarter of a hin of wine.

Leviticus 23:14 — And you shall eat neither bread nor roasted fresh grain until that very day, until you bring the gifts to your God. This is an everlasting ordinance throughout your generations in every dwelling of yours.
Leviticus 23:15 — And you shall count from the day after the Sabbath, from the day you bring the sheaf of the presentation, seven complete weeks.
Leviticus 23:16 — Until the day after the last week you shall count fifty days, and then present a new sacrifice unto the Lord.
Leviticus 23:17 — From your dwelling you shall bring bread as a presentation, two loaves. They shall be made from two tenths of fine flour and baked leavened, as firstfruits unto the Lord.

Leviticus 23:18 — And with the loaves you shall bring seven unblemished year-old lambs, one calf from the herd, and two unblemished rams. They shall be a whole burnt offering unto the Lord, with their sacrifices and drink offerings, a sacrifice, a sweet savour unto the Lord.
Leviticus 23:19 — And they shall offer one male young goat from the goats for sin and two year-old lambs as a sacrifice of deliverance with the firstfruits loaves.

Leviticus 23:20 — And the priest shall present them with the firstfruits loaves as a presentation before the Lord, with the two lambs. They shall be holy unto the Lord; they shall belong unto the priest who presents them.

Leviticus 23:21 — And you shall proclaim this day a convocation; it shall be holy for you. You shall do no laborious work on it. This is an everlasting ordinance throughout your generations in every dwelling of yours.

Leviticus 23:22 — And when you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not finish the remainder of the harvest of your field when you reap; neither shall you gather what falls from your harvest; you shall leave them for the poor and for the resident foreigner; I am the Lord your God.
Leviticus 23:23 — And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Leviticus 23:24 — Speak to the sons of Israel, saying: In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, you shall have a rest, a memorial of trumpets; it shall be a holy convocation for you.
Leviticus 23:25 — You shall do no laborious work, and you shall bring a whole burnt offering unto the Lord.
Leviticus 23:26 — And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:

Leviticus 23:27 — And on the tenth day of this seventh month is the Day of Atonement; it shall be a holy convocation unto you, and you shall humble your souls and bring a whole burnt offering unto the Lord.
Leviticus 23:28 — You shall do no work on that very day, for this is a Day of Atonement for you, to make atonement for you before the Lord your God.
Leviticus 23:29 — Every soul that shall not be humbled on that very day shall be destroyed from among his people.
Leviticus 23:30 — And every soul that does work on that very day, that soul shall perish from among his people.
Leviticus 23:31 — You shall do no work. This is an everlasting ordinance throughout your generations in all your dwellings.
Leviticus 23:32 — It shall be a Sabbath of Sabbaths unto you, and you shall humble your souls; from the ninth day of the month, from evening unto evening, you shall keep your Sabbath.
Leviticus 23:33 — And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Leviticus 23:34 — Speak to the sons of Israel, saying: On the fifteenth day of this seventh month is the Feast of Tents unto the Lord for seven days.
Leviticus 23:35 — And on the first day there shall be a holy convocation. You shall do no laborious work.

Leviticus 23:36 — For seven days you shall bring whole burnt offerings unto the Lord. The eighth day shall be a holy convocation for you, and you shall bring whole burnt offerings unto the Lord. It is a closing observance; you shall do no laborious work.

Leviticus 23:37 — These are the feasts for the Lord, which you shall proclaim as holy convocations, to present offerings unto the Lord: whole burnt offerings and their sacrifices and their drink offerings, each day’s requirement on its day,
Leviticus 23:38 — besides the Lord’s Sabbaths, besides your gifts, besides all your vows, and besides your freewill offerings that you give unto the Lord.

You shall do no laborious work, and you shall bring a whole burnt offering unto the Lord.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
And on the tenth day of this seventh month is the Day of Atonement; it shall be a holy convocation unto you, and you shall humble your souls and bring a whole burnt offering unto the Lord.
You shall do no work on that very day, for this is a Day of Atonement for you, to make atonement for you before the Lord your God.
Every soul that shall not be humbled on that very day shall be destroyed from among his people.
And every soul that does work on that very day, that soul shall perish from among his people.
You shall do no work. This is an everlasting ordinance throughout your generations in all your dwellings.
It shall be a Sabbath of Sabbaths unto you, and you shall humble your souls; from the ninth day of the month, from evening unto evening, you shall keep your Sabbath.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Speak to the sons of Israel, saying: On the fifteenth day of this seventh month is the Feast of Tents unto the Lord for seven days.
And on the first day there shall be a holy convocation. You shall do no laborious work.

For seven days you shall bring whole burnt offerings unto the Lord. The eighth day shall be a holy convocation for you, and you shall bring whole burnt offerings unto the Lord. It is a closing observance; you shall do no laborious work.

These are the feasts for the Lord, which you shall proclaim as holy convocations, to present offerings unto the Lord: whole burnt offerings and their sacrifices and their drink offerings, each day’s requirement on its day,
besides the Lord’s Sabbaths, besides your gifts, besides all your vows, and besides your freewill offerings that you give unto the Lord.

And on the fifteenth day of this seventh month, when you finish gathering the produce of the land, you shall celebrate unto the Lord for seven days. On the first day there shall be rest, and on the eighth day there shall be rest.

And on the first day you shall take beautiful fruit of a tree, and palm fronds, and dense branches of a tree, and willows, and branches of the chaste tree from a stream, to rejoice before the Lord your God seven days
of the year. This is an everlasting ordinance throughout your generations; you shall celebrate it in the seventh month.
You shall dwell in tents seven days; every native in Israel shall dwell in tents,
so that your generations may see that I made the sons of Israel dwell in tents when I brought them out of the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.
And Moses declared the Lord’s feasts to the sons of Israel.

And on the eighth day you shall hold a closing festival. You shall do no laborious work on it.
And you shall present whole burnt offerings as a sweet savour, offerings unto the Lord: one calf, one ram, and seven unblemished year-old lambs.
Their sacrifices and their drink offerings for the calf, the ram, and the lambs shall be according to their number, as prescribed.
And also offer one male goat for sin, besides the continual whole burning, their sacrifices, and their drink offerings.

You shall offer these unto the Lord at your festivals, apart from your vows, your freewill offerings, your whole burnt offerings, your sacrifices, your drink offerings, and your sacrifices of deliverance.

Deuteronomy 16:1 — Keep the month of new produce, and observe the Passover unto the Lord your God; for in the month of new produce you came forth out of Egypt by night.

Deuteronomy 16:4 — No leaven shall be seen with you in all your borders seven days; neither shall any of the flesh which you sacrifice in the evening of the first day remain overnight until the morning.

Deuteronomy 16:6 — but in the place which the Lord your God shall choose for His name to be called upon there, you shall sacrifice the Passover in the evening, at the setting of the sun, at the time when you came forth out of Egypt.

Deuteronomy 16:11 — And you shall rejoice before the Lord your God, you, and your son, and your daughter, and your male slave, and your female slave, and the Levite within your cities, and the sojourner, and the orphan, and the widow among you, in the place which the Lord your God shall choose for His name to be called upon there.
Deuteronomy 16:12 — And you shall remember that you were a household slave in the land of Egypt; and you shall keep and do these commandments.
Deuteronomy 16:13 — You shall keep the Feast of Tents seven days, when you have gathered in from your threshing floor and from your winepress.

Deuteronomy 16:14 — And you shall rejoice in your feast, you, and your son, and your daughter, and your male slave, and your female slave, and the Levite, and the sojourner, and the orphan, and the widow within your cities.

Deuteronomy 16:15 — You shall keep a feast for seven days unto the Lord your God, in the place which the Lord your God shall choose for Himself; and if the Lord your God blesses you in all your produce and in all the work of your hands, you shall rejoice.

Related indexed requirements: C0036. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Transformed — covenant belonging and circumcision
Connection to Christ: Acts and Galatians explicitly reject requiring circumcision for Gentile salvation.

Christian response today: Belong to Christ in faith, receive his call to baptism and live in love; do not require physical circumcision for salvation or condemn someone for their existing circumcised or uncircumcised status.
Saints Translation — Law: Genesis 17:10–14 Christ and the apostles: Acts 15:1–11 · Galatians 5:2–6 · 1 Corinthians 7:18–19
Ancient covenant practice: Circumcision marks Abraham’s male descendants and household within the covenant.

Development in Christ and the apostles: Acts rejects circumcision as a requirement for Gentile salvation. Paul describes circumcision of the heart, a circumcision not made by hands, and burial and resurrection with Christ in baptism. Faith working through love is decisive.
Saints Translation support: Acts 15:1–11 · Romans 2:28–29 · Colossians 2:11–12 · Galatians 5:6 · 1 Corinthians 7:18–19
Basis and scope: Direct New Testament treatment; the connection with baptism is explicit, while sacramental applications differ.

Read carefully: This does not make Jews or Jewish covenant practice inferior. Colossians connects circumcision and baptism without settling every Christian disagreement about baptism or covenant membership.
What Transformed means · Browse transformed practices

Circumcision on the eighth day is the covenant sign commanded for Abraham’s male descendants and household. The New Testament explicitly addresses its application to Gentiles: it must not be required for salvation or treated as the basis of righteousness. The historical command remains Scripture without becoming a compulsory Christian initiation rite.

title: Responsibility for rash oaths
paragraphs: Study 59: Responsibility for rash oaths
Related indexed requirements: C0410, C0411. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Connection to Christ: Hebrews’ account of Christ’s once-for-all offering is applied here to the sacrificial element; the responsibility for truthful speech remains.
Christian response today: Confess wrongdoing and speak dependably; do not carry out a harmful promise merely because you made it.
Saints Translation — Law: Leviticus 5:4–6 Christ and the apostles: Matthew 5:33–37 · James 5:12 · Hebrews 10:1–18
Text and setting: Oath and offering law
Torah: Leviticus 5:4–6

Leviticus addresses a rashly spoken oath, recognition of guilt, confession and the prescribed offering. It does not teach that a harmful promise must be carried out merely because it was spoken. Jesus and James call for dependable, truthful speech; repentance must not become an excuse to fulfill an evil intention.
Read with Christ and the apostles: Matthew 5:33–37 · James 5:12

Connection and evidence: Christian interpretation of the cited passages. Hebrews’ account of Christ’s once-for-all offering is applied here to the sacrificial element; the responsibility for truthful speech remains.
This is an editorial Christian application of the cited passages. The New Testament does not separately state that every detail of this particular rule has been fulfilled or universally reimposed.
Additional biblical support: Hebrews 10:1–18

title: The voluntary Nazirite vow
paragraphs: Study 103: The voluntary Nazirite vow

Related indexed requirements: C0811, C0812, C0813, C0814, C0815, C0816, C0817, C0818, C0819, C0820, C0821, C0822, C0823, C0824, C0825, C0826. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Connection to Christ: Acts records Jewish vow practice; the Nazirite institution is voluntary, and the New Testament does not require it of all Christians.
Christian response today: Speak responsibly and distinguish a voluntary discipline from a universal condition of faithfulness.
Saints Translation — Law: Numbers 6:1–21 Christ and the apostles: Acts 21:23–26 · Matthew 5:33–37
Text and setting: Voluntary vow
Torah: Numbers 6:1–21

The passage governs a special vow undertaken by a man or woman, with restrictions concerning vine products, hair and contact with the dead, followed by offerings. It does not command every believer to become a Nazirite. Acts records Jewish vow practice; Jesus’ teaching on truthful speech remains necessary when considering vows.
Read with Christ and the apostles: Acts 21:23–26 · Matthew 5:33–37
Connection and evidence: Explicit New Testament treatment. Acts records Jewish vow practice; the Nazirite institution is voluntary, and the New Testament does not require it of all Christians.

Where interpretations differ: Vows and their relationship to Jesus’ teaching about swearing. Read the biblical passages together and distinguish a tradition’s conclusion from the wording of the text. Compare interpretive approaches.

title: Vows, responsibility and household rules
paragraphs: Study 107: Vows, responsibility and household rules
Related indexed requirements: C0826, C0930, C0931, C0932, C0933. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Connection to Christ: Jesus and James address oath-taking and dependable speech; their teaching must accompany the ancient household rules.
Christian response today: Be truthful and responsible without treating the ancient annulment procedures as blanket control over another adult’s decisions.
Saints Translation — Law: Numbers 30:2–17 (KJV 30:1–16) Christ and the apostles: Matthew 5:33–37 · James 5:12
Text and setting: Vow law
Torah: Numbers 30:2–17 (KJV 30:1–16)

Numbers treats vows as serious commitments and describes circumstances of household confirmation or annulment in ancient Israel. Those provisions should not be silently transferred into a claim that every modern woman’s decisions require male permission. Christian application must include Jesus’ and James’ insistence on truthful, dependable speech.
Read with Christ and the apostles: Matthew 5:33–37 · James 5:12
Connection and evidence: Explicit New Testament treatment. Jesus and James address oath-taking and dependable speech; their teaching must accompany the ancient household rules.

Where interpretations differ: Solemn vows and oaths in relation to Jesus’ teaching. Read the biblical passages together and distinguish a tradition’s conclusion from the wording of the text. Compare interpretive approaches.

title: Oaths by God’s name and Jesus’ instruction
paragraphs: Study 120: Oaths by God’s name and Jesus’ instruction
Related indexed requirements: C0243, C0610, C0993, C0994. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Connection to Christ: Jesus and James directly address swearing and insist on trustworthy speech; Christians differ about solemn lawful oaths.
Christian response today: Make ordinary speech dependable and study the relevant texts before declaring all formal oaths either required or forbidden.
Saints Translation — Law: Deuteronomy 6:13 · Deuteronomy 10:20 Christ and the apostles: Matthew 5:33–37 · James 5:12
Text and setting: Covenant instruction
Torah: Deuteronomy 6:13 · Deuteronomy 10:20

Deuteronomy directs Israel’s oath-taking toward the Lord rather than rival gods. Jesus and James then warn against swearing and demand trustworthy speech. Christian traditions differ about solemn lawful oaths, but a study cannot simply command frequent swearing by God’s name while omitting these direct New Testament passages.
Read with Christ and the apostles: Matthew 5:33–37 · James 5:12
Connection and evidence: Explicit New Testament treatment. Jesus and James directly address swearing and insist on trustworthy speech; Christians differ about solemn lawful oaths.

Where interpretations differ: Whether Jesus’ instruction excludes every solemn lawful oath. Read the biblical passages together and distinguish a tradition’s conclusion from the wording of the text. Compare interpretive approaches.

title: Leviticus 27:1–34 · Valuations by age and means; animals, houses, land and Jubilee; firstborn, devoted things, tithes and redemption
paragraphs: Passage group: Valuations by age and means; animals, houses, land and Jubilee; firstborn, devoted things, tithes and redemption. Setting: Vows, dedications and tithes.

Requirements appearing in this passage: C0720, C0740, C0741, C0742, C0743, C0744, C0745, C0746, C0747, C0748, C0749, C0750, C0751, C0752, C0753, C0754, C0755, C0756, C0757, C0758, C0759, C0760, C0761, C0762, C0763. A mixed passage can link to more than one topic or classification.
Leviticus 27:1 — And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Leviticus 27:2 — Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: Whosoever vows a vow for the valuation of his soul unto the Lord,
Leviticus 27:3 — the valuation of a male from twenty to sixty years old shall be fifty didrachmas of silver, by the sacred weight.
Leviticus 27:4 — For a female the assessed value shall be thirty didrachmas.
Leviticus 27:5 — From five to twenty years old, the valuation shall be twenty didrachmas for a male and ten didrachmas for a female.
Leviticus 27:6 — From one month to five years old, the valuation shall be five didrachmas of silver for a male and three didrachmas for a female.
Leviticus 27:7 — From sixty years old and upward, the valuation shall be fifteen didrachmas of silver for a male and ten didrachmas for a female.

Leviticus 27:8 — But if he is too poor for the valuation, he shall stand before the priest, and the priest shall value him; the priest shall value him according to the strength of the hand of the one who vowed.
Leviticus 27:9 — If it concerns livestock of a kind presented as a gift unto the Lord, whatever one gives from these unto the Lord shall be holy.
Leviticus 27:10 — He shall not exchange it, good for bad or bad for good. If he does exchange it, animal for animal, both it and its substitute shall be holy.
Leviticus 27:11 — If it concerns any unclean livestock of a kind not presented as a gift unto the Lord, he shall set the animal before the priest.
Leviticus 27:12 — And the priest shall value it, between good and bad. As the priest values it, so it shall stand.
Leviticus 27:13 — If he does redeem it, he shall add a fifth to its valuation.
Leviticus 27:14 — And if a man consecrates his house as holy unto the Lord, the priest shall value it, between good and bad. As the priest values it, so it shall stand.
Leviticus 27:15 — If the one who consecrated it redeems his house, he shall add a fifth of the silver of the valuation to it, and it shall be his.
Leviticus 27:16 — If a man consecrates unto the Lord part of the field of his possession, the valuation shall be according to its seed: fifty didrachmas of silver for a kor of barley.
Leviticus 27:17 — If he consecrates his field from the year of release, it shall stand according to its valuation.

Leviticus 27:18 — If he consecrates his field later, after the release, the priest shall calculate the silver for him according to the years remaining until the year of release, and a deduction shall be made from its assessment.
Leviticus 27:19 — If the one who consecrated the field redeems it, he shall add a fifth of the silver to its valuation, and it shall be his.
Leviticus 27:20 — If he does not redeem the field and sells the field to another man, he shall no longer redeem it.
Leviticus 27:21 — When the release has passed, the field shall be holy unto the Lord like land set apart. It shall become the priest’s possession.
Leviticus 27:22 — If he consecrates unto the Lord part of a field he acquired, which is not part of the field of his inherited possession,
Leviticus 27:23 — the priest shall calculate for him the total valuation from the year of release, and he shall repay the valuation on that day as holy unto the Lord.
Leviticus 27:24 — And in the year of release the field shall be returned to the man from whom he acquired it, whose possession the land was.
Leviticus 27:25 — And every valuation shall be by sacred weights; the didrachma shall be twenty obols.
Leviticus 27:26 — And every firstborn which is born among your livestock shall belong unto the Lord, and none shall consecrate it; whether calf or sheep, it is the Lord’s.

Leviticus 27:27 — If it is one of the unclean four-footed animals, he shall exchange it according to its valuation and add a fifth to it, and it shall be his. If he does not redeem it, it shall be sold according to its assessed value.

Leviticus 27:28 — But every devoted thing which a man dedicates unto the Lord, of all that he has, from man unto livestock, and from the field of his possession, he shall neither sell nor redeem; every devoted thing shall be most holy unto the Lord.
Leviticus 27:29 — And whatsoever is devoted from among men shall not be redeemed, but shall surely be put to death.
Leviticus 27:30 — Every tithe of the land, from the seed of the land and the fruit of trees, belongs unto the Lord; it is holy unto the Lord.
Leviticus 27:31 — But if a man indeed redeems his tithe, he shall add a fifth part unto it, and it shall be his.
Leviticus 27:32 — And every tithe of cattle and sheep, and everything that comes under the staff in the count—the tenth shall be holy unto the Lord.
Leviticus 27:33 — You shall not exchange a good one for a bad one; but if you do indeed exchange it, its substitute also shall be holy; it shall not be redeemed.
Leviticus 27:34 — These are the commandments that the Lord commanded Moses for the sons of Israel on Mount Sinai.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: Whosoever vows a vow for the valuation of his soul unto the Lord,
the valuation of a male from twenty to sixty years old shall be fifty didrachmas of silver, by the sacred weight.
For a female the assessed value shall be thirty didrachmas.
From five to twenty years old, the valuation shall be twenty didrachmas for a male and ten didrachmas for a female.
From one month to five years old, the valuation shall be five didrachmas of silver for a male and three didrachmas for a female.
From sixty years old and upward, the valuation shall be fifteen didrachmas of silver for a male and ten didrachmas for a female.
But if he is too poor for the valuation, he shall stand before the priest, and the priest shall value him; the priest shall value him according to the strength of the hand of the one who vowed.
If it concerns livestock of a kind presented as a gift unto the Lord, whatever one gives from these unto the Lord shall be holy.
He shall not exchange it, good for bad or bad for good. If he does exchange it, animal for animal, both it and its substitute shall be holy.
If it concerns any unclean livestock of a kind not presented as a gift unto the Lord, he shall set the animal before the priest.
And the priest shall value it, between good and bad. As the priest values it, so it shall stand.
If he does redeem it, he shall add a fifth to its valuation.
And if a man consecrates his house as holy unto the Lord, the priest shall value it, between good and bad. As the priest values it, so it shall stand.
If the one who consecrated it redeems his house, he shall add a fifth of the silver of the valuation to it, and it shall be his.
If a man consecrates unto the Lord part of the field of his possession, the valuation shall be according to its seed: fifty didrachmas of silver for a kor of barley.
If he consecrates his field from the year of release, it shall stand according to its valuation.

If he consecrates his field later, after the release, the priest shall calculate the silver for him according to the years remaining until the year of release, and a deduction shall be made from its assessment.
If the one who consecrated the field redeems it, he shall add a fifth of the silver to its valuation, and it shall be his.
If he does not redeem the field and sells the field to another man, he shall no longer redeem it.
When the release has passed, the field shall be holy unto the Lord like land set apart. It shall become the priest’s possession.
If he consecrates unto the Lord part of a field he acquired, which is not part of the field of his inherited possession,
the priest shall calculate for him the total valuation from the year of release, and he shall repay the valuation on that day as holy unto the Lord.
And in the year of release the field shall be returned to the man from whom he acquired it, whose possession the land was.
And every valuation shall be by sacred weights; the didrachma shall be twenty obols.
And every firstborn which is born among your livestock shall belong unto the Lord, and none shall consecrate it; whether calf or sheep, it is the Lord’s.

If it is one of the unclean four-footed animals, he shall exchange it according to its valuation and add a fifth to it, and it shall be his. If he does not redeem it, it shall be sold according to its assessed value.

But every devoted thing which a man dedicates unto the Lord, of all that he has, from man unto livestock, and from the field of his possession, he shall neither sell nor redeem; every devoted thing shall be most holy unto the Lord.
And whatsoever is devoted from among men shall not be redeemed, but shall surely be put to death.
Every tithe of the land, from the seed of the land and the fruit of trees, belongs unto the Lord; it is holy unto the Lord.
But if a man indeed redeems his tithe, he shall add a fifth part unto it, and it shall be his.
And every tithe of cattle and sheep, and everything that comes under the staff in the count—the tenth shall be holy unto the Lord.
You shall not exchange a good one for a bad one; but if you do indeed exchange it, its substitute also shall be holy; it shall not be redeemed.
These are the commandments that the Lord commanded Moses for the sons of Israel on Mount Sinai.

title: Numbers 6:1–26 · Nazirite restrictions, defilement, completion and offerings; the commanded priestly blessing
paragraphs: Passage group: Nazirite restrictions, defilement, completion and offerings; the commanded priestly blessing. Setting: Vow and priestly law.

Numbers 6:1 — And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Numbers 6:2 — Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: If a man or woman solemnly vows a vow of consecration unto the Lord, to be set apart

Numbers 6:3 — from wine and strong drink, he shall be purified from wine. He shall drink neither vinegar of wine, nor vinegar of strong drink, nor anything prepared from grapes; and he shall eat neither fresh grapes nor raisins.
Numbers 6:4 — All the days of his vow he shall consume nothing made from the vine: wine, from pressed grape skins unto the seed.

Numbers 6:5 — All the days of the vow of purification no razor shall come upon his head. Until the days which he vowed unto the Lord are fulfilled, he shall be holy, letting the hair of his head grow long.
Numbers 6:6 — All the days of his vow unto the Lord he shall not enter where any dead person is.
Numbers 6:7 — For his father, or his mother, or his brother, or his sister, he shall not defile himself when they die; for the vow of his God is upon him, upon his head.
Numbers 6:8 — All the days of his vow he shall be holy unto the Lord.
Numbers 6:9 — But if anyone dies suddenly beside him, the head of his vow shall be defiled forthwith. He shall shave his head on the day when he is cleansed; on the seventh day it shall be shaved.
Numbers 6:10 — And on the eighth day he shall bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons unto the priest, at the doors of the Tent of Testimony.

Numbers 6:11 — And the priest shall prepare one for sin and one for a whole burnt offering. And the priest shall make atonement for him concerning his sin in connection with the dead person, and shall consecrate his head on that day,

Numbers 6:14 — and he shall bring his gift unto the Lord: one unblemished year-old male lamb for whole burning, and one unblemished year-old ewe lamb for sin, and one unblemished ram for deliverance,
Numbers 6:15 — and a basket of unleavened bread of fine flour, loaves prepared with oil, and unleavened wafers spread with oil, and their sacrifice and their drink offering.
Numbers 6:16 — And the priest shall present them before the Lord, and prepare his offering for sin and his whole burnt offering.
Numbers 6:17 — And he shall prepare the ram as a sacrifice of deliverance unto the Lord, with the basket of unleavened bread; and the priest shall prepare its sacrifice and its drink offering.
Numbers 6:18 — And he who has vowed shall shave the head of his vow at the doors of the Tent of Testimony, and put the hair upon the fire which is under the sacrifice of deliverance.

Numbers 6:19 — And the priest shall take the boiled foreleg from the ram, and one unleavened loaf from the basket, and one unleavened wafer, and put them upon the hands of him who has vowed, after he has shaved the hair of his vow.

Numbers 6:20 — And the priest shall bring them as a presentation before the Lord. It shall be holy unto the priest, with the breast of presentation and the foreleg of the portion set apart; and afterward he who has vowed shall drink wine.

Numbers 6:21 — This is the law of him who vows unto the Lord, his gift unto the Lord concerning the vow, apart from whatever his hand may find, according to the extent of his vow which he vows under the law of consecration.
Numbers 6:22 — And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:

Numbers 6:23 — Speak unto Aaron and unto his sons, saying: Thus you shall bless the sons of Israel, saying unto them (and they shall put My name upon the sons of Israel, and I, the Lord, will bless them):
Numbers 6:24 — The Lord bless you and keep you;
Numbers 6:25 — the Lord make His face shine upon you, and have mercy upon you;
Numbers 6:26 — the Lord lift up His face upon you, and give you peace.

title: Numbers 30:1–17 · Fulfil spoken vows; responsibilities of daughters, fathers, husbands, widows and divorced women
paragraphs: Passage group: Fulfil spoken vows; responsibilities of daughters, fathers, husbands, widows and divorced women. Setting: Vow law.
Requirements appearing in this passage: C0826, C0930, C0931, C0932, C0933. A mixed passage can link to more than one topic or classification.
Numbers 30:1 — And Moses told the sons of Israel everything that the Lord had commanded Moses.
Numbers 30:2 — And Moses spoke to the rulers of the tribes of Israel, saying: This is the word that the Lord has commanded:
Numbers 30:3 — Any person who vows a vow unto the Lord, or swears an oath, or imposes a restriction upon himself, shall not profane his word. He shall do everything that comes from his mouth.
Numbers 30:4 — If a woman vows a vow unto the Lord or imposes a restriction while in her father’s house in her youth,

Numbers 30:5 — and her father hears her vows and her restrictions that she imposed upon herself, but her father remains silent toward her, then all her vows shall stand, and all her restrictions that she imposed upon herself shall remain.

Numbers 30:6 — But if her father refuses her on the day he hears, none of her vows or restrictions that she imposed upon herself shall stand. The Lord will cleanse her, because her father refused her.
Numbers 30:7 — If she becomes a man’s wife while her vows are upon her, according to the specific statement of her lips by which she imposed a restriction upon herself,
Numbers 30:8 — and her husband hears, and remains silent toward her on the day he hears, then all her vows shall stand, and her restrictions that she imposed upon herself shall remain.

Numbers 30:9 — But if her husband refuses her on the day he hears, none of her vows or restrictions that she imposed upon herself shall remain, because her husband refused her. The Lord will cleanse her.
Numbers 30:10 — And the vow of a widow or a divorced woman—whatever she vowed concerning herself—shall remain against her.
Numbers 30:11 — If her vow was made in her husband’s house, or her restriction was imposed upon herself with an oath,

Numbers 30:12 — and her husband hears, and remains silent toward her, and does not refuse her, then all her vows shall stand, and all her restrictions which she imposed upon her soul shall stand against her.

Numbers 30:13 — But if her husband utterly annuls them on the day he hears, then whatever came from her lips concerning her vows and the restrictions upon herself shall not remain against her. Her husband has annulled them, and the Lord will cleanse her.
Numbers 30:14 — Every vow and every oath imposing a restriction to afflict her soul—her husband may establish it, or her husband may annul it.

Numbers 30:15 — But if he remains utterly silent toward her from day to day, he shall establish all her vows, and he shall establish the restrictions upon her, because he kept silence toward her on the day when he heard.
Numbers 30:16 — But if he annuls them after the day on which he heard, he shall bear his sin.
Numbers 30:17 — These are the ordinances that the Lord commanded Moses between a man and his wife, and between a father and his daughter in her youth in her father’s house.
