If she becomes a man’s wife while her vows are upon her, according to the specific statement of her lips by which she imposed a restriction upon herself,
and her husband hears, and remains silent toward her on the day he hears, then all her vows shall stand, and her restrictions that she imposed upon herself shall remain.
But if her husband refuses her on the day he hears, none of her vows or restrictions that she imposed upon herself shall remain, because her husband refused her. The Lord will cleanse her.
And the vow of a widow or a divorced woman—whatever she vowed concerning herself—shall remain against her.
If her vow was made in her husband’s house, or her restriction was imposed upon herself with an oath,
and her husband hears, and remains silent toward her, and does not refuse her, then all her vows shall stand, and all her restrictions which she imposed upon her soul shall stand against her.

But if her husband utterly annuls them on the day he hears, then whatever came from her lips concerning her vows and the restrictions upon herself shall not remain against her. Her husband has annulled them, and the Lord will cleanse her.
Every vow and every oath imposing a restriction to afflict her soul—her husband may establish it, or her husband may annul it.

But if he remains utterly silent toward her from day to day, he shall establish all her vows, and he shall establish the restrictions upon her, because he kept silence toward her on the day when he heard.
But if he annuls them after the day on which he heard, he shall bear his sin.
These are the ordinances that the Lord commanded Moses between a man and his wife, and between a father and his daughter in her youth in her father’s house.

title: Unworked stone in Israel’s altar law
paragraphs: Study 29: Unworked stone in Israel’s altar law
Related indexed requirements: C0161, C0162. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Connection to Christ: Hebrews relates the former sanctuary order to Christ; it does not separately identify the unworked-stone rule as a prediction about him.
Christian response today: Offer praise and generosity to God without treating a particular altar construction method as a universal Christian duty.
Saints Translation — Law: Exodus 20:24–25 Christ and the apostles: Hebrews 9:1–14 · Hebrews 13:15–16
Text and setting: Sanctuary instruction
Torah: Exodus 20:24–25

The law permits an altar of earth and specifies unworked stones when a stone altar is built. It addresses Israel’s worship arrangements, not a universal prohibition on tools or worked stone. Hebrews explains the former sanctuary in relation to Christ; Christian sacrifices of praise and generosity do not require rebuilding this altar.
Read with Christ and the apostles: Hebrews 9:1–14 · Hebrews 13:15–16

title: Reverence for God’s sanctuary
paragraphs: Study 90: Reverence for God’s sanctuary
Related indexed requirements: C0129, C0636. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Transformed — the sanctuary theme in Christ and his people
Connection to Christ: John identifies Jesus’ body as the temple, and Paul applies temple language to believers; Leviticus itself refers to Israel’s sanctuary and Sabbath.
Christian response today: Honor Christ and care for his people and your body; offer worship and a holy life through him, with reverence in the places where the church gathers.
Saints Translation — Law: Leviticus 19:30 Christ and the apostles: John 2:13–22 · 1 Corinthians 6:19–20
Ancient covenant practice: Leviticus commands reverence for God’s sanctuary within Israel’s worship.

Development in Christ and the apostles: John identifies the temple of which Jesus speaks as his body. Paul applies temple language to the community and to the believer’s body; Peter describes a spiritual house offering spiritual sacrifices through Christ.
Saints Translation support: John 2:19–22 · 1 Corinthians 3:16–17 · 1 Corinthians 6:19–20 · 1 Peter 2:4–5
Basis and scope: Direct New Testament temple imagery; application to this Torah command is interpretive.

Read carefully: The original verse means Israel’s sanctuary. Its accompanying Sabbath command is not automatically relabeled here, and the temple imagery does not make sacred places or Jewish worship contemptible.
What Transformed means · Browse transformed practices

Leviticus commands Sabbath observance and reverence for God’s sanctuary. It does not call an individual body a temple in this verse. John and Paul provide later temple teaching, including Paul’s moral application to the body. That is a Christian connection, not a replacement of the Torah passage’s original referent.

title: Worship according to God’s instruction
paragraphs: Study 124: Worship according to God’s instruction
Related indexed requirements: C0571, C1012, C1013, C1014, C1015. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Transformed — worship beyond one required sanctuary location
Connection to Christ: Jesus’ teaching in John 4 addresses worship beyond the rival claims of particular mountains; this informs the chosen-sanctuary law.
Christian response today: Worship the Father in spirit and truth through Christ, obey his teaching and gather with fellow believers wherever you live.
Saints Translation — Law: Deuteronomy 12:8–14 Christ and the apostles: Matthew 7:21–23 · John 4:23–24 · John 4:21–24
Ancient covenant practice: Deuteronomy directs Israel’s offerings to the place God chooses rather than to self-selected sanctuaries.

Development in Christ and the apostles: Jesus tells the Samaritan woman of worship no longer defined by the rivalry between her mountain and Jerusalem. The Father seeks worshipers in spirit and truth; Hebrews describes access through Christ.
Saints Translation support: John 4:21–24 · Hebrews 10:19–25
Basis and scope: Direct teaching of Jesus on worship, applied to the Torah’s chosen-place requirement.
Read carefully: This does not turn worship into doing whatever seems right to oneself, nor does it prohibit churches, pilgrimages or reverence for historic holy places.
What Transformed means · Browse transformed practices

The warning about doing what is right in one’s own eyes occurs here in the transition to worship at the place God chooses. It should not be detached into a prohibition on all individual judgment. Christian obedience likewise requires more than personal sincerity, while Jesus’ teaching about worship must govern the later application.

title: No Asherah or sacred pillar beside the altar
paragraphs: Study 136: No Asherah or sacred pillar beside the altar
Related indexed requirements: C0738, C1052. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Connection to Christ: Paul’s rejection of idolatrous participation carries forward the moral concern, while the particular altar arrangement remains contextual.

The prohibition concerns an Asherah and a sacred pillar associated with worship beside the Lord’s altar. It is not a blanket ban on all trees near a place of worship. The Christian connection is the rejection of idolatrous participation, while the specific altar setting and named cult objects should remain clear.

title: Exodus 20:18–26 · Fear God and avoid sin; no silver or gold gods; earthen or unhewn altars and modest approach
paragraphs: Passage group: Fear God and avoid sin; no silver or gold gods; earthen or unhewn altars and modest approach. Setting: Covenant instruction.
Saints 20:13–15 orders adultery, theft and murder. The verse links follow the actual Saints text.
Requirements appearing in this passage: C0147, C0160, C0161, C0162, C0163. A mixed passage can link to more than one topic or classification.
Exodus 20:18 — All the people saw the sound, the flashes, the trumpet’s sound, and the smoking mountain. All the people were afraid and stood far away.
Exodus 20:19 — And they said to Moses, “Speak to us yourself, and do not let God speak to us, lest we die.”
Exodus 20:20 — And Moses said to them, “Take courage; for God has come to you to test you, that His fear may be in you, so that you do not sin.”
Exodus 20:21 — The people stood far away, while Moses entered the thick darkness where God was.
Exodus 20:22 — And the Lord said to Moses, “This is what you shall say to the house of Jacob, and declare to the sons of Israel: ‘You have seen that I have spoken to you from heaven.
Exodus 20:23 — You shall not make gods of silver for yourselves, nor shall you make gods of gold for yourselves.

Exodus 20:24 — You shall make an altar of earth to Me and sacrifice on it your whole burnt offerings and your sacrifices of deliverance, your sheep and your calves, in every place where I name My name; and I will come to you and bless you.
Exodus 20:25 — But if you make Me an altar of stones, you shall not build with hewn stones; for you have laid your blade upon them, and they are defiled.
Exodus 20:26 — You shall not go up by steps to My altar, lest you uncover your nakedness on it.’”

verses.text: All the people saw the sound, the flashes, the trumpet’s sound, and the smoking mountain. All the people were afraid and stood far away.
And they said to Moses, “Speak to us yourself, and do not let God speak to us, lest we die.”
And Moses said to them, “Take courage; for God has come to you to test you, that His fear may be in you, so that you do not sin.”
The people stood far away, while Moses entered the thick darkness where God was.
And the Lord said to Moses, “This is what you shall say to the house of Jacob, and declare to the sons of Israel: ‘You have seen that I have spoken to you from heaven.
You shall not make gods of silver for yourselves, nor shall you make gods of gold for yourselves.

You shall make an altar of earth to Me and sacrifice on it your whole burnt offerings and your sacrifices of deliverance, your sheep and your calves, in every place where I name My name; and I will come to you and bless you.
But if you make Me an altar of stones, you shall not build with hewn stones; for you have laid your blade upon them, and they are defiled.
You shall not go up by steps to My altar, lest you uncover your nakedness on it.’”

title: Exodus 25:1–40 · Contributions, the sanctuary pattern, ark, cover, cherubim, table, utensils and lampstand
paragraphs: Passage group: Contributions, the sanctuary pattern, ark, cover, cherubim, table, utensils and lampstand. Setting: Sanctuary instructions.

Requirements appearing in this passage: C0251, C0252, C0253, C0254, C0255, C0256, C0257, C0258, C0259, C0260, C0261, C0262, C0263, C0264, C0265, C0266, C0267. A mixed passage can link to more than one topic or classification.
Exodus 25:1 — The Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
Exodus 25:2 — “Speak to the sons of Israel, and receive firstfruits for Me from everyone whose heart is willing. You shall receive My firstfruits.
Exodus 25:3 — This is the firstfruit offering you shall receive from them: gold, silver, and bronze;
Exodus 25:4 — blue, purple, double scarlet, spun fine linen, and goats’ hair;
Exodus 25:5 — rams’ skins dyed red, blue skins, and decay-resistant wood;
Exodus 25:7 — sardius stones and stones for engraving, for the shoulder-piece and full-length robe.
Exodus 25:8 — And you shall make Me a sanctuary, and I will appear among you.
Exodus 25:9 — And you shall make it for Me according to all that I show you upon the mountain, the pattern of the tabernacle, and the pattern of all its vessels; this is how you shall make it.
Exodus 25:10 — You shall make an ark of testimony of decay-resistant wood, two and a half cubits long, a cubit and a half wide, and a cubit and a half high.
Exodus 25:11 — You shall overlay it with pure gold, outside and inside, and make twisted gold mouldings around it.
Exodus 25:12 — You shall fashion four gold rings for it and place them on its four sides, two rings on one side and two on the other.
Exodus 25:13 — You shall make carrying poles of decay-resistant wood and overlay them with gold.
Exodus 25:14 — You shall put the poles through the rings on the ark’s sides to carry the ark with them.
Exodus 25:15 — The carrying poles shall remain fixed in the ark’s rings.
Exodus 25:16 — And you shall put into the ark the testimonies which I shall give you.
Exodus 25:17 — You shall make a propitiatory cover of pure gold, two and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.
Exodus 25:18 — You shall make two cherubim of worked gold and place them at the two sides of the propitiatory cover.
Exodus 25:19 — One cherub shall be made at this side and one at the other side of the propitiatory cover. You shall make the two cherubim at its two sides.
Exodus 25:20 — The cherubim shall spread their wings above, overshadowing the propitiatory cover with their wings. Their faces shall be toward one another, facing the propitiatory cover.
Exodus 25:21 — You shall place the propitiatory cover on top of the ark, and put into the ark the testimonies I will give you.

Exodus 25:22 — And I will be made known to you from there, and speak to you from above the propitiatory cover, from between the two cherubim upon the ark of the testimony, concerning all that I command you for the sons of Israel.
Exodus 25:23 — You shall make a table of pure gold, two cubits long, a cubit wide, and a cubit and a half high.
Exodus 25:24 — You shall make twisted gold mouldings around it.
Exodus 25:25 — You shall make a rim a handbreadth wide around it, and a twisted moulding around the rim.
Exodus 25:26 — You shall make four gold rings and put them at the four parts of its legs
Exodus 25:27 — beneath the rim; and the rings shall be holders for the carrying poles, that the table may be borne with them.
Exodus 25:28 — You shall make the carrying poles of decay-resistant wood and overlay them with pure gold, and the table shall be carried with them.
Exodus 25:29 — You shall make its dishes, incense cups, libation vessels, and cups for pouring libations. You shall make them of pure gold.
Exodus 25:30 — You shall place the bread of the Presence on the table before Me continually.
Exodus 25:31 — You shall make a lampstand of pure gold, of worked metal. Its stem, branches, bowls, knobs, and lilies shall be made from it.
Exodus 25:32 — Six branches shall extend from its sides, three from one side of the lampstand and three from the other.
Exodus 25:33 — There shall be three bowls shaped like little nuts, with a knob and lily on one branch. So it shall be for the six branches extending from the lampstand.
Exodus 25:34 — On the lampstand there shall be four bowls shaped like little nuts; on one branch shall be its knobs and lilies.
Exodus 25:35 — There shall be a knob under the two branches extending from it, and a knob under the four branches extending from it; so it shall be for the six branches extending from the lampstand.
Exodus 25:36 — Its knobs and branches shall be made from it, the whole worked from one piece of pure gold.
Exodus 25:37 — You shall make its seven lamps and set them on it, and they shall shine from one face.
Exodus 25:38 — You shall make its snuffer and supports of pure gold.
Exodus 25:39 — All these utensils shall be a talent of pure gold.
Exodus 25:40 — See that you make them according to the pattern shown to you on the mountain.”

verses.text: The Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the sons of Israel, and receive firstfruits for Me from everyone whose heart is willing. You shall receive My firstfruits.
This is the firstfruit offering you shall receive from them: gold, silver, and bronze;
blue, purple, double scarlet, spun fine linen, and goats’ hair;
rams’ skins dyed red, blue skins, and decay-resistant wood;
sardius stones and stones for engraving, for the shoulder-piece and full-length robe.
And you shall make Me a sanctuary, and I will appear among you.
And you shall make it for Me according to all that I show you upon the mountain, the pattern of the tabernacle, and the pattern of all its vessels; this is how you shall make it.
You shall make an ark of testimony of decay-resistant wood, two and a half cubits long, a cubit and a half wide, and a cubit and a half high.
You shall overlay it with pure gold, outside and inside, and make twisted gold mouldings around it.
You shall fashion four gold rings for it and place them on its four sides, two rings on one side and two on the other.
You shall make carrying poles of decay-resistant wood and overlay them with gold.
You shall put the poles through the rings on the ark’s sides to carry the ark with them.
The carrying poles shall remain fixed in the ark’s rings.
And you shall put into the ark the testimonies which I shall give you.
You shall make a propitiatory cover of pure gold, two and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.
You shall make two cherubim of worked gold and place them at the two sides of the propitiatory cover.
One cherub shall be made at this side and one at the other side of the propitiatory cover. You shall make the two cherubim at its two sides.
The cherubim shall spread their wings above, overshadowing the propitiatory cover with their wings. Their faces shall be toward one another, facing the propitiatory cover.
You shall place the propitiatory cover on top of the ark, and put into the ark the testimonies I will give you.

And I will be made known to you from there, and speak to you from above the propitiatory cover, from between the two cherubim upon the ark of the testimony, concerning all that I command you for the sons of Israel.
You shall make a table of pure gold, two cubits long, a cubit wide, and a cubit and a half high.
You shall make twisted gold mouldings around it.
You shall make a rim a handbreadth wide around it, and a twisted moulding around the rim.
You shall make four gold rings and put them at the four parts of its legs
beneath the rim; and the rings shall be holders for the carrying poles, that the table may be borne with them.
You shall make the carrying poles of decay-resistant wood and overlay them with pure gold, and the table shall be carried with them.
You shall make its dishes, incense cups, libation vessels, and cups for pouring libations. You shall make them of pure gold.
You shall place the bread of the Presence on the table before Me continually.
You shall make a lampstand of pure gold, of worked metal. Its stem, branches, bowls, knobs, and lilies shall be made from it.
Six branches shall extend from its sides, three from one side of the lampstand and three from the other.
There shall be three bowls shaped like little nuts, with a knob and lily on one branch. So it shall be for the six branches extending from the lampstand.
On the lampstand there shall be four bowls shaped like little nuts; on one branch shall be its knobs and lilies.
There shall be a knob under the two branches extending from it, and a knob under the four branches extending from it; so it shall be for the six branches extending from the lampstand.
Its knobs and branches shall be made from it, the whole worked from one piece of pure gold.
You shall make its seven lamps and set them on it, and they shall shine from one face.
You shall make its snuffer and supports of pure gold.
All these utensils shall be a talent of pure gold.
See that you make them according to the pattern shown to you on the mountain.”

title: Exodus 26:1–37 · Curtains, coverings, frames, bars, veil and entrance screen
paragraphs: Passage group: Curtains, coverings, frames, bars, veil and entrance screen. Setting: Sanctuary instructions.
Requirements appearing in this passage: C0252, C0268, C0269, C0270, C0271, C0272, C0273, C0274, C0275, C0276. A mixed passage can link to more than one topic or classification.
Exodus 26:1 — “You shall make the tabernacle with ten curtains of spun fine linen, blue, purple, and spun scarlet yarn. You shall make them with cherubim, the work of a weaver.
Exodus 26:2 — Each curtain shall be twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide. All the curtains shall have the same measure.
Exodus 26:3 — Five curtains shall be joined to one another, and the other five joined to one another.
Exodus 26:4 — You shall make blue loops along the edge of one curtain at the joining side, and do the same along the edge of the outer curtain at the second joining.
Exodus 26:5 — You shall make fifty loops on the one curtain and fifty along the edge of the curtain in the second set, with the loops opposite one another.
Exodus 26:6 — You shall make fifty clasps of gold, and join the curtains one to another with the clasps; and the tabernacle shall be one.
Exodus 26:7 — You shall make hair curtains as a covering over the tabernacle. You shall make eleven curtains.
Exodus 26:8 — Each curtain shall be thirty cubits long and four cubits wide. The eleven curtains shall have the same measure.
Exodus 26:9 — You shall join five hair curtains by themselves and six by themselves, and double over the sixth curtain at the front of the tabernacle.
Exodus 26:10 — You shall make fifty loops along the edge of the middle hair curtain at the joining, and fifty along the edge of the curtain joining the second set.
Exodus 26:11 — You shall make fifty clasps of bronze, and fasten the clasps into the loops, and join the hair curtains; and they shall be one.

Exodus 26:12 — You shall tuck under the surplus in the tabernacle’s hair curtains. You shall cover over the remaining half curtain; you shall cover over the surplus of the tabernacle’s hair curtains behind the tabernacle.
Exodus 26:13 — A cubit on this side and a cubit on that side, from the excess length of the tabernacle’s hair curtains, shall cover the tabernacle’s sides on either side.
Exodus 26:14 — You shall make a covering for the tabernacle of rams’ skins dyed red, with coverings of blue skins above it.
Exodus 26:15 — You shall make posts of decay-resistant wood for the tabernacle.
Exodus 26:16 — You shall make each post ten cubits long, and the breadth of each post shall be a cubit and a half.
Exodus 26:17 — Each post shall have two tenons fitted opposite each other. You shall make all the tabernacle’s posts this way.
Exodus 26:18 — You shall make twenty posts for the tabernacle’s north side.
Exodus 26:19 — You shall make forty silver bases for the twenty posts, two bases for one post at its two parts, and two bases for another post at its two parts.
Exodus 26:20 — For the second side, to the south, there shall be twenty posts,
Exodus 26:21 — with their forty silver bases, two bases for one post at its two parts, and two bases for another post at its two parts.
Exodus 26:22 — For the rear of the tabernacle, toward the sea, you shall make six posts.
Exodus 26:23 — You shall make two posts for the corners at the rear of the tabernacle.
Exodus 26:24 — They shall be equal below, and likewise equal at their tops, at one joining. You shall make both this way for the two corners.
Exodus 26:25 — There shall be eight posts with sixteen silver bases, two for each post at its two parts, and two for each post.
Exodus 26:26 — You shall make bars of decay-resistant wood, five for the post on one side of the tabernacle,
Exodus 26:27 — five for the post on the second side, and five for the rear post on the side toward the sea.
Exodus 26:28 — The middle bar shall pass through the middle of the posts from one side to the other.
Exodus 26:29 — You shall overlay the posts with gold and make gold rings into which you shall insert the bars. You shall overlay the bars with gold.
Exodus 26:30 — You shall erect the tabernacle according to the plan shown to you on the mountain.
Exodus 26:31 — You shall make a veil of blue, purple, and spun scarlet yarn and spun fine linen, with cherubim, the work of a weaver.
Exodus 26:32 — You shall place it on four posts of decay-resistant wood overlaid with gold, with gold capitals and four silver bases.

Exodus 26:33 — And you shall set the veil upon the posts, and bring in there, within the veil, the ark of the testimony; and the veil shall divide for you between the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies.
Exodus 26:34 — You shall screen the ark of the testimony with the veil in the Holy of Holies.
Exodus 26:35 — You shall place the table outside the veil and the lampstand opposite it on the tabernacle’s south side; the table shall be on the north side.
Exodus 26:36 — You shall make a screen of blue, purple, and spun scarlet yarn and spun fine linen, the work of an embroiderer.
Exodus 26:37 — You shall make five posts for the curtain and overlay them with gold, with gold capitals, and cast five bronze bases for them.”

For the second side, to the south, there shall be twenty posts,
with their forty silver bases, two bases for one post at its two parts, and two bases for another post at its two parts.
For the rear of the tabernacle, toward the sea, you shall make six posts.
You shall make two posts for the corners at the rear of the tabernacle.
They shall be equal below, and likewise equal at their tops, at one joining. You shall make both this way for the two corners.
There shall be eight posts with sixteen silver bases, two for each post at its two parts, and two for each post.
You shall make bars of decay-resistant wood, five for the post on one side of the tabernacle,
five for the post on the second side, and five for the rear post on the side toward the sea.
The middle bar shall pass through the middle of the posts from one side to the other.
You shall overlay the posts with gold and make gold rings into which you shall insert the bars. You shall overlay the bars with gold.
You shall erect the tabernacle according to the plan shown to you on the mountain.
You shall make a veil of blue, purple, and spun scarlet yarn and spun fine linen, with cherubim, the work of a weaver.
You shall place it on four posts of decay-resistant wood overlaid with gold, with gold capitals and four silver bases.
And you shall set the veil upon the posts, and bring in there, within the veil, the ark of the testimony; and the veil shall divide for you between the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies.
You shall screen the ark of the testimony with the veil in the Holy of Holies.
You shall place the table outside the veil and the lampstand opposite it on the tabernacle’s south side; the table shall be on the north side.
You shall make a screen of blue, purple, and spun scarlet yarn and spun fine linen, the work of an embroiderer.

Exodus 28:6 — They shall make the shoulder-piece of spun fine linen, the work of a skilled weaving embroiderer.
Exodus 28:7 — It shall have two shoulder-pieces joined to one another, fitted at the two sides.
Exodus 28:8 — The woven work of the shoulder-pieces upon it shall be made as one piece with it, of the same workmanship: gold, blue, purple, spun scarlet yarn, and spun fine linen.

Exodus 28:15 — You shall make an oracle-piece of judgments, embroidered work, according to the pattern of the shoulder-piece, of gold, blue, purple, spun scarlet yarn, and spun fine linen.
Exodus 28:16 — It shall be square and doubled, a span long and a span wide.
Exodus 28:17 — You shall weave into it a fabric set with four rows of stones. The first row shall be a sardius, topaz, and emerald;

Exodus 28:20 — the fourth row a chrysolite, beryl, and onyx. They shall be enclosed in gold and bound in gold according to their rows.
Exodus 28:21 — The stones shall bear the names of the sons of Israel, twelve according to their names, each engraved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes.
Exodus 28:22 — You shall make braided chains of pure gold for the oracle-piece.
Exodus 28:29 — And Aaron shall bear the names of the sons of Israel upon the oracle-piece of judgment, upon his breast, when he enters into the sanctuary, as a memorial before God.

Exodus 28:30 — And you shall set Manifestation and Truth upon the oracle-piece of judgment; and it shall be upon Aaron’s breast when he enters into the sanctuary before the Lord. And Aaron shall bear the judgments of the sons of Israel upon his breast before the Lord continually.
Exodus 28:31 — You shall make a full-length under-robe entirely blue.
Exodus 28:32 — And its neck opening shall be in the midst of it, with a border around the opening, the work of a weaver, its joining woven as one with it, so that it is not torn.

Exodus 28:33 — Around the under-robe’s lower hem you shall make little pomegranates like those of a flowering pomegranate tree, of blue, purple, spun scarlet yarn, and spun fine linen; likewise gold pomegranates, with bells between them all around.
Exodus 28:34 — Beside a gold pomegranate there shall be a bell and a floral ornament around the under-robe’s hem.
Exodus 28:35 — And Aaron’s sound shall be heard when he ministers, as he enters into the sanctuary before the Lord and as he goes out, so that he does not die.
Exodus 28:36 — You shall make a plate of pure gold and stamp on it like a seal: ‘The Lord’s consecrated thing.’
Exodus 28:37 — You shall fasten it to spun blue material so that it may rest on the headband, at the front of the headband.

Exodus 28:38 — It shall be on Aaron’s forehead, and Aaron shall remove the sins of the holy things the sons of Israel consecrate, of every holy gift. It shall be on Aaron’s forehead continually, acceptable for them before the Lord.
Exodus 28:39 — The tunics’ tassels shall be of fine linen. You shall make a fine-linen turban and an embroidered sash.
Exodus 28:40 — You shall make tunics, sashes, and turbans for Aaron’s sons, for honour and glory.
Exodus 28:41 — You shall clothe Aaron your brother and his sons with these garments, anoint them, fill their hands, and consecrate them to serve Me as priests.
Exodus 28:42 — You shall make linen undergarments for them to cover the nakedness of their flesh, reaching from the waist to the thighs.

Exodus 28:43 — And Aaron and his sons shall wear them when they enter into the Tent of Testimony, or draw near to minister at the altar of the sanctuary; and they shall not bring sin upon themselves, lest they die. It shall be an everlasting statute for him and for his seed after him.”

Whenever the cloud rose from the tent, the sons of Israel set out with their belongings.
If the cloud did not rise, they did not set out until the day it rose.
For a cloud was over the tent by day, and fire was over it by night, in the sight of all Israel throughout all their journeys.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:

And assemble the whole congregation at the entrance of the Tent of Testimony.
And Moses did as the Lord directed him, and he assembled the congregation at the door of the Tent of Testimony.
And Moses said unto the congregation: This is the word which the Lord commanded to be done.
And Moses brought Aaron and his sons forward and washed them with water.

And he clothed him with the tunic, girded him with the belt, clothed him with the under-robe, and put the shoulder-piece on him. He girded him according to the shoulder-piece’s workmanship and fastened him securely in it.
And he placed the oracle-piece on it and put Manifestation and Truth upon the oracle-piece.
And he put the turban on his head and placed on its front the gold plate, the consecrated holy object, as the Lord directed Moses.
And Moses took some of the anointing oil,

and sprinkled some of it on the altar seven times. He anointed the altar and consecrated it, and all its utensils, the basin and its stand, and consecrated them. He anointed the tent and everything in it and consecrated it.
And Moses poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron’s head, anointed him, and consecrated him.
And Moses brought Aaron’s sons forward, clothed them with tunics, girded them with belts, and put turbans on them, as the Lord directed Moses.
And Moses brought the calf for the sin offering forward, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the head of the calf of the sin offering.

And he slaughtered it, and Moses took some of the blood and put it with his finger all around on the altar’s horns, cleansing the altar. He poured out the blood at the altar’s base and consecrated it, to make atonement upon it.
And Moses took all the fat on the inward parts, the lobe on the liver, both kidneys and the fat on them, and Moses offered them up on the altar.
And he burned up the calf, its hide, its flesh, and its dung with fire outside the camp, as the Lord directed Moses.
And Moses brought the ram for the whole burnt offering forward, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the ram’s head.
And Moses slaughtered the ram, and Moses poured the blood all around against the altar.
And he divided the ram limb by limb, and Moses offered up the head, the limbs, and the fat.
And he washed the belly and feet with water, and Moses offered up the whole ram on the altar: a whole burnt offering for a sweet savour, an offering unto the Lord, as the Lord commanded Moses.
And Moses brought the second ram forward, a ram of consecration, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the ram’s head.
And he slaughtered it, and Moses took some of its blood and put it upon Aaron’s right earlobe, the extremity of his right hand, and the extremity of his right foot.

And Moses brought Aaron’s sons forward, and Moses put some of the blood on their right earlobes, the extremities of their right hands, and the extremities of their right feet. Moses poured the blood all around against the altar.
And he took the fat, the loin, the fat on the belly, the lobe of the liver, the two kidneys and the fat on them, and the right foreleg.
And from the basket of consecration before the Lord he took one unleavened loaf, one loaf with oil, and one wafer, and placed them on the fat and the right foreleg.
And he put everything on Aaron’s hands and his sons’ hands and offered them up as a portion set apart before the Lord.
And Moses took them from their hands, and Moses offered them up on the altar upon the whole burnt offering of consecration, which is a sweet savour, an offering unto the Lord.
And Moses took the breast and removed it as a presentation before the Lord from the ram of consecration. It became Moses’ portion, as the Lord commanded Moses.

And Moses took some of the anointing oil and some of the blood on the altar and sprinkled Aaron and his garments, and his sons and their garments with him. He consecrated Aaron and his garments, and his sons and their garments with him.

And Moses said unto Aaron and his sons: Boil the flesh in the court of the Tent of Testimony, in a holy place, and there you shall eat it, and the loaves in the basket of consecration, as I have been directed, saying: Aaron and his sons shall eat them.
And what remains of the flesh and loaves shall be burned up with fire.
And you shall not go out from the door of the Tent of Testimony for seven days, until the day is fulfilled, the day of your consecration; for he shall consecrate your hands for seven days.
As he has done this day, the Lord commanded it to be done, to make atonement for you.
And you shall remain at the door of the Tent of Testimony seven days, day and night; you shall keep the charges of the Lord, so that you do not die, for thus the Lord God commanded me.
And Aaron and his sons did all the things the Lord directed Moses.

title: Leviticus 9:1–24 · Aaron's and Israel's offerings, approach to the altar, sacrifice and blessing

Leviticus 9:1 — And it came to pass on the eighth day that Moses called Aaron and his sons and the council of elders of Israel.
Leviticus 9:2 — And Moses said unto Aaron: Take unto yourself a calf from the cattle for sin, and a ram for a whole burnt offering, unblemished, and present them before the Lord.

title: Leviticus 21:1–24 · Priests' contact with the dead, mourning, marriage, family, high priest and bodily conditions affecting altar service
paragraphs: Passage group: Priests' contact with the dead, mourning, marriage, family, high priest and bodily conditions affecting altar service. Setting: Priestly holiness.

Requirements appearing in this passage: C0213, C0591, C0632, C0633, C0654, C0655, C0656, C0657, C0658, C0659, C0660, C0661, C0662, C0663, C0664, C0665, C0666, C0667, C0668, C0669. A mixed passage can link to more than one topic or classification.
Leviticus 21:1 — And the Lord said unto Moses, saying: Speak unto the priests, the sons of Aaron, and you shall say unto them: They shall not be defiled for dead persons among their nation,
Leviticus 21:2 — except for their nearest household kin: father, mother, sons, daughters, and brother;
Leviticus 21:3 — and for a virgin sister near to him who has not been given to a man—for these he may defile himself.
Leviticus 21:4 — He shall not suddenly defile himself among his people, so as to profane himself.
Leviticus 21:5 — And you shall not shave a bald patch on your head for a dead person. They shall not shave the face of their beard or cut incisions in their flesh.
Leviticus 21:6 — They shall be holy to their God and not profane the name of their God, for they present the Lord’s sacrifices, the gifts of their God; therefore they shall be holy.
Leviticus 21:7 — They shall not take a woman who is a prostitute or profaned, nor a woman expelled by her husband, for the priest is holy unto the Lord his God.
Leviticus 21:8 — And he shall sanctify him; this man presents the gifts of the Lord your God. He shall be holy, for I am holy, the Lord who sanctifies them.
Leviticus 21:9 — And if a priest’s daughter is profaned by prostituting herself, she profanes her father’s name. She shall be burned with fire.

Leviticus 21:10 — And the high priest among his brethren, upon whose head the anointing oil has been poured, and who has been consecrated to put on the garments, shall not remove his turban, neither shall he rend his garments;
Leviticus 21:11 — and he shall not enter where there is any dead person; he shall not make himself unclean even for his father or mother.
Leviticus 21:12 — And he shall not leave the holy precincts or profane what is consecrated to his God, for the holy anointing oil of God is upon him. I am the Lord.
Leviticus 21:13 — He shall take a virgin wife from his own kin.
Leviticus 21:14 — A widow, an expelled woman, a profaned woman, or a prostitute—these he shall not take. He shall take as his wife only a virgin from his own kin.
Leviticus 21:15 — And he shall not profane his seed among his people, for I am the Lord who sanctifies him.
Leviticus 21:16 — And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Leviticus 21:17 — Say unto Aaron: A man from your kin throughout your generations, in whom there is a blemish, shall not draw near to present the gifts of his God.
Leviticus 21:18 — No man who has a blemish shall approach: a lame man, a blind man, one with a mutilated nose, or one with a cut-off ear;
Leviticus 21:19 — or a man with a broken hand or a broken foot;
Leviticus 21:20 — or a hunchback, one with a skin spot, one with diseased eyelids, a man with a severe scab or skin eruption, or one with a single testicle.

Leviticus 21:21 — No one of the seed of Aaron the priest, in whom there is a blemish, shall draw near to present the sacrifices unto your God; because a blemish is in him, he shall not draw near to present the gifts of God.
Leviticus 21:22 — He may eat the gifts of God, both the most holy things and portions of the holy things.
Leviticus 21:23 — But he shall not approach the veil or come near the altar, because he has a blemish. He shall not profane the holy place of his God, for I am the Lord who sanctifies them.
Leviticus 21:24 — And Moses spoke unto Aaron, to his sons, and to all the sons of Israel.

title: Leviticus 22:1–33 · Priestly purity, household eligibility, restitution for holy food, unblemished animals, newborns, slaughter timing and God's holy name
paragraphs: Passage group: Priestly purity, household eligibility, restitution for holy food, unblemished animals, newborns, slaughter timing and God's holy name. Setting: Holy gifts and acceptable sacrifices.

Requirements appearing in this passage: C0124, C0211, C0214, C0329, C0371, C0394, C0449, C0450, C0591, C0670, C0671, C0672, C0673, C0674, C0675, C0676, C0677, C0678. A mixed passage can link to more than one topic or classification.
Leviticus 22:1 — And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Leviticus 22:2 — Tell Aaron and his sons to exercise care concerning the holy things of the sons of Israel, which they consecrate to Me, and not profane My holy name. I am the Lord.

Leviticus 22:3 — Say unto them: Throughout your generations, any man of all your seed who draws near unto the holy things which the sons of Israel consecrate unto the Lord, while his uncleanness is upon him, that soul shall be destroyed from before Me; I am the Lord your God.

Leviticus 22:4 — And any man among the seed of Aaron the priest who has leprosy or a seminal discharge shall not eat the holy things until he is cleansed. Nor shall one who touches any uncleanness of a person, or a man from whom an emission of semen goes out,
Leviticus 22:5 — or anyone who touches any unclean creeping creature that defiles him, or a human being who defiles him through any uncleanness of his.
Leviticus 22:6 — The soul that touches them shall be unclean until evening; he shall not eat of the holy things unless he has bathed his body in water;
Leviticus 22:7 — and when the sun sets, he shall be clean; afterward he may eat the holy things, for they are his bread.
Leviticus 22:8 — He shall not eat an animal found dead or torn by beasts, becoming unclean through them. I am the Lord.
Leviticus 22:9 — And they shall keep My requirements, so that they do not incur sin through them and die through them if they profane them. I am the Lord God who sanctifies them.
Leviticus 22:10 — And no outsider shall eat holy things. A priest’s lodger or hired worker shall not eat holy things.
Leviticus 22:11 — But if a priest acquires a slave purchased with silver, he may eat of his bread; and those born in his house, they also may eat of his bread.
Leviticus 22:12 — And if a priest’s daughter marries an outsider, she shall not eat the first portions of the holy things.

Leviticus 22:13 — And if a priest’s daughter becomes a widow or is expelled, and has no seed, she shall return to her father’s house as in her youth and may eat her father’s bread. But no outsider shall eat of it.
Leviticus 22:14 — And if a man eats holy things in ignorance, he shall add a fifth to it and give the holy thing unto the priest.
Leviticus 22:15 — And they shall not profane the holy things of the sons of Israel that they set aside for the Lord,
Leviticus 22:16 — and so bring upon themselves the lawlessness of an offence by eating their holy things, for I am the Lord who sanctifies them.
Leviticus 22:17 — And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:

Leviticus 22:18 — Speak unto Aaron and unto his sons and unto all the congregation of Israel, and you shall say unto them: Any man of the sons of Israel, or of the sons of the resident foreigners attached unto them in Israel, who presents his gifts according to any of their pledges or any of their freewill offerings, which they present unto God for a whole burnt offering,
Leviticus 22:19 — to be acceptable for you, they shall be males without blemish, from the cattle, the sheep, or the goats.
Leviticus 22:20 — They shall not bring anything with a blemish unto the Lord, for it will not be acceptable for you.

Leviticus 22:21 — And if a man presents a sacrifice of deliverance unto the Lord, specifying a vow by voluntary choice or at your feasts, from the cattle or the sheep, it shall be unblemished to be accepted; there shall be no blemish in it.

Leviticus 22:22 — They shall not bring unto the Lord an animal that is blind, crushed, has its tongue cut, has warts, a severe scab, or skin eruptions. You shall not place any of these on the altar as an offering unto the Lord.
Leviticus 22:23 — And you may slaughter for yourself a calf or a sheep with a cut-off ear or a shortened tail; but for your vow it shall not be accepted.
Leviticus 22:24 — You shall not bring unto the Lord an animal castrated by crushing, or by squeezing out, or by cutting out, or by tearing away; and in your land you shall not do this.

Leviticus 22:25 — And you shall not present any of these as the gifts of your God from the hand of a foreigner, for there are corruptions in them; they have a blemish. These will not be accepted for you.
Leviticus 22:26 — And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:

Leviticus 22:27 — When a calf, sheep, or goat is born, it shall remain under its mother for seven days. On the eighth day and afterward it may be accepted among the gifts, as an offering unto the Lord.
Leviticus 22:28 — And you shall not slaughter a cow or a sheep together with her young on one day.
Leviticus 22:29 — But if you sacrifice a sacrifice, a vow of rejoicing, unto the Lord, you shall sacrifice it so that it is acceptable for you.
Leviticus 22:30 — It shall be eaten that same day. You shall leave none of the flesh until morning. I am the Lord.
Leviticus 22:31 — And you shall keep My commandments, and do them.
Leviticus 22:32 — And you shall not profane the name of the Holy One, and I will be sanctified among the sons of Israel. I am the Lord who sanctifies you,
Leviticus 22:33 — who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the Lord.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Tell Aaron and his sons to exercise care concerning the holy things of the sons of Israel, which they consecrate to Me, and not profane My holy name. I am the Lord.

Say unto them: Throughout your generations, any man of all your seed who draws near unto the holy things which the sons of Israel consecrate unto the Lord, while his uncleanness is upon him, that soul shall be destroyed from before Me; I am the Lord your God.

And any man among the seed of Aaron the priest who has leprosy or a seminal discharge shall not eat the holy things until he is cleansed. Nor shall one who touches any uncleanness of a person, or a man from whom an emission of semen goes out,
or anyone who touches any unclean creeping creature that defiles him, or a human being who defiles him through any uncleanness of his.
The soul that touches them shall be unclean until evening; he shall not eat of the holy things unless he has bathed his body in water;
and when the sun sets, he shall be clean; afterward he may eat the holy things, for they are his bread.
He shall not eat an animal found dead or torn by beasts, becoming unclean through them. I am the Lord.
And they shall keep My requirements, so that they do not incur sin through them and die through them if they profane them. I am the Lord God who sanctifies them.
And no outsider shall eat holy things. A priest’s lodger or hired worker shall not eat holy things.
But if a priest acquires a slave purchased with silver, he may eat of his bread; and those born in his house, they also may eat of his bread.
And if a priest’s daughter marries an outsider, she shall not eat the first portions of the holy things.
And if a priest’s daughter becomes a widow or is expelled, and has no seed, she shall return to her father’s house as in her youth and may eat her father’s bread. But no outsider shall eat of it.
And if a man eats holy things in ignorance, he shall add a fifth to it and give the holy thing unto the priest.
And they shall not profane the holy things of the sons of Israel that they set aside for the Lord,
and so bring upon themselves the lawlessness of an offence by eating their holy things, for I am the Lord who sanctifies them.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:

Speak unto Aaron and unto his sons and unto all the congregation of Israel, and you shall say unto them: Any man of the sons of Israel, or of the sons of the resident foreigners attached unto them in Israel, who presents his gifts according to any of their pledges or any of their freewill offerings, which they present unto God for a whole burnt offering,
to be acceptable for you, they shall be males without blemish, from the cattle, the sheep, or the goats.
They shall not bring anything with a blemish unto the Lord, for it will not be acceptable for you.

And if a man presents a sacrifice of deliverance unto the Lord, specifying a vow by voluntary choice or at your feasts, from the cattle or the sheep, it shall be unblemished to be accepted; there shall be no blemish in it.

They shall not bring unto the Lord an animal that is blind, crushed, has its tongue cut, has warts, a severe scab, or skin eruptions. You shall not place any of these on the altar as an offering unto the Lord.
And you may slaughter for yourself a calf or a sheep with a cut-off ear or a shortened tail; but for your vow it shall not be accepted.
You shall not bring unto the Lord an animal castrated by crushing, or by squeezing out, or by cutting out, or by tearing away; and in your land you shall not do this.
And you shall not present any of these as the gifts of your God from the hand of a foreigner, for there are corruptions in them; they have a blemish. These will not be accepted for you.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
When a calf, sheep, or goat is born, it shall remain under its mother for seven days. On the eighth day and afterward it may be accepted among the gifts, as an offering unto the Lord.
And you shall not slaughter a cow or a sheep together with her young on one day.
But if you sacrifice a sacrifice, a vow of rejoicing, unto the Lord, you shall sacrifice it so that it is acceptable for you.
It shall be eaten that same day. You shall leave none of the flesh until morning. I am the Lord.
And you shall keep My commandments, and do them.
And you shall not profane the name of the Holy One, and I will be sanctified among the sons of Israel. I am the Lord who sanctifies you,
who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the Lord.

And the Lord said unto Moses, saying: Register every firstborn male among the sons of Israel from one month old and upward, and take their number by name.

And you shall take the Levites for Me, I am the Lord, in place of all the firstborn of the sons of Israel, and the livestock of the Levites in place of all the firstborn among the livestock of the sons of Israel.
And Moses registered every firstborn among the sons of Israel, as the Lord commanded.
And all the firstborn males, counted by name from one month old and upward, numbered twenty-two thousand two hundred seventy-three.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Take the Levites in place of every firstborn among the sons of Israel, and the Levites’ livestock in place of their livestock. The Levites shall be Mine. I am the Lord.
And for the ransom of the two hundred seventy-three firstborn sons of Israel who exceed the number of Levites,
you shall take five shekels head by head; you shall take them according to the sacred didrachma, twenty obols to the shekel.
And you shall give the silver unto Aaron and unto his sons, as the ransom of those who exceed their number.
And Moses took the silver, the ransom of those in excess, for the redemption of the Levites.
From the firstborn of the sons of Israel he took the silver: one thousand three hundred sixty-five sanctuary shekels.
And Moses gave the ransom of those in excess unto Aaron and his sons by the voice of the Lord, as the Lord instructed Moses.

Numbers 7:9 — And unto the sons of Kohath he gave none, for they have the ministries of the sanctuary; they shall bear them upon their shoulders.

Numbers 7:11 — And the Lord said unto Moses: One ruler each day, a ruler each day, shall present their gifts for the dedication of the altar.

Numbers 8:6 — Take the Levites from among the sons of Israel, and you shall purify them.

Numbers 8:8 — And they shall take one calf from the cattle, and its sacrifice of fine flour prepared with oil; and you shall take a year-old calf from the cattle for sin.
Numbers 8:9 — And you shall bring the Levites before the Tent of Testimony, and shall gather the whole congregation of the sons of Israel.
Numbers 8:10 — And you shall bring the Levites before the Lord, and the sons of Israel shall lay their hands upon the Levites.
Numbers 8:11 — And Aaron shall set the Levites apart as a gift before the Lord from the sons of Israel, so that they may perform the works of the Lord.

title: Numbers 18:1–32 · Guard the sanctuary; assigned duties; holy portions, firstfruits, firstborn redemption, tithes and the Levites' tithe
paragraphs: Passage group: Guard the sanctuary; assigned duties; holy portions, firstfruits, firstborn redemption, tithes and the Levites' tithe. Setting: Priestly and Levitical law.

Requirements appearing in this passage: C0119, C0674, C0767, C0770, C0772, C0774, C0798, C0873, C0874, C0875, C0876, C0877, C0878, C0879, C0880, C0881, C0882, C0883, C0884. A mixed passage can link to more than one topic or classification.

Numbers 18:1 — And the Lord said unto Aaron, saying: You and your sons and your father’s house shall bear the sins concerning the holy things; and you and your sons shall bear the sins concerning your priesthood.

Numbers 18:2 — And bring your brethren, the tribe of Levi, your father’s clan, near unto you; and let them join you and minister unto you; and you and your sons with you shall be before the Tent of Testimony.
Numbers 18:3 — And they shall keep your charges and the charges of the Tent; only they shall not approach the holy vessels and the altar, that neither they nor you may die.
Numbers 18:4 — And they shall join you, and shall keep the charges of the Tent of Testimony according to all the ministries of the Tent; and the outsider shall not approach you.
Numbers 18:5 — And you shall keep the charges of the holy things and the charges of the altar, and there shall be no wrath among the sons of Israel.
Numbers 18:6 — And I have taken your brothers the Levites from among the sons of Israel, a gift given unto the Lord, to perform the ministries of the Tent of Testimony.

Numbers 18:7 — And you and your sons with you shall keep your priesthood in every matter of the altar and within the veil; and you shall perform the ministries, a gift of your priesthood; and the outsider who approaches shall die.

Numbers 18:8 — And the Lord spoke unto Aaron: And I, behold, have given you charge of the firstfruits; from all things sanctified unto Me by the sons of Israel, I have given them unto you for a share of honour, and unto your sons after you, an everlasting ordinance.

Numbers 18:9 — And this shall be yours from the consecrated holy offerings: from all their gifts, and from all their sacrifices, and from every guilt offering of theirs, and from all their sin offerings which they render unto Me; from all the holy things it shall be yours and your sons’.
Numbers 18:10 — You shall eat them in the most holy place; every male shall eat them, you and your sons; they shall be holy unto you.

Numbers 18:11 — And this shall be yours, the firstfruits of their gifts: from all the presentations of the sons of Israel, I have given them unto you, and unto your sons and unto your daughters with you, an everlasting ordinance. Everyone clean in your house shall eat them.
Numbers 18:12 — Every firstfruit of oil, and every firstfruit of wine and grain, their firstfruits which they give unto the Lord, I have given them unto you.
Numbers 18:13 — All the first produce in their land, which they bring unto the Lord, shall be yours; everyone clean in your house shall eat it.
Numbers 18:14 — Everything devoted among the sons of Israel shall be yours.

Numbers 18:15 — And everything that opens the womb of all flesh, which they present unto the Lord, from man unto livestock, shall be yours; but the firstborn of men shall surely be redeemed, and you shall redeem the firstborn of unclean livestock.
Numbers 18:16 — And its redemption shall be from one month old; the valuation is five shekels by the holy shekel, which is twenty obols.

Numbers 18:17 — But you shall not redeem the firstborn of calves, and the firstborn of sheep, and the firstborn of goats; they are holy. And you shall pour their blood against the altar, and you shall offer up the fat as an offering of sweet savour unto the Lord.
Numbers 18:18 — And their flesh shall be yours; as the breast of the presentation and the right foreleg, it shall be yours.

Numbers 18:19 — Every portion of the holy things which the sons of Israel set apart unto the Lord I have given unto you, and unto your sons and unto your daughters with you, an everlasting ordinance; it is a covenant of everlasting salt before the Lord for you and for your seed after you.
Numbers 18:20 — And the Lord spoke unto Aaron: You shall not inherit in their land, neither shall you have a portion among them; for I am your portion and your inheritance among the sons of Israel.

verses.text: And the Lord said unto Aaron, saying: You and your sons and your father’s house shall bear the sins concerning the holy things; and you and your sons shall bear the sins concerning your priesthood.
And bring your brethren, the tribe of Levi, your father’s clan, near unto you; and let them join you and minister unto you; and you and your sons with you shall be before the Tent of Testimony.
And they shall keep your charges and the charges of the Tent; only they shall not approach the holy vessels and the altar, that neither they nor you may die.
And they shall join you, and shall keep the charges of the Tent of Testimony according to all the ministries of the Tent; and the outsider shall not approach you.
And you shall keep the charges of the holy things and the charges of the altar, and there shall be no wrath among the sons of Israel.
And I have taken your brothers the Levites from among the sons of Israel, a gift given unto the Lord, to perform the ministries of the Tent of Testimony.

And you and your sons with you shall keep your priesthood in every matter of the altar and within the veil; and you shall perform the ministries, a gift of your priesthood; and the outsider who approaches shall die.

And the Lord spoke unto Aaron: And I, behold, have given you charge of the firstfruits; from all things sanctified unto Me by the sons of Israel, I have given them unto you for a share of honour, and unto your sons after you, an everlasting ordinance.

And this shall be yours from the consecrated holy offerings: from all their gifts, and from all their sacrifices, and from every guilt offering of theirs, and from all their sin offerings which they render unto Me; from all the holy things it shall be yours and your sons’.
You shall eat them in the most holy place; every male shall eat them, you and your sons; they shall be holy unto you.

And this shall be yours, the firstfruits of their gifts: from all the presentations of the sons of Israel, I have given them unto you, and unto your sons and unto your daughters with you, an everlasting ordinance. Everyone clean in your house shall eat them.
Every firstfruit of oil, and every firstfruit of wine and grain, their firstfruits which they give unto the Lord, I have given them unto you.
All the first produce in their land, which they bring unto the Lord, shall be yours; everyone clean in your house shall eat it.
Everything devoted among the sons of Israel shall be yours.

And everything that opens the womb of all flesh, which they present unto the Lord, from man unto livestock, shall be yours; but the firstborn of men shall surely be redeemed, and you shall redeem the firstborn of unclean livestock.
And its redemption shall be from one month old; the valuation is five shekels by the holy shekel, which is twenty obols.

But you shall not redeem the firstborn of calves, and the firstborn of sheep, and the firstborn of goats; they are holy. And you shall pour their blood against the altar, and you shall offer up the fat as an offering of sweet savour unto the Lord.
And their flesh shall be yours; as the breast of the presentation and the right foreleg, it shall be yours.

Every portion of the holy things which the sons of Israel set apart unto the Lord I have given unto you, and unto your sons and unto your daughters with you, an everlasting ordinance; it is a covenant of everlasting salt before the Lord for you and for your seed after you.
And the Lord spoke unto Aaron: You shall not inherit in their land, neither shall you have a portion among them; for I am your portion and your inheritance among the sons of Israel.
And to the sons of Levi, look, I have given every tithe in Israel as an allotment in return for their ministries, the service they perform in the Tent of Testimony.
And the sons of Israel shall no longer approach the Tent of Testimony, incurring a death-bringing sin.

And the Levite himself shall perform the ministry of the Tent of Testimony, and they shall bear their offences. It is an everlasting ordinance throughout their generations. Among the sons of Israel they shall receive no inheritance.

For the tithes of the sons of Israel that they set apart for the Lord as a portion set apart I have given to the Levites as an allotment. Therefore I have said to them: Among the sons of Israel they shall receive no allotment.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:

And you shall speak unto the Levites, and shall say unto them: When you receive from the sons of Israel the tithe which I have given you from them for an allotment, you shall take from it a portion set apart unto the Lord, a tithe of the tithe.
And your portions set apart shall be reckoned to you as grain from the threshing floor and as a portion set apart from the winepress.

Thus you shall also take of the portions set apart unto the Lord, from all your tithes which you receive from the sons of Israel; and from them you shall give a portion set apart unto the Lord unto Aaron the priest.
From all your gifts you shall take a portion set apart unto the Lord, or from all the firstfruits the consecrated portion thereof.
And you shall say unto them: When you take the firstfruits from it, it shall be reckoned unto the Levites as produce from the threshing floor and as produce from the winepress.
And you shall eat it in every place, you and your households, for it is your wage in return for your ministries in the Tent of Testimony.
And you shall incur no sin through it, when you take the firstfruits from it; and you shall not profane the holy things of the sons of Israel, lest you die.

Deuteronomy 9:2 — a people great and numerous and tall, the sons of Anak, whom you know, and of whom you have heard: Who shall stand before the sons of Anak?

And you shall know this day that the Lord your God, He goes before you; He is a consuming fire. He shall destroy them, and He shall turn them back from before you, and you shall destroy them, as the Lord has spoken unto you.

when I went up into the mountain to receive the tablets of stone, the tablets of the covenant which the Lord made with you. And I abode in the mountain forty days and forty nights; I ate no bread, and drank no water.
And the Lord gave me the two tablets of stone, written with the finger of God; and upon them were written all the words which the Lord spoke unto you in the mountain, in the day of the assembly.
And after forty days and forty nights, the Lord gave me the two stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant.

And the Lord said unto me: Arise, go down speedily from hence; for your people, whom you brought forth out of the land of Egypt, have acted lawlessly. They have quickly turned aside from the way which you commanded them; they have made for themselves a molten image.
And the Lord said unto me: I have spoken unto you once and twice, saying: I have seen this people, and behold, it is a stiff-necked people.
Let Me destroy them, and I will blot out their name from under heaven, and make you a nation great and strong and more numerous than this.
And I turned and came down from the mountain, and the mountain burned with fire, and the two tablets were in my two hands.
And I saw that you had sinned before the Lord your God, and made for yourselves a molten image, and turned aside from the way which the Lord commanded you.
And I took hold of the two tablets, and cast them out of my two hands, and broke them before your eyes.

And I besought the Lord a second time, as at the first, forty days and forty nights; I ate no bread, and drank no water, because of all your sins which you had sinned, in doing evil before the Lord your God, to provoke Him.

And the Lord was very angry with Aaron, intending to destroy him; I prayed for Aaron also at that time.

And I took your sin, the calf which you had made, and burned it with fire, and broke it in pieces, grinding it thoroughly until it became fine; and it became as dust, and I cast the dust into the torrent that descended from the mountain.
And at Burning, and at Testing, and at the Graves of Desire, you provoked the Lord your God.

And when the Lord sent you forth from Kadesh-barnea, saying: Go up and inherit the land which I give you, you disobeyed the word of the Lord your God, and did not believe Him, and did not hearken unto His voice.
You were disobedient toward the Lord from the day when He became known unto you.
And I besought the Lord forty days and forty nights, during which I besought Him; for the Lord had said that He would destroy you.

And I prayed unto God, and said: O Lord, Lord, King of the gods, destroy not Thy people and Thy portion, whom Thou hast redeemed by Thy great strength, whom Thou hast brought forth out of the land of Egypt by Thy great strength, and by Thy mighty hand, and by Thine uplifted arm.
Remember Thy servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, unto whom Thou didst swear by Thyself. Look not upon the hardness of this people, nor upon their ungodliness, nor upon their sins,

lest the inhabitants of the land whence Thou hast brought us forth say: Because the Lord was not able to bring them into the land which He promised them, and because He hated them, He brought them forth to slay them in the wilderness.
And these are Thy people and Thine inheritance, whom Thou hast brought forth out of the land of Egypt by Thy great strength and by Thine uplifted arm.

title: The firstborn belong to God
paragraphs: Study 18: The firstborn belong to God
Related indexed requirements: C0088, C0115, C0117, C0118, C0119. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Connection to Christ: Luke records Jesus’ presentation under the firstborn law; Hebrews supplies a broader Christian account of consecration through his offering.
Christian response today: Dedicate life to God without presenting Israel’s firstborn redemption procedure as a requirement for every Christian family.
Saints Translation — Law: Exodus 13:1–2 · Exodus 13:11–16 Christ and the apostles: Luke 2:22–24 · Hebrews 10:10
Text and setting: Israel’s worship
Torah: Exodus 13:1–2 · Exodus 13:11–16

Israel is to consecrate its firstborn in remembrance of deliverance, with distinctions between animals offered and firstborn sons redeemed. The text does not authorize sacrificing children. Luke records Jesus’ presentation under this law. Christian dedication is read in the light of Christ’s once-for-all offering, not as a new requirement to reproduce Israel’s sanctuary system.
Read with Christ and the apostles: Luke 2:22–24 · Hebrews 10:10
Connection and evidence: Explicit New Testament treatment. Luke records Jesus’ presentation under the firstborn law; Hebrews supplies a broader Christian account of consecration through his offering.

title: Offerings must not disguise wrongful earnings
paragraphs: Study 148: Offerings must not disguise wrongful earnings
Related indexed requirements: C1161, C1162. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Connection to Christ: Jesus’ teaching on justice and the example of Zacchaeus show why religious giving cannot replace repentance and restitution.
Christian response today: Stop wrongful conduct and make amends rather than using a donation to disguise its proceeds.
Saints Translation — Law: Deuteronomy 23:19 (KJV 23:18) Christ and the apostles: Matthew 23:23 · Luke 19:8–10
Text and setting: Worship and ethics
Torah: Deuteronomy 23:19 (KJV 23:18)

The verse specifically prohibits bringing a prostitute’s earnings or the price of a dog into the Lord’s house for a vow; the meaning of “dog” in this setting is disputed. A broad label such as “dirty money” needs that explanation. A religious donation does not erase an obligation to stop wrongdoing and make restitution.
Read with Christ and the apostles: Matthew 23:23 · Luke 19:8–10
Connection and evidence: Related New Testament teaching. Jesus’ teaching on justice and the example of Zacchaeus show why religious giving cannot replace repentance and restitution.
These passages support a related teaching or moral application. The connection is not presented as a direct quotation of this exact Torah rule.

Requirements appearing in this passage: C0371, C0372, C0373, C0374, C0375, C0376, C0377, C0378, C0379, C0380, C0381, C0382, C0383, C0384, C0385, C1231. A mixed passage can link to more than one topic or classification.
Leviticus 1:1 — And He called unto Moses, and the Lord spoke unto him from the Tent of Testimony, saying,

Leviticus 1:2 — Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: If a man among you brings gifts unto the Lord, you shall bring your gifts from the livestock, from the cattle and from the flock.
Leviticus 1:3 — If his gift is a whole burnt offering from the cattle, he shall bring an unblemished male; he shall bring it unto the door of the Tent of Testimony, acceptable before the Lord.
Leviticus 1:4 — And he shall lay his hand upon the head of the offering, acceptable for him, to make atonement for him.

Leviticus 1:5 — And they shall slaughter the calf before the Lord; and the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall bring the blood, and pour the blood round about upon the altar which is at the doors of the Tent of Testimony.
Leviticus 1:6 — And when they have skinned the whole burnt offering, they shall divide it limb by limb.
Leviticus 1:7 — And the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall put fire upon the altar, and pile wood upon the fire.
Leviticus 1:8 — And the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall pile the divided parts, and the head, and the fat upon the wood upon the fire which is upon the altar.
Leviticus 1:9 — But they shall wash the entrails and the feet with water; and the priests shall place all upon the altar. It is an offering, a sacrifice, a sweet savour unto the Lord.
Leviticus 1:10 — And if his gift unto the Lord is from the flock, from lambs and young goats, for a whole burnt offering, he shall bring an unblemished male, and lay his hand upon its head.
Leviticus 1:11 — And they shall slaughter it at the north side of the altar before the Lord; and the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall pour its blood round about upon the altar.
Leviticus 1:12 — And they shall divide it limb by limb, with the head and the fat; and the priests shall pile them upon the wood upon the fire which is upon the altar.
Leviticus 1:13 — And they shall wash the entrails and the feet with water; and the priest shall bring all, and place it upon the altar. It is an offering, a sacrifice, a sweet savour unto the Lord.
Leviticus 1:14 — And if you bring an offering of birds as a gift unto the Lord, he shall bring his gift from the turtledoves or the pigeons.
Leviticus 1:15 — And the priest shall bring it unto the altar, and pinch off the head; and the priest shall place it upon the altar, and drain the blood at the base of the altar.
Leviticus 1:16 — And he shall remove the crop with the feathers, and cast it beside the altar toward the east, into the place of the ashes.

Leviticus 1:17 — And he shall break it open by its wings, but shall not divide it; and the priest shall place it upon the altar, upon the wood upon the fire. It is an offering, a sacrifice, a sweet savour unto the Lord.

verses.text: And He called unto Moses, and the Lord spoke unto him from the Tent of Testimony, saying,
Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: If a man among you brings gifts unto the Lord, you shall bring your gifts from the livestock, from the cattle and from the flock.
If his gift is a whole burnt offering from the cattle, he shall bring an unblemished male; he shall bring it unto the door of the Tent of Testimony, acceptable before the Lord.
And he shall lay his hand upon the head of the offering, acceptable for him, to make atonement for him.

And they shall slaughter the calf before the Lord; and the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall bring the blood, and pour the blood round about upon the altar which is at the doors of the Tent of Testimony.
And when they have skinned the whole burnt offering, they shall divide it limb by limb.
And the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall put fire upon the altar, and pile wood upon the fire.
And the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall pile the divided parts, and the head, and the fat upon the wood upon the fire which is upon the altar.
But they shall wash the entrails and the feet with water; and the priests shall place all upon the altar. It is an offering, a sacrifice, a sweet savour unto the Lord.
And if his gift unto the Lord is from the flock, from lambs and young goats, for a whole burnt offering, he shall bring an unblemished male, and lay his hand upon its head.
And they shall slaughter it at the north side of the altar before the Lord; and the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall pour its blood round about upon the altar.
And they shall divide it limb by limb, with the head and the fat; and the priests shall pile them upon the wood upon the fire which is upon the altar.
And they shall wash the entrails and the feet with water; and the priest shall bring all, and place it upon the altar. It is an offering, a sacrifice, a sweet savour unto the Lord.
And if you bring an offering of birds as a gift unto the Lord, he shall bring his gift from the turtledoves or the pigeons.
And the priest shall bring it unto the altar, and pinch off the head; and the priest shall place it upon the altar, and drain the blood at the base of the altar.
And he shall remove the crop with the feathers, and cast it beside the altar toward the east, into the place of the ashes.

And he shall break it open by its wings, but shall not divide it; and the priest shall place it upon the altar, upon the wood upon the fire. It is an offering, a sacrifice, a sweet savour unto the Lord.

Leviticus 4:19 — And he shall remove all the fat from it, and offer it up upon the altar.

Leviticus 4:23 — and the sin which he has committed becomes known unto him, he shall bring as his gift an unblemished male young goat from the goats.
Leviticus 4:24 — And he shall lay his hand upon the young goat’s head; and they shall slaughter it in the place where they slaughter the whole burnt offerings before the Lord. It is a sin offering.

Leviticus 4:25 — And the priest shall put some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger upon the horns of the altar of whole burnt offerings; and he shall pour out all its blood beside the base of the altar of whole burnt offerings.
Leviticus 4:26 — And he shall offer up all its fat upon the altar, as the fat of a sacrifice of deliverance. And the priest shall make atonement for him from his sin, and he shall be forgiven.
Leviticus 4:27 — And if one soul from the people of the land sins unintentionally, by doing any of the things which the commandments of the Lord forbid, and commits an offence,
Leviticus 4:28 — and the sin which he has committed becomes known unto him, he shall bring an unblemished female young goat from the goats; he shall bring it for the sin which he has committed.

Leviticus 4:29 — And he shall lay his hand upon the head of his sin offering; and they shall slaughter the female young goat of the sin offering in the place where they slaughter the whole burnt offerings.

Leviticus 4:30 — And the priest shall take some of its blood with his finger, and put it upon the horns of the altar of whole burnt offerings; and he shall pour out all its blood beside the base of the altar.

Leviticus 4:31 — And he shall remove all the fat, as fat is removed from a sacrifice of deliverance; and the priest shall offer it up upon the altar for a sweet savour unto the Lord. And the priest shall make atonement for him, and he shall be forgiven.

Leviticus 4:33 — And he shall lay his hand upon the head of the sin offering; and they shall slaughter it in the place where they slaughter the whole burnt offerings.

Leviticus 4:34 — And the priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger, and put it upon the horns of the altar of whole burning; and he shall pour out all its blood beside the base of the altar of whole burning.

And the priest shall make atonement for him for the sin which he has committed, and he shall be forgiven.
