title: Leviticus 5:1–26 · Witness, impurity, rash oaths, confession, means-based offerings, holy things, guilt, fraud and restitution
paragraphs: Passage group: Witness, impurity, rash oaths, confession, means-based offerings, holy things, guilt, fraud and restitution. Setting: Sacrificial and restitution law.

Requirements appearing in this passage: C0409, C0410, C0411, C0412, C0413, C0414, C0415, C0416, C0417, C0418, C0419, C0420, C0421, C0422, C0423, C0424, C0425, C0426. A mixed passage can link to more than one topic or classification.

Leviticus 5:1 — And if a soul sins, and hears the voice of a solemn adjuration, and he is a witness, whether he has seen or has knowledge of the matter, if he does not declare it, he shall bear the sin.

Leviticus 5:2 — Or if a soul touches any unclean thing, whether a dead thing, or an unclean thing torn by wild beasts, or one of the dead things, or one of the unclean abominations, or a carcass of unclean livestock,
Leviticus 5:3 — or touches human uncleanness, any uncleanness of a man by touching which he is defiled, and it escapes his notice, but afterward he knows it and incurs guilt;

Leviticus 5:4 — or if a soul swears, declaring with his lips to do evil or to do good, whatsoever a man declares with an oath, and it escapes his notice, and he knows it and sins in any one of these matters,
Leviticus 5:5 — he shall confess the sin concerning that wherein he has sinned.

Leviticus 5:6 — And he shall bring unto the Lord, for the offence and the sin which he has committed, a female from the flock, a ewe lamb or a female young goat from the goats, for sin. And the priest shall make atonement for him for the sin which he has committed, and his sin shall be forgiven him.

Leviticus 5:7 — And if his hand cannot provide enough for a sheep, he shall bring unto the Lord for the sin which he has committed two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for sin and one for a whole burnt offering.
Leviticus 5:8 — And he shall bring them unto the priest, and the priest shall bring the one for sin first; and the priest shall pinch its head at the neck joint, but shall not divide it.
Leviticus 5:9 — And he shall sprinkle some of the blood of the offering for sin upon the wall of the altar; but the remaining blood he shall drain at the base of the altar, for it is for sin.
Leviticus 5:10 — And he shall prepare the second as a whole burnt offering, as is fitting. And the priest shall make atonement for the sin which he has committed, and he shall be forgiven.

Leviticus 5:11 — And if his hand cannot obtain a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons, he shall bring his gift for the sin which he has committed: a tenth of an oiphi of fine flour for sin. He shall pour no oil upon it, neither shall he put frankincense upon it, for it is for sin.

Leviticus 5:12 — And he shall bring it unto the priest; and the priest shall take from it a full handful, and place its memorial portion upon the altar of whole burnt offerings unto the Lord. It is a sin offering.

Leviticus 5:13 — And the priest shall make atonement for him for the sin which he has committed in any one of these matters, and he shall be forgiven. But what remains shall be the priest’s, as the sacrifice of fine flour.
Leviticus 5:14 — And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying,

Leviticus 5:15 — If a soul is overtaken by forgetfulness, and sins unintentionally concerning the holy things of the Lord, he shall bring unto the Lord for his offence an unblemished ram from the flock, valued in silver shekels according to the sanctuary shekel, for the offence which he has committed.

Leviticus 5:16 — And he shall repay that wherein he has sinned against the holy things, and add a fifth part unto it, and give it unto the priest; and the priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering, and he shall be forgiven.
Leviticus 5:17 — And if a soul sins, and does any of the things which the commandments of the Lord forbid, though he did not know it, and incurs guilt and bears the sin,

Leviticus 5:18 — he shall bring unto the priest an unblemished ram from the flock, valued in silver, for a guilt offering; and the priest shall make atonement for him for his ignorance, wherein he acted ignorantly and did not know it, and he shall be forgiven.
Leviticus 5:19 — For he has indeed committed an offence before the Lord.
Leviticus 5:20 — And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying,

Leviticus 5:21 — If a soul sins, and utterly disregards the commandments of the Lord, and deals falsely with his neighbour concerning a deposit, or a partnership, or robbery, or any wrong which he has done unto his neighbour,
Leviticus 5:22 — or finds a lost thing and deals falsely concerning it, and swears unjustly concerning any of all the things which a man may do so as to sin therein,

Leviticus 5:23 — then it shall be, when he has sinned and incurred guilt, that he shall return the plunder which he seized, or that which he obtained by wrong, or the deposit which was entrusted unto him, or the lost thing which he found,

Leviticus 5:24 — concerning every matter about which he swore unjustly. And he shall repay the principal, and add a fifth part unto it; he shall repay it unto the one to whom it belongs, on the day when he is convicted.
Leviticus 5:25 — And for his offence he shall bring unto the Lord an unblemished ram from the flock, of a value corresponding to the offence which he has committed against Him.
Leviticus 5:26 — And the priest shall make atonement for him before the Lord, and he shall be forgiven concerning any of all the things which he has done and wherein he has offended Him.

Numbers 15:5 — And you shall prepare wine for a drink offering, a fourth of a hin, with the whole burning or with the sacrifice; you shall prepare this much for each lamb, an offering of sweet savour unto the Lord.
Numbers 15:6 — And for a ram, when you prepare it for a whole burnt offering or for a sacrifice, you shall prepare a sacrifice of two tenths of fine flour mixed with oil, a third of a hin.
Numbers 15:7 — And you shall present wine for a drink offering, a third of a hin, for a sweet savour unto the Lord.
Numbers 15:8 — But if you prepare an animal from the cattle for a whole burnt offering or for a sacrifice to honour a vow, or for a sacrifice of deliverance unto the Lord,
Numbers 15:9 — he shall present with the calf a sacrifice of three tenths of fine flour mixed with oil, half a hin,
Numbers 15:10 — and half a hin of wine as a drink offering, an offering of sweet savour unto the Lord.
Numbers 15:11 — Thus you shall do for each calf, or each ram, or each lamb from the sheep or from the goats.
Numbers 15:12 — According to the number that you prepare, thus you shall do for each one according to their number.
Numbers 15:13 — Every native-born person shall do such things in this way when presenting offerings of sweet savour unto the Lord.

Numbers 15:14 — But if a sojourner who joins you in your land, or whosoever is among you throughout your generations, makes an offering of sweet savour unto the Lord, as you do, so shall the congregation do unto the Lord.
Numbers 15:15 — You shall have one law, both you and the sojourners joined unto you, an everlasting law throughout your generations. As you are, so shall the sojourner be before the Lord.
Numbers 15:16 — One law and one ordinance shall apply to you and the sojourner attached to you.
Numbers 15:17 — And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Numbers 15:18 — Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: When you enter the land whither I bring you,
Numbers 15:19 — then it shall be, when you eat of the loaves of the land, that you shall take a portion, a gift set apart unto the Lord.
Numbers 15:20 — As the firstfruits of your dough, you shall set apart a loaf for a portion set apart; as a portion from the threshing floor, so you shall take it,
Numbers 15:21 — the firstfruits of your dough; and you shall give unto the Lord a portion set apart throughout your generations.
Numbers 15:22 — But when you err, and do not carry out all these commandments which the Lord spoke unto Moses,
Numbers 15:23 — as the Lord commanded you through Moses, from the day the Lord gave command to you and onward throughout your generations,

Numbers 15:24 — And if it happened unintentionally, out of the congregation’s sight, the whole congregation shall prepare one unblemished calf from the cattle as a whole burnt offering of sweet savour unto the Lord, with its sacrifice and drink offering according to the ordinance, and one male goat for sin.

Numbers 15:25 — And the priest shall make atonement for the whole congregation of the sons of Israel, and they shall be forgiven, because it was unintentional. They have brought their gift, an offering unto the Lord for their sin, before the Lord for their unintentional acts.
Numbers 15:26 — And forgiveness shall extend throughout the whole congregation of the sons of Israel and to the sojourner attached to you, because it was unintentional for the whole people.
Numbers 15:27 — But if one soul sins unintentionally, he shall present one year-old female goat for sin.
Numbers 15:28 — And the priest shall make atonement before the Lord for the person who acted unintentionally and sinned unintentionally, making atonement for that person.
Numbers 15:29 — For the native among the sons of Israel, and for the sojourner joined unto them, they shall have one law for whosoever acts unintentionally.
Numbers 15:30 — And the soul that acts with a presumptuous hand, whether of the natives or of the sojourners, provokes God; that soul shall be destroyed from his people,
Numbers 15:31 — because he treated the word of the Lord as worthless, and scattered His commandments. That soul shall surely be wiped out; his sin is upon him.
Numbers 15:32 — And while the sons of Israel were in the wilderness, they found a man gathering wood on the Sabbath day.
Numbers 15:33 — And those who found him gathering wood on the Sabbath day brought him unto Moses, Aaron, and the whole congregation of the sons of Israel.
Numbers 15:34 — And they placed him in custody, because they had not determined what they should do to him.
Numbers 15:35 — And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying: The man must certainly be put to death. Stone him with stones, all the congregation.
Numbers 15:36 — And the whole congregation brought him outside the camp, and the whole congregation stoned him with stones outside the camp, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
Numbers 15:37 — And the Lord said unto Moses, saying:

Numbers 15:38 — Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: Let them make for themselves fringes upon the corners of their garments throughout their generations; and you shall put a blue thread upon the fringes of the corners.

Numbers 15:39 — And it shall be among your fringes; and you shall see them, and remember all the commandments of the Lord, and do them; and you shall not turn aside after your thoughts and after your eyes, after which you go a whoring,
Numbers 15:40 — that you may remember and do all My commandments, and be holy unto your God.
Numbers 15:41 — I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the Lord your God.

as the Lord commanded you through Moses, from the day the Lord gave command to you and onward throughout your generations,

Ancient covenant practice: The Torah prohibits cooking a young goat in its own mother’s milk; later meat-and-dairy practice develops this rule further.
Development in Christ and the apostles: Saints.Bible reads the Christian application through the New Testament’s treatment of food, thanksgiving and consideration for another person’s conscience.
Saints Translation support: Mark 7:18–23 · Romans 14:1–4 · Romans 14:13–23 · 1 Timothy 4:4–5

What Transformed means · Browse transformed practices

Distinguish the biblical text, Jewish interpretive practice and Christian decisions of conscience without presenting them as identical authorities.

Saints Translation — Law: Leviticus 3:16–17 · Leviticus 7:22–25 Christ and the apostles: Hebrews 10:1–10 · Romans 14:2–3

Development in Christ and the apostles: Hebrews locates the former offering order in relation to Christ’s offering. The Christian application of food restrictions is read with thanksgiving and concern for conscience.
Saints Translation support: Hebrews 10:1–10 · Romans 14:13–23 · 1 Timothy 4:4–5 · Acts 15:28–29
Basis and scope: Christian interpretation combining Hebrews’ sacrificial teaching with apostolic food teaching.
Read carefully: The linked food teaching is applied to this case; it does not quote the fat restriction individually. The adjacent prohibition concerning blood must still be read with Acts 15.
What Transformed means · Browse transformed practices

Leviticus concerns fat reserved to the Lord and explicitly names oxen, sheep and goats. “Do not eat fat” without qualification is too broad: the passage is not a ban on every dietary fat, such as olive oil. Its sacrificial setting and Christian teaching about food should accompany any discussion of present practice.

Ancient covenant practice: Leviticus distinguishes clean and unclean animals in Israel’s covenant life.

Development in Christ and the apostles: Jesus locates moral defilement in what comes from the heart. The current Saints reading of Mark 7:19 speaks of cleansing all foods. Paul joins freedom concerning food to love, conscience and thanksgiving. Acts 15 supplies additional apostolic instructions.
Saints Translation support: Mark 7:18–23 · Romans 14:13–23 · 1 Timothy 4:3–5 · Acts 15:28–29 · Acts 10:28
Basis and scope: Direct New Testament treatment of food and defilement; this Christian synthesis is disputed by some traditions.

Read carefully: Christians disagree about continuing clean-and-unclean distinctions and the scope of Acts 15. Peter applies his vision explicitly to receiving people in Acts 10:28; that verse must not be reduced to a standalone menu rule.
What Transformed means · Browse transformed practices

Leviticus gives Israel detailed distinctions among land animals, water creatures, birds and swarming creatures. Christian application requires reading Jesus’ teaching about defilement, the Jerusalem council and Paul on food. Traditions differ on continuing dietary observance; the study must identify that disagreement rather than claim the Torah alone settles every Christian practice.

title: Ritual status during menstruation
paragraphs: Study 62: Ritual status during menstruation
Related indexed requirements: C0533, C0534, C0535, C0536. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Transformed — ritual status and access to God
Connection to Christ: Jesus receives the woman with bleeding, and Hebrews distinguishes ritual regulation from cleansing of conscience; this is a contextual Christian reading.
Christian response today: Approach God through Christ and treat menstruating people with dignity; do not equate a bodily process with moral guilt or reduced spiritual worth.
Saints Translation — Law: Leviticus 15:19–24 Christ and the apostles: Mark 5:25–34 · Hebrews 9:9–14
Ancient covenant practice: Leviticus sets temporary ritual-status and contact rules concerning menstruation within Israel’s sanctuary life.

Development in Christ and the apostles: Jesus receives and heals the woman with prolonged bleeding. Hebrews distinguishes bodily regulations from the cleansing of conscience and invites believers to approach God through Christ.
Saints Translation support: Mark 5:25–34 · Hebrews 9:9–14 · Hebrews 10:19–22
Basis and scope: Christian interpretation of Jesus’ healing and Hebrews’ teaching; the Gospel incident is not itself a repeal formula.
Read carefully: The woman’s prolonged bleeding is not identical to ordinary menstruation. The application draws on the wider covenant teaching; churches differ in some ritual disciplines.
What Transformed means · Browse transformed practices

Leviticus describes temporary ritual uncleanness and associated contact rules. Menstruation itself is not described as a moral fault. Ritual status in Israel’s sanctuary system should not be equated with a person’s dignity, spiritual worth or modern medical diagnosis. The Gospel’s account of the woman with bleeding provides an important complementary reading.

title: Discharges, skin conditions and ritual cleansing
paragraphs: Study 63: Discharges, skin conditions and ritual cleansing

Transformed — ritual cleansing and service with a clean conscience
Connection to Christ: Jesus’ healing and Hebrews’ sanctuary teaching illuminate the rites without identifying every examination or washing as a separate prophecy.
Christian response today: Care compassionately for people who are ill and seek holiness through Christ, keeping ritual status, moral conduct and medical care distinct.
Saints Translation — Law: Leviticus 13:1–8 · Leviticus 14:1–9 · Leviticus 15:1–18 Christ and the apostles: Mark 1:40–44 · Hebrews 9:9–14
Ancient covenant practice: Israel’s laws prescribe examinations, separation, washings and offerings concerning skin conditions and bodily discharges.

Development in Christ and the apostles: Jesus heals and restores people; in Mark 1 he also tells the healed man to present the Mosaic offering. Hebrews later interprets the bodily regulations through Christ’s cleansing of conscience.
Saints Translation support: Mark 1:40–44 · Hebrews 9:9–14 · Hebrews 10:19–22
Basis and scope: Christian interpretation of the wider sanctuary teaching; not a separate New Testament ruling on every washing.
Read carefully: Jesus’ healing must not be misquoted as an immediate cancellation of the priestly procedure he explicitly commands in that scene.
What Transformed means · Browse transformed practices

Calling the whole collection “hygiene” can obscure its sanctuary purpose and the difference between ritual impurity and disease. It is not a substitute for modern medical care. Jesus’ healing and Hebrews’ account of cleansing provide the Christian context.

title: Intercourse during menstrual impurity
paragraphs: Study 67: Intercourse during menstrual impurity
Related indexed requirements: C0589. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Connection to Christ: Hebrews and First Corinthians supply relevant context, but neither directly adjudicates every Christian application of this exact provision.
Christian response today: Practice mutual care and respect, distinguishing menstrual ritual status from personal moral worth.
Saints Translation — Law: Leviticus 18:19 · Leviticus 20:18 Christ and the apostles: Hebrews 9:9–14 · 1 Corinthians 7:3–5
Text and setting: Purity and sexual law
Torah: Leviticus 18:19 · Leviticus 20:18

The Torah specifically prohibits intercourse during menstrual impurity and gives an Israelite sanction. Christians differ over the continuing force of this provision. Neither menstruation nor ritual status makes a woman morally inferior. Discuss application within the wider biblical teaching on holiness, mutual care and the changed sanctuary order described in Hebrews.
Read with Christ and the apostles: Hebrews 9:9–14 · 1 Corinthians 7:3–5

title: Corpse contact and ritual cleansing
paragraphs: Study 105: Corpse contact and ritual cleansing

Related indexed requirements: C0895, C0896, C0897, C0898, C0899, C0900, C0901, C0902, C0903, C0904. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Transformed — outward purification and cleansing of conscience
Connection to Christ: Hebrews explicitly compares the rite’s outward cleansing with the cleansing of conscience through Christ.
Christian response today: Serve God through Christ with a cleansed conscience, and care reverently for the dying and dead without treating that care as moral guilt.
Saints Translation — Law: Numbers 19:11–22 Christ and the apostles: Hebrews 9:13–14
Ancient covenant practice: Contact with a corpse calls for the prescribed purification involving heifer ashes and water.
Development in Christ and the apostles: Hebrews explicitly compares the rite’s outward cleansing with Christ’s deeper cleansing of conscience for service to the living God.
Saints Translation support: Hebrews 9:13–14 · Hebrews 10:19–22
Basis and scope: Direct comparison made in Hebrews.
Read carefully: Fulfilled identifies the Christ-centered cleansing comparison; Transformed identifies its Christian application. Bodily care and ordinary precautions remain important.
What Transformed means · Browse transformed practices

Contact with a human corpse creates temporary ritual uncleanness under the specified purification procedure. This does not make burial or care for the dead morally wrong. Hebrews explicitly contrasts the cleansing associated with heifer ashes and the deeper cleansing of conscience through Christ.

title: Food prohibited to Israel
paragraphs: Study 127: Food prohibited to Israel
Related indexed requirements: C0467, C0468, C0469, C0470, C0471. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Transformed — dietary holiness and loving fellowship
Connection to Christ: Jesus and Paul address food and defilement; Christians interpret their relationship to Israel’s food distinctions differently.

Christian response today: Practice purity of heart and grateful eating, avoid idolatry, and protect fellowship and conscience rather than turning dietary choices into a measure of another person’s worth.
Saints Translation — Law: Deuteronomy 14:3–20 Christ and the apostles: Mark 7:14–23 · Romans 14:1–3
Ancient covenant practice: Deuteronomy lists the creatures Israel may and may not eat as a holy people.

Development in Christ and the apostles: Read with Leviticus 11, this study understands the practice through Jesus’ teaching on the heart and apostolic teaching on food, thanksgiving, conscience and fellowship.
Saints Translation support: Mark 7:18–23 · Romans 14:13–23 · 1 Timothy 4:3–5 · Acts 15:28–29
Basis and scope: Direct New Testament food teaching; application to Deuteronomy’s list remains disputed by some Christians.
Read carefully: Keep Acts 15’s explicit instructions alongside Paul. The Transformed mark expresses this study’s Christian reading without claiming that all churches agree on dietary observance.
What Transformed means · Browse transformed practices

title: An animal that dies on its own
paragraphs: Study 128: An animal that dies on its own
Related indexed requirements: C0238, C0672. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Transformed — food, covenant recipients and conscience
Connection to Christ: Acts and Romans supply Christian food guidance; the Torah’s different treatment of recipients must remain visible.
Christian response today: Eat responsibly and gratefully, care for other people’s conscience, and retain Acts 15’s instructions when considering particular foods.
Saints Translation — Law: Deuteronomy 14:21 Christ and the apostles: Acts 15:19–29 · Romans 14:1–3
Ancient covenant practice: Israel is forbidden to eat an animal that dies on its own; the text explicitly distinguishes Israel from other recipients.
Development in Christ and the apostles: The Christian application is considered through Jesus’ teaching about defilement, the council’s instructions and Paul’s concern for love and conscience.
Saints Translation support: Mark 7:18–23 · Acts 15:28–29 · Romans 14:13–23
Basis and scope: Christian application of wider food teaching, not a separate apostolic ruling on carrion.
Read carefully: A covenant interpretation does not make spoiled food safe or authorize giving harmful food to someone else. Blood and strangled-animal questions must not disappear behind this label.
What Transformed means · Browse transformed practices

Israel is forbidden to eat an animal that dies of itself; the verse permits giving it to a resident foreigner or selling it to a foreigner. That permission is not a command to give unsafe food to someone else. The explicit difference between recipients also limits sweeping claims that every Torah rule applies identically to every person.

title: Leviticus 3:1–17 · Peace or deliverance sacrifices; cattle, sheep and goats; blood, fat and altar portions
paragraphs: Passage group: Peace or deliverance sacrifices; cattle, sheep and goats; blood, fat and altar portions. Setting: Sacrificial law.
Requirements appearing in this passage: C0019, C0394, C0395, C0396, C0397, C0398, C0399, C1232. A mixed passage can link to more than one topic or classification.
Leviticus 3:1 — And if his gift unto the Lord is a sacrifice of deliverance, if he brings it from his cattle, whether male or female, he shall bring it unblemished before the Lord.

Leviticus 3:2 — And he shall lay his hands upon the head of the gift, and slaughter it beside the doors of the Tent of Testimony; and the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall pour the blood round about upon the altar of whole burnt offerings.
Leviticus 3:3 — And from the sacrifice of deliverance they shall bring an offering unto the Lord: the fat which covers the belly, and all the fat upon the belly,
Leviticus 3:4 — and the two kidneys, and the fat upon them which is by the thighs, and the lobe upon the liver, which he shall remove with the kidneys.

Leviticus 3:5 — And the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall offer them up upon the altar, upon the whole burnt offerings, upon the wood upon the fire upon the altar: an offering, a sweet savour unto the Lord.
Leviticus 3:6 — And if his gift is from the flock, as a sacrifice of deliverance unto the Lord, whether male or female, he shall bring it unblemished.
Leviticus 3:7 — If he brings a lamb as his gift, he shall bring it before the Lord,

Leviticus 3:8 — and lay his hands upon the head of his gift, and slaughter it beside the doors of the Tent of Testimony; and the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall pour the blood round about upon the altar.

title: Leviticus 11:1–47 · Land animals, water creatures, birds, insects, carcasses, contact, vessels, food and creeping creatures
paragraphs: Passage group: Land animals, water creatures, birds, insects, carcasses, contact, vessels, food and creeping creatures. Setting: Food and purity law.

Requirements appearing in this passage: C0213, C0465, C0467, C0468, C0469, C0470, C0471, C0472, C0473, C0474, C0475, C0476, C0477, C0478, C0479. A mixed passage can link to more than one topic or classification.
Leviticus 11:1 — And the Lord spoke unto Moses and Aaron, saying:
Leviticus 11:2 — Speak to the sons of Israel, saying: These are the animals you may eat among all the animals on the earth.
Leviticus 11:3 — Every animal among the livestock that divides the hoof, and cleaves its claws into two hoofs, and brings up the cud: these you may eat.

Leviticus 11:4 — Nevertheless, of these you shall not eat: among those that bring up the cud and those that divide the hoof and cleave the claws, the camel, because it brings up the cud, but does not divide the hoof; it is unclean unto you;
Leviticus 11:5 — and the hare, because it brings up the cud but does not divide the hoof; it is unclean for you;
Leviticus 11:6 — and the choirogryllios, because it brings up the cud but does not divide the hoof; it is unclean for you;
Leviticus 11:7 — and the pig, because it divides the hoof and has cleft hoof-claws but does not bring up the cud; it is unclean for you.
Leviticus 11:8 — You shall not eat their flesh or touch their carcasses; they are unclean for you.
Leviticus 11:9 — And these you may eat among all that are in the waters: whatever has fins and scales in the waters, in the seas and streams, you may eat.
Leviticus 11:10 — And whatever has neither fins nor scales in the water, in the seas and streams, among all that the waters bring forth and every living creature in the water, is an abomination.
Leviticus 11:11 — And they shall be abominations for you. You shall not eat their flesh, and you shall abhor their carcasses.
Leviticus 11:12 — And whatever among the things in the water has no fins and scales is an abomination for you.
Leviticus 11:13 — And these you shall abhor among the birds; they shall not be eaten, for they are an abomination: the eagle, the gryps, and the sea-eagle;
Leviticus 11:14 — and the vulture, the kite, and those like it;
Leviticus 11:15 — and the raven and those like it;
Leviticus 11:16 — and the ostrich, the owl, the gull and those like it, and the hawk and those like it;
Leviticus 11:17 — and the night-raven, the diving bird, and the ibis;
Leviticus 11:18 — and the purple waterbird, the pelican, and the swan;
Leviticus 11:19 — and the owl, the heron, the plover and those like it, the hoopoe, and the bat.
Leviticus 11:20 — And every winged creeping thing that walks on four is an abomination for you.
Leviticus 11:21 — But among the winged creeping things that walk on four, you may eat those that have legs above their feet for leaping on the earth.
Leviticus 11:22 — And these among them you may eat: the brouchos and those like it, the attakes and those like it, the locust and those like it, and the snake-fighter and those like it.
Leviticus 11:23 — Every winged creeping thing that has four feet is an abomination for you.
Leviticus 11:24 — And by these you shall become defiled: everyone who touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening,
Leviticus 11:25 — and whosoever carries any of their carcasses shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 11:26 — Every animal that divides the hoof and has cleft claws but does not chew the cud shall be unclean for you. Whosoever touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 11:27 — And among all wild animals that walk on four, whatever walks on its hands shall be unclean for you. Whosoever touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 11:28 — And whosoever carries their carcasses shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening. They are unclean for you.
Leviticus 11:29 — And these are unclean for you among the creeping things that creep on the earth: the weasel, the mouse, and the land crocodile;
Leviticus 11:30 — the shrew, the chameleon, the spotted lizard, the lizard, and the mole.
Leviticus 11:31 — These are unclean for you among all the creeping things on the earth. Whosoever touches them when they are dead shall be unclean until evening.

Leviticus 11:32 — And anything on which one of them falls when dead shall become unclean: any wooden utensil, garment, skin, or sack, any article used for work. It shall be dipped in water and remain unclean until evening; then it shall be clean.
Leviticus 11:33 — And if one of them falls inside any earthenware vessel, everything in it shall become unclean, and the vessel shall be shattered.
Leviticus 11:34 — And any food that may be eaten, on which water comes, shall become unclean, and any drink that may be drunk in any vessel shall become unclean.
Leviticus 11:35 — And anything on which any of their carcasses falls shall become unclean. Ovens and pot-stands shall be demolished; these are unclean and shall be unclean for you.
Leviticus 11:36 — But springs of water, a cistern, and a gathering of water shall remain clean; whosoever touches their carcasses shall be unclean.
Leviticus 11:37 — If any of their carcasses falls on seed intended for sowing, it remains clean.
Leviticus 11:38 — But if water is poured on any seed and any of their carcasses falls on it, it is unclean for you.
Leviticus 11:39 — If an animal that you may eat dies, whosoever touches its carcass shall be unclean until evening.

Leviticus 11:40 — And whosoever eats from these carcasses shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening. Whosoever carries any of their carcasses shall wash his garments, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 11:41 — And every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth shall be an abomination for you; it shall not be eaten.

Leviticus 11:42 — And whatever moves on its belly, whatever walks on four continually, whatever has many feet among all the creeping things that creep upon the earth, you shall not eat, for it is an abomination for you.

Leviticus 11:43 — And you shall in no wise make your souls abominable through any creeping things that creep upon the earth; neither shall you be defiled through them, nor shall you be unclean through them;

Leviticus 11:44 — for I am the Lord your God; and you shall be sanctified and you shall be holy, for I am holy, the Lord your God. And you shall not defile your souls through any creeping things that move upon the earth;
Leviticus 11:45 — for I am the Lord who brought you up out of the land of Egypt to be your God; and you shall be holy, for I am holy, the Lord.
Leviticus 11:46 — This is the law concerning animals, birds, every creature that moves in the water, and every creature that creeps upon the earth,
Leviticus 11:47 — to distinguish between the unclean and the clean, and between the living creatures that are eaten and the living creatures that are not eaten.

to distinguish between the unclean and the clean, and between the living creatures that are eaten and the living creatures that are not eaten.

title: Leviticus 12:1–8 · Childbirth, eighth-day circumcision, purification periods and means-based offerings
paragraphs: Passage group: Childbirth, eighth-day circumcision, purification periods and means-based offerings. Setting: Purity law.
Requirements appearing in this passage: C0036, C0480, C0481, C0482, C0483. A mixed passage can link to more than one topic or classification.
Leviticus 12:1 — And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:

Leviticus 12:2 — Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: If a woman receives seed and bears a male, she shall be unclean seven days; she shall be unclean as in the days of separation for her menstrual discharge.
Leviticus 12:3 — And on the eighth day he shall circumcise the flesh of his foreskin.
Leviticus 12:4 — And she shall remain thirty-three days in her unclean blood. She shall touch nothing holy and shall not enter the sanctuary until the days of her purification are completed.
Leviticus 12:5 — But if she bears a female, she shall be unclean twice seven days according to her menstrual discharge; and she shall remain sixty-six days in her unclean blood.

Leviticus 12:6 — And when the days of her purification for a son or daughter are completed, she shall bring unto the priest at the door of the Tent of Testimony an unblemished year-old lamb for a whole burnt offering and a young pigeon or turtledove for sin.
Leviticus 12:7 — And the priest shall present it before the Lord, and make atonement for her, and cleanse her from the fountain of her blood. This is the law for her that bears a male or a female.

Leviticus 12:8 — If her hand cannot provide enough for a lamb, she shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a whole burnt offering and one for sin. The priest shall make atonement for her, and she shall be cleansed.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:

Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: If a woman receives seed and bears a male, she shall be unclean seven days; she shall be unclean as in the days of separation for her menstrual discharge.
And on the eighth day he shall circumcise the flesh of his foreskin.
And she shall remain thirty-three days in her unclean blood. She shall touch nothing holy and shall not enter the sanctuary until the days of her purification are completed.
But if she bears a female, she shall be unclean twice seven days according to her menstrual discharge; and she shall remain sixty-six days in her unclean blood.

And when the days of her purification for a son or daughter are completed, she shall bring unto the priest at the door of the Tent of Testimony an unblemished year-old lamb for a whole burnt offering and a young pigeon or turtledove for sin.
And the priest shall present it before the Lord, and make atonement for her, and cleanse her from the fountain of her blood. This is the law for her that bears a male or a female.

If her hand cannot provide enough for a lamb, she shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a whole burnt offering and one for sin. The priest shall make atonement for her, and she shall be cleansed.

title: Leviticus 13:1–59 · Priestly inspection, quarantine, skin and hair lesions, burns, isolation, clothing and leather
paragraphs: Passage group: Priestly inspection, quarantine, skin and hair lesions, burns, isolation, clothing and leather. Setting: Purity law.

Requirements appearing in this passage: C0484, C0485, C0486, C0487, C0488, C0489, C0490, C0491, C0492, C0493, C0494, C0495, C0496, C0497, C0498, C0499, C0500. A mixed passage can link to more than one topic or classification.
Leviticus 13:1 — And the Lord spoke unto Moses and Aaron, saying:

Leviticus 13:2 — If anyone has on the skin of his body a bright scar-like mark, and it becomes a lesion of leprosy on his skin, he shall be brought unto Aaron the priest or to one of his sons, the priests.

Leviticus 13:3 — And the priest shall examine the lesion on the skin of his body. If the hair in the lesion has turned white and the lesion appears lower than the skin of his body, it is a lesion of leprosy. The priest shall examine him and declare him unclean.

Leviticus 13:4 — If the bright spot on his skin is white but does not appear lower than the skin, and its hair has not turned white, but it is faint, the priest shall isolate the lesion for seven days.

Leviticus 13:5 — And the priest shall examine the lesion on the seventh day; and, behold, if the lesion remains before him, and the lesion has not shifted in the skin, the priest shall isolate him for a second seven days.

Leviticus 13:6 — And the priest shall examine him on the seventh day a second time; and, behold, if the lesion is faint, and the lesion has not shifted in the skin, the priest shall declare him clean, for it is a mark; and having washed his garments, he shall be clean.
Leviticus 13:7 — But if the mark changes and shifts in the skin after the priest has examined him for cleansing, he shall appear before the priest a second time,
Leviticus 13:8 — and the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the mark has shifted in the skin, the priest shall declare him unclean; it is leprosy.
Leviticus 13:9 — And when a lesion of leprosy occurs in anyone, he shall come unto the priest.
Leviticus 13:10 — And the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if there is a white scar in the skin, and it has turned the hair white, and there is some sound living flesh in the scar,
Leviticus 13:11 — it is longstanding leprosy on the skin of his body. The priest shall declare him unclean and isolate him, for he is unclean.
Leviticus 13:12 — But if the leprosy breaks out abundantly in the skin, and the leprosy covers all the skin of the lesion from head to foot, throughout the whole view of the priest,

Leviticus 13:13 — the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the leprosy has covered all the skin of his body, the priest shall declare him clean as to the lesion, because it has all turned white; it is clean.
Leviticus 13:14 — And on whatever day living skin appears on him, he shall be defiled.
Leviticus 13:15 — And the priest shall examine the sound skin, and the sound skin shall make him unclean, because it is unclean; it is leprosy.
Leviticus 13:16 — But if the sound skin is restored and turns white, he shall come unto the priest,
Leviticus 13:17 — and the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the lesion has turned white, the priest shall declare the lesion clean; he is clean.
Leviticus 13:18 — And if an ulcer occurs on the skin of the body and heals,
Leviticus 13:19 — and a white scar or a whitish or fiery-red bright spot appears in the place of the ulcer, he shall appear before the priest.

Leviticus 13:20 — And the priest shall examine it; and, behold, if its appearance is lower than the skin, and its hair has turned white, the priest shall declare him unclean; it is leprosy which has blossomed in the ulcer.
Leviticus 13:21 — But if the priest examines it, and, behold, there is no white hair in it, and it is not lower than the skin of the body, but is faint, the priest shall isolate him seven days.
Leviticus 13:22 — If it spreads in the skin, the priest shall declare him unclean; it is a lesion of leprosy that has blossomed in the ulcer.
Leviticus 13:23 — But if the bright spot stays in its place and does not spread, it is the scar of the ulcer; the priest shall declare him clean.
Leviticus 13:24 — And if the skin of the body has a burn from fire, and the healed area of the burn on his skin becomes a shining, bright, whitish-red or completely white spot,

Leviticus 13:25 — the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the hair in the shining spot has turned white, and its appearance is lower than the skin, it is leprosy which has blossomed in the burn; and the priest shall declare him unclean; it is a lesion of leprosy.
Leviticus 13:26 — But if the priest examines it, and, behold, there is no white hair in the shining spot, and it is not lower than the skin, but is faint, the priest shall isolate him seven days.

Leviticus 13:27 — And the priest shall examine him on the seventh day; but if it has indeed spread in the skin, the priest shall declare him unclean; it is a lesion of leprosy which has blossomed in the ulcer.
Leviticus 13:28 — But if the shining spot stays in its place, has not spread in the skin, and is faint, it is the scar of the burn. The priest shall declare him clean, for it is the mark of the burn.
Leviticus 13:29 — And if a man or woman has a lesion of leprosy on the head or beard,

Leviticus 13:30 — the priest shall examine the lesion; and, behold, if its appearance is more hollow than the skin, and there is fine yellowish hair in it, the priest shall declare him unclean; it is a broken patch, leprosy of the head or leprosy of the beard.

Leviticus 13:31 — And if the priest examines the lesion of the broken patch, and, behold, its appearance is not more hollow than the skin, and there is no yellowish hair in it, the priest shall isolate the lesion of the broken patch seven days.

Leviticus 13:32 — And the priest shall examine the lesion on the seventh day; and, behold, if the broken patch has not spread, and there is no yellowish hair in it, and the appearance of the broken patch is not hollow below the skin,
Leviticus 13:33 — then the skin shall be shaved, but the broken patch shall not be shaved. The priest shall isolate the broken patch for a second seven days.

Leviticus 13:34 — And the priest shall examine the broken patch on the seventh day; and, behold, if the broken patch has not spread in the skin after he was shaved, and its appearance is not hollow below the skin, the priest shall declare him clean; and having washed his garments, he shall be clean.
Leviticus 13:35 — But if the broken patch has indeed spread in the skin after he has been cleansed,
Leviticus 13:36 — the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the broken patch has spread in the skin, the priest shall not inspect for yellow hair, for he is unclean.
Leviticus 13:37 — But if before him the broken patch has remained in place and black hair has grown in it, the broken patch has healed. He is clean, and the priest shall declare him clean.
Leviticus 13:38 — And if a man or woman has shining, whitish patches on the skin of the body,

Leviticus 13:39 — the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if there are shining, whitish patches on the skin of his body, it is a white eruption; he is clean. It blossoms in the skin of his body; he is clean.
Leviticus 13:40 — If anyone loses the hair of his head, he is bald; he is clean.
Leviticus 13:41 — If he loses the hair at the front of his head, he is bald at the forehead; he is clean.
Leviticus 13:42 — But if there is a white or fiery-red lesion on his bald head or bald forehead, it is leprosy on his bald head or bald forehead.

Leviticus 13:43 — And the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the appearance of the lesion on his bald head or his bald forehead is white tinged with red, like the appearance of leprosy on the skin of his body,
Leviticus 13:44 — he is a man with leprosy; the priest shall surely declare him unclean; his lesion is upon his head.
Leviticus 13:45 — And he that has leprosy, in whom the lesion is, shall have his garments loosened and his head uncovered, and shall put a covering about his mouth, and shall be called unclean;
Leviticus 13:46 — all the days in which the lesion is upon him, being unclean, he shall be unclean; he shall dwell apart; his dwelling shall be outside the camp.
Leviticus 13:47 — And if a garment has a lesion of leprosy, whether a woollen garment or a garment of coarse flax,
Leviticus 13:48 — or in warp or weft, or in linen or wool, or in leather or any worked leather,
Leviticus 13:49 — and the lesion in the leather, garment, warp, weft, or any worked leather article is greenish or fiery red, it is a lesion of leprosy, and he shall show it unto the priest.
Leviticus 13:50 — And the priest shall examine the lesion, and the priest shall isolate the lesion for seven days.

Leviticus 13:51 — And on the seventh day the priest shall examine the lesion. If it has spread in the garment, warp, weft, or leather, in whatever use is made of leather, the lesion is persistent leprosy; it is unclean.
Leviticus 13:52 — He shall burn up the garment, the warp or weft in wool or linen, or any leather article that has the lesion, for it is persistent leprosy; it shall be burned up with fire.
Leviticus 13:53 — But if the priest examines it and the lesion has not spread in the garment, warp, weft, or any leather article,
Leviticus 13:54 — then the priest shall give instructions, and he shall wash the article with the lesion; the priest shall isolate the lesion for a second seven days.

Leviticus 13:55 — And after it has been washed, the priest shall examine the lesion. If it has not changed its appearance and has not spread, it is unclean; it shall be burned up with fire. It has become established in the garment, warp, or weft.
Leviticus 13:56 — And if the priest examines it and the lesion is faint after washing, he shall tear it out of the garment, leather, warp, or weft.
Leviticus 13:57 — If it appears again in the garment, warp, weft, or any leather article, it is blossoming leprosy; the affected article shall be burned up with fire.
Leviticus 13:58 — And a garment, warp, weft, or any leather article that is washed, from which the lesion departs, shall be washed a second time and be clean.
Leviticus 13:59 — This is the law of a lesion of leprosy in a garment of wool or coarse flax, or in warp or weft, or in any leather article, for declaring it clean or unclean.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke unto Moses and Aaron, saying:
If anyone has on the skin of his body a bright scar-like mark, and it becomes a lesion of leprosy on his skin, he shall be brought unto Aaron the priest or to one of his sons, the priests.

And the priest shall examine the lesion on the skin of his body. If the hair in the lesion has turned white and the lesion appears lower than the skin of his body, it is a lesion of leprosy. The priest shall examine him and declare him unclean.
If the bright spot on his skin is white but does not appear lower than the skin, and its hair has not turned white, but it is faint, the priest shall isolate the lesion for seven days.

And the priest shall examine the lesion on the seventh day; and, behold, if the lesion remains before him, and the lesion has not shifted in the skin, the priest shall isolate him for a second seven days.

And the priest shall examine him on the seventh day a second time; and, behold, if the lesion is faint, and the lesion has not shifted in the skin, the priest shall declare him clean, for it is a mark; and having washed his garments, he shall be clean.
But if the mark changes and shifts in the skin after the priest has examined him for cleansing, he shall appear before the priest a second time,
and the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the mark has shifted in the skin, the priest shall declare him unclean; it is leprosy.
And when a lesion of leprosy occurs in anyone, he shall come unto the priest.
And the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if there is a white scar in the skin, and it has turned the hair white, and there is some sound living flesh in the scar,
it is longstanding leprosy on the skin of his body. The priest shall declare him unclean and isolate him, for he is unclean.
But if the leprosy breaks out abundantly in the skin, and the leprosy covers all the skin of the lesion from head to foot, throughout the whole view of the priest,
the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the leprosy has covered all the skin of his body, the priest shall declare him clean as to the lesion, because it has all turned white; it is clean.
And on whatever day living skin appears on him, he shall be defiled.
And the priest shall examine the sound skin, and the sound skin shall make him unclean, because it is unclean; it is leprosy.
But if the sound skin is restored and turns white, he shall come unto the priest,
and the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the lesion has turned white, the priest shall declare the lesion clean; he is clean.
And if an ulcer occurs on the skin of the body and heals,
and a white scar or a whitish or fiery-red bright spot appears in the place of the ulcer, he shall appear before the priest.

And the priest shall examine it; and, behold, if its appearance is lower than the skin, and its hair has turned white, the priest shall declare him unclean; it is leprosy which has blossomed in the ulcer.
But if the priest examines it, and, behold, there is no white hair in it, and it is not lower than the skin of the body, but is faint, the priest shall isolate him seven days.
If it spreads in the skin, the priest shall declare him unclean; it is a lesion of leprosy that has blossomed in the ulcer.
But if the bright spot stays in its place and does not spread, it is the scar of the ulcer; the priest shall declare him clean.
And if the skin of the body has a burn from fire, and the healed area of the burn on his skin becomes a shining, bright, whitish-red or completely white spot,

the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the hair in the shining spot has turned white, and its appearance is lower than the skin, it is leprosy which has blossomed in the burn; and the priest shall declare him unclean; it is a lesion of leprosy.
But if the priest examines it, and, behold, there is no white hair in the shining spot, and it is not lower than the skin, but is faint, the priest shall isolate him seven days.
And the priest shall examine him on the seventh day; but if it has indeed spread in the skin, the priest shall declare him unclean; it is a lesion of leprosy which has blossomed in the ulcer.
But if the shining spot stays in its place, has not spread in the skin, and is faint, it is the scar of the burn. The priest shall declare him clean, for it is the mark of the burn.
And if a man or woman has a lesion of leprosy on the head or beard,

the priest shall examine the lesion; and, behold, if its appearance is more hollow than the skin, and there is fine yellowish hair in it, the priest shall declare him unclean; it is a broken patch, leprosy of the head or leprosy of the beard.

And if the priest examines the lesion of the broken patch, and, behold, its appearance is not more hollow than the skin, and there is no yellowish hair in it, the priest shall isolate the lesion of the broken patch seven days.

And the priest shall examine the lesion on the seventh day; and, behold, if the broken patch has not spread, and there is no yellowish hair in it, and the appearance of the broken patch is not hollow below the skin,
then the skin shall be shaved, but the broken patch shall not be shaved. The priest shall isolate the broken patch for a second seven days.

And the priest shall examine the broken patch on the seventh day; and, behold, if the broken patch has not spread in the skin after he was shaved, and its appearance is not hollow below the skin, the priest shall declare him clean; and having washed his garments, he shall be clean.
But if the broken patch has indeed spread in the skin after he has been cleansed,
the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the broken patch has spread in the skin, the priest shall not inspect for yellow hair, for he is unclean.
But if before him the broken patch has remained in place and black hair has grown in it, the broken patch has healed. He is clean, and the priest shall declare him clean.
And if a man or woman has shining, whitish patches on the skin of the body,
the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if there are shining, whitish patches on the skin of his body, it is a white eruption; he is clean. It blossoms in the skin of his body; he is clean.
If anyone loses the hair of his head, he is bald; he is clean.
If he loses the hair at the front of his head, he is bald at the forehead; he is clean.
But if there is a white or fiery-red lesion on his bald head or bald forehead, it is leprosy on his bald head or bald forehead.
And the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the appearance of the lesion on his bald head or his bald forehead is white tinged with red, like the appearance of leprosy on the skin of his body,
he is a man with leprosy; the priest shall surely declare him unclean; his lesion is upon his head.
And he that has leprosy, in whom the lesion is, shall have his garments loosened and his head uncovered, and shall put a covering about his mouth, and shall be called unclean;
all the days in which the lesion is upon him, being unclean, he shall be unclean; he shall dwell apart; his dwelling shall be outside the camp.
And if a garment has a lesion of leprosy, whether a woollen garment or a garment of coarse flax,
or in warp or weft, or in linen or wool, or in leather or any worked leather,
and the lesion in the leather, garment, warp, weft, or any worked leather article is greenish or fiery red, it is a lesion of leprosy, and he shall show it unto the priest.
And the priest shall examine the lesion, and the priest shall isolate the lesion for seven days.

And on the seventh day the priest shall examine the lesion. If it has spread in the garment, warp, weft, or leather, in whatever use is made of leather, the lesion is persistent leprosy; it is unclean.
He shall burn up the garment, the warp or weft in wool or linen, or any leather article that has the lesion, for it is persistent leprosy; it shall be burned up with fire.
But if the priest examines it and the lesion has not spread in the garment, warp, weft, or any leather article,
then the priest shall give instructions, and he shall wash the article with the lesion; the priest shall isolate the lesion for a second seven days.

And after it has been washed, the priest shall examine the lesion. If it has not changed its appearance and has not spread, it is unclean; it shall be burned up with fire. It has become established in the garment, warp, or weft.
And if the priest examines it and the lesion is faint after washing, he shall tear it out of the garment, leather, warp, or weft.
If it appears again in the garment, warp, weft, or any leather article, it is blossoming leprosy; the affected article shall be burned up with fire.
And a garment, warp, weft, or any leather article that is washed, from which the lesion departs, shall be washed a second time and be clean.
This is the law of a lesion of leprosy in a garment of wool or coarse flax, or in warp or weft, or in any leather article, for declaring it clean or unclean.

title: Leviticus 14:1–57 · Cleansing the afflicted person, birds, washing, shaving, blood and oil, offerings, poverty provision and affected houses
paragraphs: Passage group: Cleansing the afflicted person, birds, washing, shaving, blood and oil, offerings, poverty provision and affected houses. Setting: Purity law.

Requirements appearing in this passage: C0501, C0502, C0503, C0504, C0505, C0506, C0507, C0508, C0509, C0510, C0511, C0512, C0513, C0514, C0515, C0516, C0517, C0518, C0519, C0520, C0521, C0522, C0523, C0524, C0525, C0526, C0527, C0528, C0529, C0530, C0531, C0532, C1236, C1237, C1238. A mixed passage can link to more than one topic or classification.
Leviticus 14:1 — And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Leviticus 14:2 — This is the law of the person with leprosy on the day he is cleansed: he shall be brought unto the priest,
Leviticus 14:3 — and the priest shall go outside the camp, and the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the lesion of leprosy has healed in him that had leprosy,
Leviticus 14:4 — then the priest shall give orders, and they shall take two living clean birds, cedarwood, spun scarlet thread, and hyssop for the person who has been cleansed.
Leviticus 14:5 — And the priest shall give orders, and they shall slaughter one bird into an earthenware vessel over living water.
Leviticus 14:6 — And he shall take the living bird, cedarwood, spun scarlet thread, and hyssop, and dip them and the living bird in the blood of the bird slaughtered over the living water.
Leviticus 14:7 — And he shall sprinkle the person cleansed from leprosy seven times, and he shall be clean. He shall release the living bird into the plain.

Leviticus 14:8 — And the person who has been cleansed shall wash his garments, shave off all his hair, bathe in water, and be clean. Afterward he shall enter the camp, but he shall remain outside his house for seven days.

Leviticus 14:9 — And on the seventh day he shall shave off all his hair: his head, his beard, and his eyebrows; he shall shave off all his hair. He shall wash his garments, bathe his body in water, and be clean.
Leviticus 14:10 — And on the eighth day he shall take two unblemished year-old lambs, one unblemished year-old sheep, three tenths of fine flour mixed with oil for a sacrifice, and one kotyle of oil,
Leviticus 14:11 — and the priest who performs the cleansing shall present the person being cleansed and these things before the Lord at the entrance of the Tent of Testimony.
Leviticus 14:12 — And the priest shall take one lamb and present it for the guilt offering, with the kotyle of oil, and separate it as a separated portion before the Lord.

Leviticus 14:13 — And they shall slaughter the lamb in a holy place where they slaughter the whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin. The offering for sin is like the guilt offering: it belongs unto the priest; it is most holy.

Leviticus 14:14 — And the priest shall take some of the guilt offering’s blood and put it on the right earlobe of the person being cleansed, the extremity of his right hand, and the extremity of his right foot.
Leviticus 14:15 — And the priest shall take some of the kotyle of oil and pour it upon the priest’s left hand,
Leviticus 14:16 — and dip his right finger into the oil on his left hand and sprinkle with his finger seven times before the Lord.

Leviticus 14:17 — The priest shall put the oil remaining in his hand on the right earlobe of the person being cleansed, the extremity of his right hand, and the extremity of his right foot, upon the place of the blood of the guilt offering.
Leviticus 14:18 — The priest shall put the remaining oil in his hand on the head of the person who has been cleansed. The priest shall make atonement for him before the Lord.

Leviticus 14:19 — And the priest shall prepare the offering for sin and make atonement for the unclean person being cleansed from his sin. Afterward the priest shall slaughter the whole burnt offering.
Leviticus 14:20 — And the priest shall offer up the whole burnt offering and sacrifice on the altar before the Lord. The priest shall make atonement for him, and he shall be cleansed.

Leviticus 14:21 — If he is poor and his hand cannot provide, he shall take one lamb for his offence as a portion set apart, to make atonement for him, a tenth of fine flour mixed with oil for a sacrifice, and one kotyle of oil,
Leviticus 14:22 — and two turtledoves or two young pigeons, whichever his hand can provide, one for sin and one for a whole burnt offering.
Leviticus 14:23 — And on the eighth day he shall bring them for his cleansing unto the priest, at the entrance of the Tent of Testimony before the Lord.
Leviticus 14:24 — And the priest shall take the lamb of the guilt offering and the kotyle of oil, and place them as a presentation before the Lord.

Leviticus 14:25 — And he shall slaughter the lamb of the guilt offering. The priest shall take some of its blood and put it on the right earlobe of the person being cleansed, the extremity of his right hand, and the extremity of his right foot.
Leviticus 14:26 — And the priest shall pour some of the oil upon the priest’s left hand,
Leviticus 14:27 — and with his right finger the priest shall sprinkle some of the oil in his left hand seven times before the Lord.

Leviticus 14:28 — And the priest shall put some of the oil on his hand on the right earlobe of the person being cleansed, the extremity of his right hand, and the extremity of his right foot, on the place of the guilt offering’s blood.
Leviticus 14:29 — He shall put the remaining oil in the priest’s hand on the head of the person who has been cleansed, and the priest shall make atonement for him before the Lord.
Leviticus 14:30 — And he shall prepare one of the turtledoves or young pigeons, as his hand can provide,
Leviticus 14:31 — one for sin and one for a whole burnt offering, together with the sacrifice. The priest shall make atonement before the Lord for the person being cleansed.
Leviticus 14:32 — This is the law for the one with a lesion of leprosy and for the one whose hand cannot provide for his cleansing.
Leviticus 14:33 — And the Lord spoke unto Moses and Aaron, saying:
Leviticus 14:34 — When you enter the land of the Canaanites, which I give unto you for a possession, and I put a lesion of leprosy in the houses of the land of your possession,
Leviticus 14:35 — then the owner of the house shall come and tell the priest, saying: Something like a lesion has appeared to me in the house.

Leviticus 14:36 — And the priest shall command that the house be emptied before he enters to examine the lesion, so that nothing in the house becomes unclean. Afterward the priest shall enter to examine the house.
Leviticus 14:37 — And he shall examine the lesion in the walls of the house, greenish or fiery-red hollows whose appearance is lower than the walls,
Leviticus 14:38 — and the priest shall leave the house, go to its door, and isolate the house for seven days.
Leviticus 14:39 — And the priest shall return on the seventh day, and examine the house; and, behold, if the lesion has not spread in the walls of the house,
Leviticus 14:40 — then the priest shall command them to remove the stones that have the lesion and throw them outside the city into an unclean place.
Leviticus 14:41 — And they shall scrape the house all around inside and pour the dust outside the city into an unclean place.
Leviticus 14:42 — And they shall take other scraped stones and put them in place of those stones. They shall take other earth and plaster the house.
Leviticus 14:43 — If a lesion comes again and springs up in the house after the stones have been removed and the house scraped and plastered,
Leviticus 14:44 — then the priest shall enter and examine it. If the lesion has spread in the house, it is persistent leprosy in the house; it is unclean.
Leviticus 14:45 — And they shall demolish the house, and carry its timbers, its stones, and all its dust outside the city into an unclean place.
Leviticus 14:46 — And whosoever enters the house during any of the days it is isolated shall be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 14:47 — And whosoever sleeps in the house shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening, and whosoever eats in the house shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening.

Leviticus 14:48 — But if the priest comes and enters and examines it, and, behold, the lesion has not spread at all in the house after the house was plastered, the priest shall declare the house clean, for the lesion has healed.

Leviticus 14:50 — And he shall slaughter one bird into an earthenware vessel over living water,
Leviticus 14:51 — and take the cedarwood, spun scarlet thread, hyssop, and living bird, dip it in the blood of the bird slaughtered over living water, and sprinkle the house with them seven times,
Leviticus 14:52 — and he shall purify the house with the bird’s blood, the living water, the living bird, the cedarwood, the hyssop, and the spun scarlet thread.
Leviticus 14:53 — And he shall release the living bird outside the city into the plain, make atonement for the house, and it shall be clean.
Leviticus 14:54 — This is the law concerning every lesion of leprosy and every broken patch,
Leviticus 14:55 — and for leprosy of a garment or house,
Leviticus 14:56 — and for a scar, a mark, or a shining spot,
Leviticus 14:57 — and to explain on what day it is unclean and on what day it shall be cleansed. This is the law of leprosy.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
This is the law of the person with leprosy on the day he is cleansed: he shall be brought unto the priest,
and the priest shall go outside the camp, and the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the lesion of leprosy has healed in him that had leprosy,
then the priest shall give orders, and they shall take two living clean birds, cedarwood, spun scarlet thread, and hyssop for the person who has been cleansed.
And the priest shall give orders, and they shall slaughter one bird into an earthenware vessel over living water.
And he shall take the living bird, cedarwood, spun scarlet thread, and hyssop, and dip them and the living bird in the blood of the bird slaughtered over the living water.
And he shall sprinkle the person cleansed from leprosy seven times, and he shall be clean. He shall release the living bird into the plain.

And the person who has been cleansed shall wash his garments, shave off all his hair, bathe in water, and be clean. Afterward he shall enter the camp, but he shall remain outside his house for seven days.
And on the seventh day he shall shave off all his hair: his head, his beard, and his eyebrows; he shall shave off all his hair. He shall wash his garments, bathe his body in water, and be clean.
And on the eighth day he shall take two unblemished year-old lambs, one unblemished year-old sheep, three tenths of fine flour mixed with oil for a sacrifice, and one kotyle of oil,
and the priest who performs the cleansing shall present the person being cleansed and these things before the Lord at the entrance of the Tent of Testimony.
And the priest shall take one lamb and present it for the guilt offering, with the kotyle of oil, and separate it as a separated portion before the Lord.

And they shall slaughter the lamb in a holy place where they slaughter the whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin. The offering for sin is like the guilt offering: it belongs unto the priest; it is most holy.
And the priest shall take some of the guilt offering’s blood and put it on the right earlobe of the person being cleansed, the extremity of his right hand, and the extremity of his right foot.
And the priest shall take some of the kotyle of oil and pour it upon the priest’s left hand,
and dip his right finger into the oil on his left hand and sprinkle with his finger seven times before the Lord.

The priest shall put the oil remaining in his hand on the right earlobe of the person being cleansed, the extremity of his right hand, and the extremity of his right foot, upon the place of the blood of the guilt offering.
The priest shall put the remaining oil in his hand on the head of the person who has been cleansed. The priest shall make atonement for him before the Lord.
And the priest shall prepare the offering for sin and make atonement for the unclean person being cleansed from his sin. Afterward the priest shall slaughter the whole burnt offering.
And the priest shall offer up the whole burnt offering and sacrifice on the altar before the Lord. The priest shall make atonement for him, and he shall be cleansed.

If he is poor and his hand cannot provide, he shall take one lamb for his offence as a portion set apart, to make atonement for him, a tenth of fine flour mixed with oil for a sacrifice, and one kotyle of oil,
and two turtledoves or two young pigeons, whichever his hand can provide, one for sin and one for a whole burnt offering.
And on the eighth day he shall bring them for his cleansing unto the priest, at the entrance of the Tent of Testimony before the Lord.
And the priest shall take the lamb of the guilt offering and the kotyle of oil, and place them as a presentation before the Lord.

And he shall slaughter the lamb of the guilt offering. The priest shall take some of its blood and put it on the right earlobe of the person being cleansed, the extremity of his right hand, and the extremity of his right foot.
And the priest shall pour some of the oil upon the priest’s left hand,
and with his right finger the priest shall sprinkle some of the oil in his left hand seven times before the Lord.

And the priest shall put some of the oil on his hand on the right earlobe of the person being cleansed, the extremity of his right hand, and the extremity of his right foot, on the place of the guilt offering’s blood.
He shall put the remaining oil in the priest’s hand on the head of the person who has been cleansed, and the priest shall make atonement for him before the Lord.
And he shall prepare one of the turtledoves or young pigeons, as his hand can provide,
one for sin and one for a whole burnt offering, together with the sacrifice. The priest shall make atonement before the Lord for the person being cleansed.
This is the law for the one with a lesion of leprosy and for the one whose hand cannot provide for his cleansing.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses and Aaron, saying:
When you enter the land of the Canaanites, which I give unto you for a possession, and I put a lesion of leprosy in the houses of the land of your possession,
then the owner of the house shall come and tell the priest, saying: Something like a lesion has appeared to me in the house.
And the priest shall command that the house be emptied before he enters to examine the lesion, so that nothing in the house becomes unclean. Afterward the priest shall enter to examine the house.
And he shall examine the lesion in the walls of the house, greenish or fiery-red hollows whose appearance is lower than the walls,
and the priest shall leave the house, go to its door, and isolate the house for seven days.
And the priest shall return on the seventh day, and examine the house; and, behold, if the lesion has not spread in the walls of the house,
then the priest shall command them to remove the stones that have the lesion and throw them outside the city into an unclean place.
And they shall scrape the house all around inside and pour the dust outside the city into an unclean place.
And they shall take other scraped stones and put them in place of those stones. They shall take other earth and plaster the house.
If a lesion comes again and springs up in the house after the stones have been removed and the house scraped and plastered,
then the priest shall enter and examine it. If the lesion has spread in the house, it is persistent leprosy in the house; it is unclean.
And they shall demolish the house, and carry its timbers, its stones, and all its dust outside the city into an unclean place.
And whosoever enters the house during any of the days it is isolated shall be unclean until evening.
And whosoever sleeps in the house shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening, and whosoever eats in the house shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening.

But if the priest comes and enters and examines it, and, behold, the lesion has not spread at all in the house after the house was plastered, the priest shall declare the house clean, for the lesion has healed.
And to purify the house he shall take two living clean birds, cedarwood, spun scarlet thread, and hyssop.
And he shall slaughter one bird into an earthenware vessel over living water,
and take the cedarwood, spun scarlet thread, hyssop, and living bird, dip it in the blood of the bird slaughtered over living water, and sprinkle the house with them seven times,
and he shall purify the house with the bird’s blood, the living water, the living bird, the cedarwood, the hyssop, and the spun scarlet thread.
And he shall release the living bird outside the city into the plain, make atonement for the house, and it shall be clean.
This is the law concerning every lesion of leprosy and every broken patch,
and for leprosy of a garment or house,
and for a scar, a mark, or a shining spot,
and to explain on what day it is unclean and on what day it shall be cleansed. This is the law of leprosy.

title: Leviticus 15:1–33 · Male and female discharges, bodily contact, bedding, washing, waiting periods, offerings and sanctuary protection
paragraphs: Passage group: Male and female discharges, bodily contact, bedding, washing, waiting periods, offerings and sanctuary protection. Setting: Purity law.

Leviticus 15:1 — And the Lord spoke unto Moses and Aaron, saying:
Leviticus 15:2 — Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: If any man has a flow from his body, his flow is unclean.

Leviticus 15:3 — And this is the law of his uncleanness: discharging seed from his body through the flow by which his body has become stopped up, this is his uncleanness in him; all the days of the flow of his body, in which his body has become stopped up through the flow, are his uncleanness.
Leviticus 15:4 — Every bed on which the man with a seminal discharge lies is unclean, and every article on which the man with a seminal discharge sits shall be unclean.
Leviticus 15:5 — And whosoever touches his bed shall wash his garments, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:6 — And whosoever sits on an article on which the man with a seminal discharge has sat shall wash his garments, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:7 — And whosoever touches the skin of the man with a seminal discharge shall wash his garments, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:8 — If the man with a seminal discharge spits on someone clean, that person shall wash his garments, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:9 — And any donkey saddle on which the man with a seminal discharge mounts shall be unclean until evening.

Leviticus 15:10 — And whosoever touches anything that was under him shall be unclean until evening. Whosoever carries those things shall wash his garments, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:11 — And anyone whom the man with a seminal discharge touches when he has not washed his hands shall wash his garments, bathe his body in water, and be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:12 — And an earthenware vessel touched by the man with a seminal discharge shall be shattered, and a wooden vessel shall be washed with water and be clean.
Leviticus 15:13 — When the man with a seminal discharge is cleansed from his flow, he shall count seven days for his cleansing, wash his garments, bathe his body in water, and be clean.
Leviticus 15:14 — And on the eighth day he shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, bring them before the Lord to the doors of the Tent of Testimony, and give them unto the priest.
Leviticus 15:15 — And the priest shall prepare them, one for sin and one for a whole burnt offering. The priest shall make atonement for him before the Lord for his flow.
Leviticus 15:16 — And if a man has an emission of semen, he shall bathe his whole body in water and be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:17 — And every garment and every skin on which there is semen shall be washed with water and be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:18 — And if a man lies with a woman with an emission of semen, they shall bathe in water and be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:19 — And if a woman has a flow of blood, her flow shall be in her body; she shall remain in her menstrual discharge for seven days. Whosoever touches her shall be unclean until evening,
Leviticus 15:20 — and everything on which she lies during her menstrual discharge shall be unclean, and everything on which she sits shall be unclean.
Leviticus 15:21 — And whosoever touches her bed shall wash his garments, bathe his body in water, and be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:22 — And whosoever touches any article on which she sits shall wash his garments, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:23 — If, while she is on her bed or on the article on which she sits, he touches her, he shall be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:24 — If anyone lies with her and her uncleanness comes upon him, he shall be unclean for seven days, and every bed on which he lies shall be unclean.

Leviticus 15:25 — And if a woman has a flow of blood for many days outside the time of her menstrual discharge, or if she also has a flow after her menstrual discharge, all the days of her unclean flow shall be like the days of her menstrual discharge; she shall be unclean.

Leviticus 15:26 — And every bed on which she lies during all the days of her flow shall be like the bed of her menstrual discharge, and every article on which she sits shall be unclean, as in the uncleanness of her menstrual discharge.
Leviticus 15:27 — Whosoever touches her shall be unclean. He shall wash his garments, bathe his body in water, and be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:28 — When she is cleansed from her flow, she shall count seven days, and afterward she shall be cleansed.
Leviticus 15:29 — And on the eighth day she shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and bring them unto the priest at the entrance of the Tent of Testimony.
Leviticus 15:30 — And the priest shall prepare one for sin and one for a whole burnt offering. The priest shall make atonement for her before the Lord for her unclean flow.
Leviticus 15:31 — And you shall make the sons of Israel wary of their uncleannesses, so that they do not die because of their uncleanness in defiling My tent which is among them.
Leviticus 15:32 — This is the law for the man with a seminal discharge and for anyone who has an emission of semen and becomes defiled through it,

Leviticus 15:33 — and for the woman bleeding in her menstrual discharge, for the one with a seminal discharge in his flow, male or female, and for the man who lies with a woman in menstrual separation.
