title: Leviticus 17:1–16 · Authorized sacrificial place; rejection of illicit sacrifice; blood, hunted animals, carcasses and washing
paragraphs: Passage group: Authorized sacrificial place; rejection of illicit sacrifice; blood, hunted animals, carcasses and washing. Setting: Sacrifice, blood and purity law.
Requirements appearing in this passage: C0019, C0397, C0473, C0571, C0572, C0573, C0574, C0575, C1232. A mixed passage can link to more than one topic or classification.
Leviticus 17:1 — And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Leviticus 17:2 — Speak unto Aaron and unto his sons and unto all the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: This is the word which the Lord commanded, saying:
Leviticus 17:3 — Any person of the sons of Israel or of the resident foreigners attached to you who slaughters a calf, sheep, or goat in the camp, or slaughters it outside the camp,

Leviticus 17:4 — and does not bring it unto the door of the Tent of Testimony, to prepare it as a whole burnt offering or an offering of deliverance acceptable unto the Lord for a sweet savour; and whosoever slaughters outside, and does not bring it unto the door of the Tent of Testimony, so as not to present a gift unto the Lord before the tent of the Lord: blood shall be reckoned unto that man; he has poured out blood; that soul shall be destroyed from among his people.

Leviticus 17:5 — This is so that the sons of Israel may bring up their sacrifices, which they themselves slaughter in the plains; they shall bring them unto the Lord, to the doors of the Tent of Testimony, unto the priest, and sacrifice them as a sacrifice of deliverance unto the Lord.
Leviticus 17:6 — And the priest shall pour the blood all around against the altar before the Lord beside the doors of the Tent of Testimony and offer up the fat for a sweet savour unto the Lord.

Leviticus 17:7 — And they shall no longer sacrifice their sacrifices to the vain things after which they prostitute themselves. This shall be an everlasting ordinance for you throughout your generations.
Leviticus 17:8 — And you shall say unto them: Any man of the sons of Israel, or of the sons of the resident foreigners attached unto you, who prepares a whole burnt offering or a sacrifice,
Leviticus 17:9 — and does not bring it to the door of the Tent of Testimony to offer it unto the Lord, that person shall be destroyed from among his people.

Leviticus 17:10 — And any man of the sons of Israel, or of the resident foreigners attached unto you, who eats any blood: I will set My face against the soul that eats the blood, and destroy him from among his people.
Leviticus 17:11 — For the life of all flesh is its blood, and I have given it unto you upon the altar to make atonement for your lives; for its blood shall make atonement in place of the life.
Leviticus 17:12 — Therefore I have said unto the sons of Israel: No soul among you shall eat blood; and the resident foreigner attached unto you shall not eat blood.

Leviticus 17:13 — And any person of the sons of Israel or of the resident foreigners attached to you who hunts a wild animal or bird that may be eaten shall pour out the blood and cover it with earth.

Leviticus 17:14 — For the life of all flesh is its blood; and I said unto the sons of Israel: You shall eat no blood of any flesh, for the life of all flesh is its blood; whosoever eats it shall be destroyed.

Leviticus 17:15 — And every soul, whether among the natives or among the resident foreigners, that eats an animal which has died or has been taken by wild beasts, shall wash his garments and bathe in water, and be unclean until evening, and shall be clean.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Speak unto Aaron and unto his sons and unto all the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: This is the word which the Lord commanded, saying:
Any person of the sons of Israel or of the resident foreigners attached to you who slaughters a calf, sheep, or goat in the camp, or slaughters it outside the camp,

and does not bring it unto the door of the Tent of Testimony, to prepare it as a whole burnt offering or an offering of deliverance acceptable unto the Lord for a sweet savour; and whosoever slaughters outside, and does not bring it unto the door of the Tent of Testimony, so as not to present a gift unto the Lord before the tent of the Lord: blood shall be reckoned unto that man; he has poured out blood; that soul shall be destroyed from among his people.

This is so that the sons of Israel may bring up their sacrifices, which they themselves slaughter in the plains; they shall bring them unto the Lord, to the doors of the Tent of Testimony, unto the priest, and sacrifice them as a sacrifice of deliverance unto the Lord.
And the priest shall pour the blood all around against the altar before the Lord beside the doors of the Tent of Testimony and offer up the fat for a sweet savour unto the Lord.
And they shall no longer sacrifice their sacrifices to the vain things after which they prostitute themselves. This shall be an everlasting ordinance for you throughout your generations.
And you shall say unto them: Any man of the sons of Israel, or of the sons of the resident foreigners attached unto you, who prepares a whole burnt offering or a sacrifice,
and does not bring it to the door of the Tent of Testimony to offer it unto the Lord, that person shall be destroyed from among his people.
And any man of the sons of Israel, or of the resident foreigners attached unto you, who eats any blood: I will set My face against the soul that eats the blood, and destroy him from among his people.
For the life of all flesh is its blood, and I have given it unto you upon the altar to make atonement for your lives; for its blood shall make atonement in place of the life.
Therefore I have said unto the sons of Israel: No soul among you shall eat blood; and the resident foreigner attached unto you shall not eat blood.
And any person of the sons of Israel or of the resident foreigners attached to you who hunts a wild animal or bird that may be eaten shall pour out the blood and cover it with earth.
For the life of all flesh is its blood; and I said unto the sons of Israel: You shall eat no blood of any flesh, for the life of all flesh is its blood; whosoever eats it shall be destroyed.

And every soul, whether among the natives or among the resident foreigners, that eats an animal which has died or has been taken by wild beasts, shall wash his garments and bathe in water, and be unclean until evening, and shall be clean.
But if he does not wash his garments and does not bathe his body in water, he shall bear his lawless deed.

title: Numbers 19:1–22 · Red heifer, ashes, water of purification, corpse contact, third and seventh days, washing and consequences
paragraphs: Passage group: Red heifer, ashes, water of purification, corpse contact, third and seventh days, washing and consequences. Setting: Purification law.

Requirements appearing in this passage: C0885, C0886, C0887, C0888, C0889, C0890, C0891, C0892, C0893, C0894, C0895, C0896, C0897, C0898, C0899, C0900, C0901, C0902, C0903, C0904. A mixed passage can link to more than one topic or classification.
Numbers 19:1 — And the Lord spoke unto Moses and Aaron, saying:

Numbers 19:2 — This is the provision of the law which the Lord commanded, saying: Speak unto the sons of Israel, and let them bring unto you a red heifer without blemish, wherein is no defect, and upon which no yoke has been laid.
Numbers 19:3 — And you shall give it unto Eleazar the priest, and they shall bring it outside the camp unto a clean place, and shall slaughter it before him.
Numbers 19:4 — And Eleazar shall take some of its blood and sprinkle some of its blood seven times toward the front of the Tent of Testimony.
Numbers 19:5 — And they shall burn it before him; its skin, flesh, and blood, together with its dung, shall be burned.
Numbers 19:6 — And the priest shall take cedar wood, hyssop, and scarlet material, and they shall throw them into the burning heifer.
Numbers 19:7 — And the priest shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water. Afterward he may enter the camp, but the priest shall be unclean until evening.
Numbers 19:8 — And the one who burns it shall wash his clothes and bathe his body, and he shall be unclean until evening.

Numbers 19:9 — And a clean person shall gather the heifer's ashes and deposit them outside the camp in a clean place. They shall be kept for the congregation of the sons of Israel as water of sprinkling; it is a means of purification.

Numbers 19:10 — And the one who gathers the heifer's ashes shall wash his clothes and be unclean until evening. This shall be an everlasting ordinance for the sons of Israel and the attached sojourners.
Numbers 19:11 — Whosoever touches a dead person, any human being who has died, shall be unclean for seven days.
Numbers 19:12 — That person shall be purified on the third day and on the seventh day, and he shall be clean. If he is not purified on the third day and on the seventh day, he shall not be clean.

Numbers 19:13 — Whosoever touches the dead body of any human being who has died, and is not purified, has defiled the Tent of the Lord; that soul shall be wiped out from Israel. Because water of sprinkling was not sprinkled upon him, he is unclean; his uncleanness is still in him.
Numbers 19:14 — And this is the law: If a person dies in a house, everyone who enters the house and everything in the house shall be unclean for seven days.
Numbers 19:15 — And every open vessel without a fastening tied upon it is unclean.
Numbers 19:16 — And anyone who touches, on the open plain, one slain, a dead person, a human bone, or a tomb shall be unclean for seven days.
Numbers 19:17 — And for the unclean person they shall take some ashes from what was burned for purification, and they shall pour living water over them into a vessel.

Numbers 19:18 — And a clean man shall take hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle it around the house, the vessels, and the people who were there, and on whoever touched the human bone, the slain person, the dead person, or the tomb.

Numbers 19:19 — And the clean person shall sprinkle the unclean person on the third day and on the seventh day. He shall be purified on the seventh day, wash his clothes, and bathe in water, and he shall be unclean until evening.

Numbers 19:20 — And if a man is defiled, and is not purified, that soul shall be destroyed from the midst of the congregation, because he has defiled the holy things of the Lord; because water of sprinkling was not sprinkled upon him, he is unclean.

Numbers 19:21 — And this shall be an everlasting ordinance for you. The one who sprinkles the water of sprinkling shall wash his clothes, and whosoever touches the water of sprinkling shall be unclean until evening.
Numbers 19:22 — And whatever the unclean person touches shall be unclean, and the person who touches it shall be unclean until evening.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke unto Moses and Aaron, saying:

This is the provision of the law which the Lord commanded, saying: Speak unto the sons of Israel, and let them bring unto you a red heifer without blemish, wherein is no defect, and upon which no yoke has been laid.
And you shall give it unto Eleazar the priest, and they shall bring it outside the camp unto a clean place, and shall slaughter it before him.
And Eleazar shall take some of its blood and sprinkle some of its blood seven times toward the front of the Tent of Testimony.
And they shall burn it before him; its skin, flesh, and blood, together with its dung, shall be burned.
And the priest shall take cedar wood, hyssop, and scarlet material, and they shall throw them into the burning heifer.
And the priest shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water. Afterward he may enter the camp, but the priest shall be unclean until evening.
And the one who burns it shall wash his clothes and bathe his body, and he shall be unclean until evening.

And a clean person shall gather the heifer's ashes and deposit them outside the camp in a clean place. They shall be kept for the congregation of the sons of Israel as water of sprinkling; it is a means of purification.
And the one who gathers the heifer's ashes shall wash his clothes and be unclean until evening. This shall be an everlasting ordinance for the sons of Israel and the attached sojourners.
Whosoever touches a dead person, any human being who has died, shall be unclean for seven days.
That person shall be purified on the third day and on the seventh day, and he shall be clean. If he is not purified on the third day and on the seventh day, he shall not be clean.

Whosoever touches the dead body of any human being who has died, and is not purified, has defiled the Tent of the Lord; that soul shall be wiped out from Israel. Because water of sprinkling was not sprinkled upon him, he is unclean; his uncleanness is still in him.
And this is the law: If a person dies in a house, everyone who enters the house and everything in the house shall be unclean for seven days.
And every open vessel without a fastening tied upon it is unclean.
And anyone who touches, on the open plain, one slain, a dead person, a human bone, or a tomb shall be unclean for seven days.
And for the unclean person they shall take some ashes from what was burned for purification, and they shall pour living water over them into a vessel.

And a clean man shall take hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle it around the house, the vessels, and the people who were there, and on whoever touched the human bone, the slain person, the dead person, or the tomb.

And the clean person shall sprinkle the unclean person on the third day and on the seventh day. He shall be purified on the seventh day, wash his clothes, and bathe in water, and he shall be unclean until evening.

And if a man is defiled, and is not purified, that soul shall be destroyed from the midst of the congregation, because he has defiled the holy things of the Lord; because water of sprinkling was not sprinkled upon him, he is unclean.
And this shall be an everlasting ordinance for you. The one who sprinkles the water of sprinkling shall wash his clothes, and whosoever touches the water of sprinkling shall be unclean until evening.
And whatever the unclean person touches shall be unclean, and the person who touches it shall be unclean until evening.

paragraphs: Study 1: Human fruitfulness as God’s blessing
Related indexed requirements: C0001, C0002, C0003, C0004. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Connection to Christ: Jesus and Paul recognize celibacy alongside the creation blessing of human fruitfulness.
Christian response today: Receive family life as a gift, and honor faithful single people and those unable to have children.
Saints Translation — Law: Genesis 1:27–28 · Genesis 35:11 Christ and the apostles: Matthew 19:10–12 · 1 Corinthians 7:7
Text and setting: Creation
Torah: Genesis 1:27–28 · Genesis 35:11

God blesses humanity with fruitfulness and repeats the promise to Jacob. These passages concern embodied human life and descendants. They do not require every individual to marry or have children: Jesus and Paul also recognize faithful celibacy. Spiritual fruit is a related Christian theme, not a replacement translation of this verse.

verses.text: This is what the Lord commanded: Gather from it, each for those belonging to him, an omer per person according to your number. Each of you shall gather with your tent companions.”

verses.text: After the next day Moses sat to judge the people, and all the people stood before Moses from morning until evening.
And when Jethro saw all that he did to the people, he said, “What is this that you do to the people? Why do you sit alone, while all the people stand before you from morning until evening?”
Moses said to his father-in-law, “The people come to me to seek judgment from God.
When they have a dispute and come to me, I judge each case and instruct them in God’s ordinances and His law.”
And Moses’ father-in-law said to him, “You are not doing this rightly.
You shall be worn out with unbearable exhaustion, both you and all this people who are with you; this matter is heavy for you, and you cannot do it alone.
Now therefore listen to me, and I will counsel you, and God shall be with you. Represent the people in matters pertaining to God, and bring their words to God.
And you shall solemnly instruct them in the ordinances of God and His law, and show them the ways in which they shall walk, and the works which they shall do.

And choose for yourself from all the people able men who fear God, righteous men who hate arrogance; and you shall set them over the people as rulers of thousands, and rulers of hundreds, and rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens.

And they shall judge the people at all times; the weighty matter they shall bring to you, but the lesser judgments they shall judge themselves; and they shall lighten your burden, and bear it with you.
If you do this thing, God shall strengthen you, and you shall be able to stand; and all this people shall come to their own place in peace.”
Moses listened to his father-in-law and did all that he said.
Moses chose capable men from all Israel and appointed them over the people as leaders of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.
They judged the people at all times. They brought every weighty matter to Moses, but judged every light matter themselves.

title: Exodus 36:1–38 · Craftsmanship, sufficiency of contributions and the priestly garments in the Saints Greek order
paragraphs: Passage group: Craftsmanship, sufficiency of contributions and the priestly garments in the Saints Greek order. Setting: Execution record.
Construction is reported here rather than newly commanded. The Greek-based arrangement differs substantially from Hebrew-based chapter arrangements.
Requirements appearing in this passage: M008, C0366. A mixed passage can link to more than one topic or classification.

Exodus 36:1 — Bezalel, Eliab, and every person wise in understanding, who had been given wisdom and knowledge to understand how to do all the work for the holy service, worked according to all that the Lord had commanded.
Exodus 36:2 — Moses called Bezalel, Eliab, and all who possessed wisdom, to whom God had given knowledge in their hearts, and all who willingly came forward to the work to complete it.

Exodus 36:3 — They received from Moses all the contributions the sons of Israel had brought for all the work of the sanctuary, to carry it out. They continued receiving gifts from those who brought them, morning after morning.
Exodus 36:4 — All the skilled workers who were doing the work of the sanctuary came, each according to the work he was doing,
Exodus 36:5 — and they said to Moses, “The people are bringing more than is needed for the work the Lord commanded to be done.”
Exodus 36:6 — Moses gave a command and proclaimed in the camp, “Let neither man nor woman work any longer for the firstfruits of the sanctuary.” The people were restrained from bringing any more.
Exodus 36:7 — The work supplied was sufficient for the construction, with some left over.
Exodus 36:8 — Every skilled worker among the craftsmen made the holy robes for Aaron the priest, as the Lord commanded Moses.
Exodus 36:9 — They made the shoulder-piece of gold, blue, purple, spun scarlet, and spun fine linen.
Exodus 36:10 — The gold plates were cut into threads to be woven with the blue, purple, spun scarlet, and spun fine linen, a woven work.
Exodus 36:11 — They made joined shoulder sections for it on both sides,

Exodus 36:12 — a woven work intertwined together. They made it by itself from the same material, according to its workmanship: gold, blue, purple, spun scarlet, and spun fine linen, as the Lord commanded Moses.
Exodus 36:13 — They made the two emerald stones, clasped and set in gold, engraved like seals with the names of the sons of Israel.
Exodus 36:14 — He put them on the shoulders of the shoulder-piece as memorial stones for the sons of Israel, as the Lord commanded Moses.
Exodus 36:15 — They made the oracle-piece with woven embroidery, like the workmanship of the shoulder-piece, of gold, blue, purple, spun scarlet, and spun fine linen.
Exodus 36:16 — They made the oracle-piece square and doubled, a span long and a span wide when doubled.
Exodus 36:17 — A fabric set with four rows of stones was woven into it. The first row was a sardius, topaz, and emerald;
Exodus 36:18 — the second row a carbuncle, sapphire, and jasper;
Exodus 36:19 — the third row a ligure, agate, and amethyst;
Exodus 36:20 — the fourth row was a chrysolite, beryl, and onyx, enclosed in gold and bound in gold.
Exodus 36:21 — There were twelve stones bearing the names of the sons of Israel, each engraved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes.
Exodus 36:22 — They made braided chains of pure gold for the oracle-piece.
Exodus 36:23 — They made two gold rosettes and two gold rings, and put the two gold rings at the two ends of the oracle-piece.
Exodus 36:24 — They put the gold braids into the rings on both sides of the oracle-piece,
Exodus 36:25 — and the two braids into the two joinings. They put them on the two rosettes and on the shoulders of the shoulder-piece, facing forward.
Exodus 36:26 — They made two gold rings and put them at the two ends of the oracle-piece, on its edge toward the rear, on the inner side of the shoulder-piece.
Exodus 36:27 — They made two gold rings and put them on both shoulders of the shoulder-piece, below it at the front, by the joining above the shoulder-piece’s interwoven fabric.

Exodus 36:28 — He fastened the oracle-piece by its rings to the rings of the shoulder-piece with blue cord, interwoven into the shoulder-piece’s fabric so that the oracle-piece would not come loose from it, as the Lord commanded Moses.
Exodus 36:29 — They made the robe beneath the shoulder-piece of woven work, entirely blue.
Exodus 36:30 — The opening of the robe was in its middle, woven and joined together, with a border around the opening so that it would not tear.
Exodus 36:31 — They made pomegranates at the lower hem of the robe, of blue, purple, spun scarlet, and spun fine linen, like a pomegranate tree in bloom.
Exodus 36:32 — They made gold bells and placed the bells at the hem of the robe, all around between the pomegranates,
Exodus 36:33 — a gold bell and a pomegranate at the hem of the robe all around, for ministry, as the Lord commanded Moses.
Exodus 36:34 — They made woven tunics of fine linen for Aaron and his sons,
Exodus 36:35 — the turbans of fine linen, the headband of fine linen, and the linen undergarments of spun fine linen.
Exodus 36:36 — They made their sashes of fine linen, blue, purple, and spun scarlet, the work of an embroiderer, as the Lord commanded Moses.
Exodus 36:37 — They made the gold plate, the holy consecration emblem, of pure gold. He wrote upon it letters engraved as on a seal: “A holy thing to the Lord.”
Exodus 36:38 — They put a blue band on it, to fasten it on the headband above, as the Lord commanded Moses.

Exodus 37:1 — They made ten curtains for the tent.
Exodus 37:2 — Each curtain was twenty-eight cubits long; all were alike. Each curtain was four cubits wide.
Exodus 37:3 — They made the veil of blue, purple, spun scarlet, and spun fine linen, with woven cherubim.
Exodus 37:4 — They placed it on four pillars of decay-resistant wood overlaid with gold. Their capitals were gold, and their four bases were silver.
Exodus 37:5 — They made the entrance veil of the Tent of Testimony of blue, purple, spun scarlet, and spun fine linen, with woven cherubim.
Exodus 37:6 — They made its five pillars and their rings, overlaid their capitals and their bands with gold, and made their five bases of bronze.
Exodus 37:7 — They made the court, with its southwest hangings of spun fine linen, a hundred by a hundred.
Exodus 37:8 — There were twenty pillars and twenty bases.
Exodus 37:9 — The north side was a hundred by a hundred, with twenty pillars and twenty bases.
Exodus 37:10 — On the side toward the sea were curtains of fifty cubits, with ten pillars and ten bases.
Exodus 37:11 — On the east side were fifty cubits.
Exodus 37:12 — On the flank were hangings of fifteen cubits, with three pillars and three bases.
Exodus 37:13 — On the second flank, on either side by the gate of the court, were curtains of fifteen cubits, with three pillars and three bases.
Exodus 37:14 — All the curtains of the court were of spun fine linen.
Exodus 37:15 — Their pillars’ bases were bronze, their hooks silver, their capitals overlaid with silver, and all the court’s pillars overlaid with silver.

Exodus 37:18 — and the pillars themselves were overlaid with silver. All the pegs around the court were bronze.
Exodus 37:19 — This is the arrangement of the Tent of Testimony, as appointed for Moses, with the service belonging to the Levites through Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
Exodus 37:20 — Bezalel son of Uri, of the tribe of Judah, did as the Lord commanded Moses.
Exodus 37:21 — Eliab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, directed the woven, needleworked, and embroidered work, weaving in scarlet and fine linen.

title: Exodus 38:1–27 · Ark, sanctuary furnishings, altars and washing equipment in the Saints Greek order
paragraphs: Passage group: Ark, sanctuary furnishings, altars and washing equipment in the Saints Greek order. Setting: Execution record.

Exodus 38:1 — Bezalel made the ark.
Exodus 38:2 — He overlaid it with pure gold inside and outside.
Exodus 38:3 — He cast four gold rings for it, two on one side and two on the other.
Exodus 38:4 — The rings were wide enough for the carrying poles, so that the ark could be carried with them.
Exodus 38:5 — He made the propitiatory cover above the ark of gold.
Exodus 38:6 — He made the two gold cherubim,
Exodus 38:7 — one cherub at one end of the propitiatory cover and one cherub at its other end,
Exodus 38:8 — sheltering the propitiatory cover with their wings.
Exodus 38:9 — He made the table of presentation of pure gold.
Exodus 38:10 — He cast four rings for it, two on one side and two on the other, wide enough for the poles with which it would be carried.
Exodus 38:11 — He made the carrying poles of the ark and of the table, and overlaid them with gold.
Exodus 38:12 — He made the table’s utensils of gold: its dishes, incense vessels, ladles, and libation vessels with which to pour drink offerings.
Exodus 38:13 — He made the gold lampstand that gives light, with a solid shaft,
Exodus 38:14 — and its branches on both sides.
Exodus 38:15 — Shoots extended from its branches, three on this side and three on that side, corresponding to one another.

Exodus 38:16 — The lamp supports at their ends were nut-shaped and formed from them, as were the fittings on which the lamps would stand. The seventh fitting was at the end of the lamp support, at the top above; it was wholly solid gold.
Exodus 38:17 — He made seven gold lamps on it, its gold tongs, and its gold trays.
Exodus 38:18 — He overlaid the pillars with silver, cast gold rings for the pillar, and overlaid the bars with gold. He overlaid the pillars of the veil with gold and made gold hooks.
Exodus 38:19 — He also made the rings of the tent of gold, and the rings of the court and the rings for stretching the covering overhead of bronze.
Exodus 38:20 — He cast the silver capitals of the tent and the bronze capitals of the tent doorway and the gate of the court. He made silver hooks for the pillars; he silvered them.
Exodus 38:21 — He made the pegs of the tent and the pegs of the court of bronze.
Exodus 38:22 — He made the bronze altar from the bronze censers belonging to the men who had rebelled with the assembly of Korah.
Exodus 38:23 — He made all the altar’s utensils: its firepan, its base, its bowls, and its bronze meat forks.

Exodus 38:24 — He made a grating for the altar, a work of network beneath its firepan, below it as far as its middle. He put four bronze rings on the four sides of the altar’s grating, wide enough for the bars with which the altar would be carried.
Exodus 38:25 — He made the holy anointing oil and the compounded incense, the pure work of a perfumer.
Exodus 38:26 — He made the bronze basin and its bronze base from the mirrors of the women who fasted, who fasted at the doors of the Tent of Testimony on the day he set it up.

Exodus 38:27 — He made the basin so that Moses, Aaron, and his sons might wash their hands and feet from it. When they entered the Tent of Testimony, or approached the altar to minister, they washed from it, as the Lord commanded Moses.

title: Exodus 39:1–23 · Materials account, completed work, delivery and inspection in the Saints Greek order
paragraphs: Passage group: Materials account, completed work, delivery and inspection in the Saints Greek order. Setting: Execution record.

Exodus 39:1 — All the gold worked into the objects, for all the work of the holy things, was the gold of the firstfruits: twenty-nine talents and seven hundred and twenty shekels, by the holy shekel.
Exodus 39:2 — The silver contribution from the enrolled men of the congregation was a hundred talents and one thousand seven hundred and seventy-five shekels,
Exodus 39:3 — one drachma per head, half a shekel by the holy shekel, for everyone passing into the enrolment from twenty years old upward: six hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty.
Exodus 39:4 — The hundred talents of silver were used to cast the hundred capitals of the tent and the capitals of the veil: a hundred capitals for the hundred talents, a talent per capital.
Exodus 39:5 — They used the one thousand seven hundred and seventy-five shekels for the pillars’ hooks; he gilded their capitals and adorned them.
Exodus 39:6 — The bronze of the contribution was seventy talents and one thousand five hundred shekels.
Exodus 39:7 — From it he made the bases of the entrance of the Tent of Testimony,
Exodus 39:8 — the bases of the court all around, the bases of the court’s gate, the pegs of the tent, and the pegs of the surrounding court,
Exodus 39:9 — and the bronze grating of the altar, all the altar’s utensils, and all the equipment of the Tent of Testimony.
Exodus 39:10 — The sons of Israel did as the Lord commanded Moses; so they did.
Exodus 39:11 — From the gold remaining from the contribution they made utensils for ministering before the Lord.
Exodus 39:12 — From the remaining blue, purple, and scarlet they made Aaron’s robes for ministry, to minister in the sanctuary.
Exodus 39:13 — They brought to Moses the robes, the tent and its utensils, its bases, its bars, and its pillars;
Exodus 39:14 — the ark of the covenant and its carrying poles;
Exodus 39:15 — the altar and all its utensils, the anointing oil, and the compounded incense;
Exodus 39:16 — the pure lampstand and its lamps, the lamps for burning, and the oil for the light;
Exodus 39:17 — the table of presentation and all its utensils, and the bread of the Presence;
Exodus 39:18 — Aaron’s robes for the sanctuary and his sons’ robes for priestly service;
Exodus 39:19 — the hangings of the court and the pillars, the veil for the entrance of the tent and for the gate of the court, all the utensils of the tent, and all its equipment;
Exodus 39:20 — the leather coverings of rams’ skins dyed red, the coverings of blue skins, and the coverings for the remaining things;
Exodus 39:21 — the pegs, and all the equipment for the work of the Tent of Testimony.

verses.text: All the gold worked into the objects, for all the work of the holy things, was the gold of the firstfruits: twenty-nine talents and seven hundred and twenty shekels, by the holy shekel.
The silver contribution from the enrolled men of the congregation was a hundred talents and one thousand seven hundred and seventy-five shekels,
one drachma per head, half a shekel by the holy shekel, for everyone passing into the enrolment from twenty years old upward: six hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty.
The hundred talents of silver were used to cast the hundred capitals of the tent and the capitals of the veil: a hundred capitals for the hundred talents, a talent per capital.
They used the one thousand seven hundred and seventy-five shekels for the pillars’ hooks; he gilded their capitals and adorned them.
The bronze of the contribution was seventy talents and one thousand five hundred shekels.
From it he made the bases of the entrance of the Tent of Testimony,
the bases of the court all around, the bases of the court’s gate, the pegs of the tent, and the pegs of the surrounding court,
and the bronze grating of the altar, all the altar’s utensils, and all the equipment of the Tent of Testimony.
The sons of Israel did as the Lord commanded Moses; so they did.
From the gold remaining from the contribution they made utensils for ministering before the Lord.
From the remaining blue, purple, and scarlet they made Aaron’s robes for ministry, to minister in the sanctuary.
They brought to Moses the robes, the tent and its utensils, its bases, its bars, and its pillars;
the ark of the covenant and its carrying poles;
the altar and all its utensils, the anointing oil, and the compounded incense;
the pure lampstand and its lamps, the lamps for burning, and the oil for the light;
the table of presentation and all its utensils, and the bread of the Presence;
Aaron’s robes for the sanctuary and his sons’ robes for priestly service;
the hangings of the court and the pillars, the veil for the entrance of the tent and for the gate of the court, all the utensils of the tent, and all its equipment;
the leather coverings of rams’ skins dyed red, the coverings of blue skins, and the coverings for the remaining things;
the pegs, and all the equipment for the work of the Tent of Testimony.
The sons of Israel made all the equipment as the Lord commanded Moses.
Moses saw all the work, and they had done it in the way the Lord commanded Moses; so they had done it. Moses blessed them.

Could sheep and cattle be slaughtered for them and be enough? Could all the food of the sea be gathered for them and be enough?
And the Lord said unto Moses: Shall the hand of the Lord not suffice? Now you shall know whether My word shall overtake you or not.
And Moses went out and told the people the Lord’s words. He gathered seventy men from the elders of the people and stationed them around the tent.

And the Lord came down in a cloud and spoke to him. He took some of the Spirit that was upon him and put it upon the seventy men, the elders. When the Spirit rested upon them, they prophesied, and did not do so again.

Numbers 14:19 — Forgive this people’s sin according to Thy great mercy, as Thou hast been gracious to them from Egypt until now.
Numbers 14:20 — And the Lord said unto Moses: I am gracious to them according to your word.

Numbers 14:29 — In this wilderness your bodies shall fall, with your entire registration and those of you counted from twenty years old and upward who grumbled against Me.
Numbers 14:30 — You shall certainly not enter the land over which I stretched out My hand to settle you upon it, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.

Numbers 14:34 — According to the number of days you searched out the land—forty days, a day for a year—you shall bear your sins for forty years, and you shall know the fury of My anger.

The Lord is long-suffering, and abundant in mercy, and true, taking away lawlessness and wrongdoing and sins; yet He will in no wise cleanse the guilty, repaying the sins of fathers upon children unto the third and fourth generations.
Forgive this people’s sin according to Thy great mercy, as Thou hast been gracious to them from Egypt until now.
And the Lord said unto Moses: I am gracious to them according to your word.
But as I live, and as My name lives, the glory of the Lord shall fill all the earth;
all the men who have seen My glory and the signs I did in Egypt and this wilderness, and have tested Me this tenth time and have not listened to My voice,

shall certainly not see the land I swore to their fathers. But their children who are here with Me, who do not know good or evil, every inexperienced young person—to these I will give the land. None of those who provoke Me shall see it.
But My servant Caleb, because a different spirit was in him and he followed Me, I will bring into the land he entered, and his seed shall inherit it.
Amalek and the Canaanites live in the valley. Tomorrow turn and depart for the wilderness by the way of the Red Sea.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses and Aaron, saying:
How long with this evil congregation? They grumble before Me; I have heard the sons of Israel’s grumbling that they have directed against you.
Say to them, I live, says the Lord: I will certainly do to you just as you have spoken into My ears.
In this wilderness your bodies shall fall, with your entire registration and those of you counted from twenty years old and upward who grumbled against Me.
You shall certainly not enter the land over which I stretched out My hand to settle you upon it, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.
And I will bring into the land the children whom you said would become plunder, and they shall inherit the land from which you turned away.
And your bodies shall fall in this wilderness.
But your sons shall live as herders in the wilderness for forty years and bear your whoredom, until your bodies are consumed in the wilderness.
According to the number of days you searched out the land—forty days, a day for a year—you shall bear your sins for forty years, and you shall know the fury of My anger.
I, the Lord, have spoken. I will certainly do this to this evil congregation that has banded together against Me. In this wilderness they shall be consumed, and there they shall die.
And the men Moses had sent to inspect the land came back and grumbled against it before the congregation, bringing out evil words about the land.
And those men who spoke evil against the land died in the plague before the Lord.
And Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh lived, out of those men who had gone to explore the land.
And Moses spoke these words to all the sons of Israel, and the people mourned greatly.
And they rose early in the morning and went up to the top of the mountain, saying: Here we are! We will go up to the place the Lord has spoken of, for we have sinned.
And Moses said: Why do you transgress the Lord’s word? Things will not go well for you.
Do not go up, for the Lord is not with you, and you shall fall before your enemies.
Amalek and the Canaanites are there before you, and you shall fall by the sword. Because you turned away in disobedience unto the Lord, the Lord will not be among you.
And they forced their way up to the top of the mountain. The ark of the Lord’s covenant and Moses did not move from the camp.
And Amalek and the Canaanites who lived on that mountain came down, routed them, and cut them down as far as Erman. Then they returned to the camp.

And Balaam rose in the morning, saddled his donkey, and went with the officials of Moab.
And God grew angry because he went. God's angel rose to obstruct him. Balaam was riding his donkey, with his two servants beside him.
And the donkey saw God's angel opposing them in the road with his sword drawn in his hand. She turned off the road into the plain, and he struck her with the staff to direct her onto the road.
And God's angel stood in the furrows of the vineyards, with a fence on either side.
And the donkey saw God's angel and pressed herself against the wall, crushing Balaam's foot. He whipped her again.
And God's angel went farther and stood in a narrow place where there was no way to turn right or left.
And the donkey saw God's angel and crouched beneath Balaam. Balaam became angry and beat the donkey with his staff.
And God opened the donkey's mouth, and she says to Balaam: What have I done unto you that you have struck me this third time?
And Balaam said to the donkey: Because you have mocked me! If I had a sword in my hand, I would have stabbed you already.
And the donkey says to Balaam: Am I not your donkey, which you have ridden from your youth until this day? Have I acted like this toward you out of deliberate disregard? He said: No.
God uncovered Balaam's eyes, and he sees the Lord's angel opposing him in the road with his sword drawn in his hand. He bent down and prostrated himself on his face.
And God's angel said to him: Why have you struck your donkey this third time? Behold, I have come out to oppose you, because your way is not fitting before me.
And the donkey saw me and turned away from me this third time. If she had not turned away, I would now have killed you and preserved her.
And Balaam said unto the Lord's angel: I have sinned, for I did not know that you were opposing me in the road. Now, if this does not please you, I will turn back.
And God's angel said to Balaam: Go with the men, but take care to speak the word that I tell you. Balaam went with Balak's officials.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Exact vengeance for the sons of Israel from the Midianites. Finally you shall be gathered to your people.
And Moses spoke to the people, saying: Equip men from among you to draw up for battle before the Lord against Midian, to repay Midian with vengeance from the Lord.
Send a thousand from each tribe, from all the tribes of Israel, to draw up for battle.
And they counted out a thousand from each tribe from the thousands of Israel: twelve thousand equipped for battle.
And Moses sent them, a thousand from each tribe, with their force and Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, with the sacred vessels and the signalling trumpets in their hands.
And they drew up for battle against Midian, as the Lord had commanded Moses, and killed every male.
And they killed the kings of Midian together with their slain: Evi, Zur, Rekem, Hur, and Robok, the five kings of Midian. They also killed Balaam son of Beor with the sword together with their slain.
And they took the women of Midian and their dependents as spoil, and plundered their livestock, all their possessions, and their resources.
And they burned all their towns in their settlements and their farmsteads with fire.
And they took all the plunder and all their spoils, from people to livestock,
and brought the captives, the spoils, and the plunder unto Moses, Eleazar the priest, and all the sons of Israel, at the camp at Araboth Moab, which is on the Jordan opposite Jericho.
And Moses, Eleazar the priest, and all the rulers of the congregation went out to meet them outside the camp.
And Moses was angry with the overseers of the force, the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds who were returning from the battle formation,
and Moses said to them: Why have you taken every female alive?
For these women, according to Balaam’s word, caused the sons of Israel to turn away and disregard the Lord’s word because of Peor, and the plague came upon the Lord’s congregation.
And now kill every male among all the dependents, and kill every woman who has known a male’s bed.
Take alive all the female dependents who have not known a male’s bed.
And you shall camp outside the camp for seven days. Everyone who killed someone or touches someone slain shall be purified on the third day and the seventh day, both you and your captives.
And you shall thoroughly purify every covering, every leather article, every object made from goats’ hair, and every wooden article.
And Eleazar the priest said to the men of the force who were returning from the battle formation, This is the ordinance of the law that the Lord prescribed unto Moses:
Only the gold, and the silver, and the bronze, and the iron, and the lead, and the tin,
everything that passes through fire shall also be cleansed, but it shall be purified with the water of purification. Everything that does not pass through fire shall pass through water.
And you shall wash your clothes on the seventh day and be cleansed; afterward you shall enter the camp.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Take a total of the spoils of captivity, from people to livestock, you, Eleazar the priest, and the rulers of the congregation’s ancestral houses.
And you shall divide the spoils between the warriors who go forth into battle and the whole congregation.

And you shall set apart a levy unto the Lord from the warriors who went forth into battle: one living being out of five hundred, from the men, and from the livestock, and from the cattle, and from the sheep, and from the goats.
And you shall take it from their half; and you shall give unto Eleazar the priest the firstfruits of the Lord.

And from the half belonging to the sons of Israel you shall take one out of fifty, from the men, and from the cattle, and from the sheep, and from the donkeys, and from all the livestock; and you shall give them unto the Levites who keep the charges in the Tent of the Lord.
And Moses and Eleazar the priest did as the Lord had prescribed unto Moses.
And the surplus of the plunder that the warriors had taken was six hundred seventy-five thousand sheep,
And seventy-two thousand cattle,
And sixty-one thousand donkeys,
and thirty-two thousand human beings in all, from the women who had not known a man’s bed.
And the half-share belonging to those who went out to war numbered three hundred thirty-seven thousand five hundred sheep,
and the levy for the Lord from the sheep was six hundred seventy-five.
And the cattle numbered thirty-six thousand, and the levy for the Lord was seventy-two.
And the donkeys numbered thirty thousand five hundred, and the levy for the Lord was sixty-one.
And the human beings numbered sixteen thousand, and their levy for the Lord was thirty-two persons.
And Moses gave the levy for the Lord, the portion set apart unto God, to Eleazar the priest, as the Lord had prescribed unto Moses.
From the half belonging to the sons of Israel, which Moses had separated from the warriors—
And the congregation’s half was three hundred thirty-seven thousand five hundred sheep,
And thirty-six thousand cattle,
thirty thousand five hundred donkeys,
and sixteen thousand human beings—

and Moses took from the half belonging to the sons of Israel one out of fifty, from the men and from the livestock, and gave them unto the Levites who kept the charges of the Tent of the Lord, as the Lord commanded Moses.
And all those appointed over the army’s units of a thousand, the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, approached Moses.
And they said unto Moses: Your servants have counted the warriors in our company, and not even one of them is missing.
And we have brought the gift unto the Lord, each man whatever gold article he found—armlets, bracelets, rings, wrist ornaments, and hair ornaments—to make atonement for us before the Lord.
And Moses and Eleazar the priest received the gold from them, every article worked by hand.
And all the gold, the portion set apart that they set aside for the Lord from the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, was sixteen thousand seven hundred fifty shekels.
And the warriors had taken plunder, each for himself.
And Moses and Eleazar the priest received the gold from the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and brought it into the Tent of Testimony as a memorial for the sons of Israel before the Lord.

verses.text: And we turned and departed into the wilderness by the way of the Red Sea, as the Lord had spoken unto me; and we compassed Mount Seir many days.
And the Lord said unto me:
Let it suffice you to have compassed this mountain; turn therefore northward.
And command the people, saying: You are passing through the borders of your brethren, the sons of Esau, who dwell in Seir; and they shall fear you, and be exceedingly wary of you.
Do not join battle with them, for I will give you none of their land, no, not so much as a footstep; for I have given Mount Seir unto the sons of Esau for a possession.
Buy food from them for silver, and eat; and you shall take water from them by measure for silver, and drink.

For the Lord our God has blessed you in all the work of your hands. Consider how you passed through that great and fearful wilderness. Behold, these forty years the Lord your God has been with you; you have lacked nothing.
And we passed by our brethren, the sons of Esau who dwell in Seir, along the way of Arabah, from Ailon and from Ezion-geber; and we turned and passed along the wilderness way of Moab.

And the Lord said unto me: Do not deal as enemies with the Moabites, neither join battle with them; for I will give you none of their land for a possession, for I have given Seir unto the sons of Lot to inherit.
The Emim dwelt there aforetime, a nation great and numerous and strong as the Anakim.
These also are reckoned as Rephaim, like the Anakim; and the Moabites call them Emim.

And the Horites dwelt in Seir aforetime; but the sons of Esau destroyed them, and blotted them out from before them, and dwelt in their stead, as Israel did in the land of its inheritance, which the Lord gave unto them.
Now therefore arise, and set forth, and pass through the Ravine Zered. And we passed through the Ravine Zered.

And the time wherein we journeyed from Kadesh-barnea until we passed through the Ravine Zered was thirty and eight years, until the whole generation of men of war had fallen, dying out of the camp, as God had sworn unto them.
And the hand of God was upon them, to consume them out of the camp, until they had fallen.
And it came to pass, when all the men of war had fallen, dying out from among the people,
that the Lord spoke unto me, saying:
You shall pass this day through the borders of Moab, even Seir,

and you shall draw near unto the sons of Ammon. Do not deal as enemies with them, neither join battle with them; for I will give you none of the land of the sons of Ammon for a possession, because I have given it unto the sons of Lot for a possession.
It is reckoned a land of Rephaim; for the Rephaim dwelt there aforetime, and the Ammonites call them Zamzummim,
a nation great and numerous and mightier than you, like the Anakim. And the Lord destroyed them from before the Ammonites, who inherited the land and dwelt in their stead unto this day,
even as they did for the sons of Esau who dwell in Seir, when they blotted out the Horites from before them, and inherited the land, and dwelt in their stead unto this day.
And the Hivites who dwelt in settlements as far as Gaza, the Cappadocians who came forth from Cappadocia blotted them out, and dwelt in their stead.

Now therefore arise, and set forth, and pass through the Ravine Arnon. Behold, I have delivered into your hands Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land. Begin to inherit it; join battle with him.
This day begin to put the dread of you and the fear of you before all the nations under heaven, who, when they hear your name, shall be troubled and shall suffer pangs before you.
And I sent messengers from the wilderness of Kedemoth unto Sihon king of Heshbon with words of peace, saying:
I will pass through your land. I will pass along the way; I will turn neither to the right nor to the left.
You shall sell me food for silver, and I will eat; and you shall sell me water for silver, and I will drink. Only let me pass through on foot,
as the sons of Esau who dwell in Seir, and the Moabites who dwell in Aroer, did for me, until I pass over the Jordan into the land which the Lord our God gives us.
And Sihon king of Heshbon would not let us pass through his land; for the Lord our God hardened his spirit and strengthened his heart, that he might be delivered into your hands, as at this day.
And the Lord said unto me: Behold, I have begun to deliver before you Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land; begin to inherit his land.
And Sihon king of Heshbon came out to meet us, he and all his people, unto battle at Jahaz.
And the Lord our God delivered him before us; and we smote him, and his sons, and all his people.
And we took all his cities at that time, and utterly destroyed every city in succession, with their women and their children; we left none alive as a captive.
Only the cattle we took as plunder, and the spoil of the cities we took.

From Aroer, which is upon the bank of the torrent Arnon, and the city which is in the ravine, even unto the hill country of Gilead, there was no city that escaped us; the Lord our God delivered them all into our hands.
Only unto the land of the sons of Ammon we did not draw near, all that borders upon the torrent Jabbok, and the cities in the hill country, as the Lord our God commanded us.

And at that time we took the land from the hands of the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, from the torrent Arnon unto Hermon.
The Phoenicians call Hermon Sanior, and the Amorites call it Senir.
All the cities of Misor, and all Gilead, and all Bashan, as far as Salcah and Edrei, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan.

For only Og king of Bashan remained of the Rephaim. Behold, his bed was a bed of iron; behold, it is in the citadel of the sons of Ammon, nine cubits in length and four cubits in breadth, by the cubit of a man.
And we inherited that land at that time. From Aroer, which is upon the bank of the torrent Arnon, and half the hill country of Gilead, with its cities, I gave unto Reuben and unto Gad.
And the rest of Gilead, and all Bashan, the kingdom of Og, I gave unto the half tribe of Manasseh, with all the region of Argob, all that Bashan; it is reckoned a land of Rephaim.
And Jair son of Manasseh took all the region of Argob, unto the borders of Gargasi and the Maacathites; and he called those places of Bashan after his own name, Havvoth-jair, unto this day.
And unto Machir I gave Gilead.
And unto Reuben and unto Gad I gave from Gilead unto the torrent Arnon, the midst of the torrent being the border, and unto Jabbok, the torrent which is the border of the sons of Ammon;
and the Arabah, and the Jordan as the border, Machanareth, and as far as the Sea of Arabah, the Salt Sea, below Asedoth-Pisgah toward the east.
And I commanded you at that time, saying: The Lord your God has given you this land for a possession. Go armed before your brethren, the sons of Israel, every able man.
Only let your wives, and your children, and your cattle, for I know that you have much cattle, dwell in your cities which I have given you,

until the Lord your God gives rest unto your brethren, as unto you, and they also inherit the land which the Lord our God gives them beyond the Jordan; then you shall return, every man unto his inheritance which I have given you.

And I commanded Joshua at that time, saying: Your eyes have seen all that the Lord our God has done unto these two kings; so shall the Lord our God do unto all the kingdoms whither you are passing over.
You shall not fear, for the Lord our God Himself shall fight for you.
And I besought the Lord at that time, saying:

O Lord, Lord, Thou hast begun to show Thy servant Thy strength, and Thy power, and Thy mighty hand, and Thine uplifted arm; for what god is there in heaven or upon earth who shall do as Thou hast done, and according to Thy strength?
Let me therefore pass over and see this good land beyond the Jordan, this good hill country and Anti-Lebanon.
And the Lord disregarded me for your sakes, and did not hearken unto me; and the Lord said unto me: Let it suffice you; speak no more of this matter.

Go up unto the summit of the Hewn Place, and lift up your eyes toward the sea, and northward, and toward the southwest, and eastward, and behold with your eyes; for you shall not pass over this Jordan.
And command Joshua, and strengthen him, and encourage him; for he shall pass over before this people, and he shall cause them to inherit the land which you have seen.
And we dwelt in the valley near the house of Peor.

verses.text: And Moses finished speaking all these words unto all the sons of Israel.
And he said unto them, I am a hundred and twenty years old this day; I shall no longer be able to go in and come out. And the Lord said unto me, You shall not cross this Jordan.

The Lord your God, who goes before your face, shall Himself destroy these nations from before your face, and you shall take possession of them; and Joshua shall go before your face, as the Lord has spoken.
And the Lord shall do unto them as He did unto Sihon and Og, the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, and unto their land, when He destroyed them.
And the Lord delivered them unto you, and you shall do unto them as I commanded you.

Be courageous and strong; fear not, neither be fainthearted, neither be terrified before their face; for the Lord your God, who goes before you, is with you and among you. He will in no wise fail you, neither will He forsake you.

And Moses called Joshua, and said unto him before all Israel, Be courageous and strong; for you shall go before the face of this people into the land which the Lord sware unto our fathers to give unto them, and you shall give it unto them for an inheritance.
And the Lord who goes with you will not fail you, neither will He forsake you; fear not, neither be fainthearted.
And Moses wrote the words of this law in a book, and gave it unto the priests, the sons of Levi, who bear the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and unto the elders of the sons of Israel.
And Moses commanded them in that day, saying, After seven years, at the appointed time of the year of release, at the Feast of the Pitching of Tents,
when all Israel comes together to appear before the Lord your God in the place which the Lord shall choose, you shall read this law before all Israel in their hearing.

Gather the people, the men, and the women, and the children, and the sojourner who is in your cities, that they may hear, and that they may learn to fear the Lord your God; and they shall hearken to do all the words of this law.
And their sons, who do not know, shall hear and learn to fear the Lord your God all the days that they live upon the land into which you are crossing the Jordan to inherit it.

And the Lord said unto Moses, Behold, the days of your death draw near; call Joshua, and stand beside the doors of the Tent of Testimony, and I will command him. And Moses and Joshua went unto the Tent of Testimony, and stood beside the doors of the Tent of Testimony.
And the Lord descended in a cloud, and stood beside the doors of the Tent of Testimony; and the pillar of the cloud stood beside the doors of the Tent.

And the Lord said unto Moses, Behold, you shall sleep with your fathers; and this people shall arise and go a-whoring after the foreign gods of the land into which it goes; and they shall forsake Me, and break My covenant which I made with them.

And I will be kindled in wrath against them in that day, and will forsake them, and turn My face from them; and the people shall be devoured, and many evils and afflictions shall find it. And it shall say in that day, Because the Lord my God is not within me, these evils have found me.
But I will surely turn My face from them in that day, because of all the wickedness which they have done, for they have turned unto foreign gods.
And now write the words of this song, and teach it unto the sons of Israel, and put it in their mouth, that this song may be a witness for Me among the sons of Israel.

For I will bring them into the good land which I sware unto their fathers to give unto them, a land flowing with milk and honey; and they shall eat, and be filled, and be sated; and they shall turn unto foreign gods, and serve them, and provoke Me, and break My covenant.

And this song shall stand against them, bearing witness before their face; for it shall in no wise be forgotten from their mouth, nor from the mouth of their seed. For I know their wickedness, all that they do here this day, before I bring them into the good land which I sware unto their fathers.
And Moses wrote this song in that day, and taught it unto the sons of Israel.
And Moses commanded Joshua, and said unto him, Be courageous and strong; for you shall bring the sons of Israel into the land which the Lord sware unto them, and He shall be with you.
And when Moses had finished writing all the words of this law in a book, even unto the end,
he commanded the Levites who bear the ark of the covenant of the Lord, saying,
Take this book of the law, and lay it beside the ark of the covenant of the Lord your God; and it shall be there for a witness against you.
For I know your provocation and your stiff neck; for while I yet live with you this day, you have been provoking God: how much more after my death!
Gather unto me your tribal chiefs, and your elders, and your judges, and your recording officers, that I may speak all these words in their hearing, and call heaven and earth to witness unto them.

For I know that after my death you shall deal utterly lawlessly, and turn aside from the way which I commanded you; and evils shall meet you in the latter days, because you shall do that which is evil before the Lord, to provoke Him to anger by the works of your hands.
And Moses spoke in the hearing of all the assembly of Israel the words of this song, even unto the end:

verses.text: Give ear, O heaven, and I will speak; and let the earth hear the words of my mouth.
Let my utterance be awaited as the rain, and let my words descend as the dew, as a shower upon the grass, and as snow upon the herbage.
For I have called upon the name of the Lord; ascribe greatness unto our God.
God—true are His works, and all His ways are judgments; a faithful God, and there is no unrighteousness; righteous and holy is the Lord.
Blemished children, not His, have sinned—a crooked and perverse generation.
Do you thus repay the Lord, O foolish people and unwise? Is not He Himself your Father, who acquired you, and made you, and created you?
Remember the days of old; consider the years of generation upon generation. Ask your father, and he shall declare unto you; your elders, and they shall tell you.
When the Most High divided the nations, when He scattered the sons of Adam, He set the bounds of the nations according to the number of the angels of God.
And His people Jacob became the portion of the Lord; Israel, the measured lot of His inheritance.
He sustained him in a wilderness land, in the thirst of burning heat, in a waterless place; He compassed him about, and instructed him, and kept him as the pupil of an eye.
As an eagle would shelter its nest, it yearned over its young; spreading its wings, it received them, and took them up upon its back.
The Lord alone led them, and there was no foreign god with them.
He brought them up upon the strength of the earth, and fed them the produce of the fields; they sucked honey out of the rock, and oil out of the solid rock,
butter of cattle and milk of sheep, with the fat of lambs and rams, young bulls and goats, with the fat of the kernels of wheat; and they drank wine, the blood of the grape.
And Jacob ate and was filled, and the beloved one kicked; he grew fat, he grew thick, he grew broad; and he forsook God who made him, and departed from God his Saviour.
They provoked Me with foreign gods; with their abominations they embittered Me.
They sacrificed unto demons, and not unto God, unto gods whom they did not know; new ones, lately come, whom their fathers did not know.
You forsook God who begat you, and forgot God who nourishes you.
And the Lord saw, and was jealous, and was provoked by the anger of His sons and daughters.
And He said, I will turn My face from them, and show what shall befall them at the last; for they are a perverse generation, sons in whom is no faithfulness.

They made Me jealous with that which is no god; they provoked Me to anger with their idols. And I will make them jealous with that which is no nation; with a nation without understanding will I provoke them to anger.
For a fire has been kindled out of My wrath; it shall burn unto Hades beneath, devour the earth and its produce, and set ablaze the foundations of the mountains.
I will gather evils against them, and spend My arrows upon them.

They shall waste away with hunger, and be devoured by birds, and suffer incurable backward-bending spasms; I will send against them the teeth of wild beasts, with the fury of things that crawl upon the ground.
Without, the sword shall bereave them; and from the inner chambers, terror: the young man together with the maiden, the nursing child with the aged elder.
I said, I will scatter them; I will make their remembrance cease from among men,
were it not for the wrath of enemies, lest they endure long, and lest the adversaries join in the attack; lest they say, Our hand is exalted, and the Lord has not done all these things.
For it is a nation that has lost counsel, and there is no knowledge in them.
They did not have the wisdom to understand these things; let them receive them for the time to come.
How shall one pursue a thousand, and two put tens of thousands to flight, unless God had sold them, and the Lord had delivered them up?
For their gods are not as our God; and our enemies are without understanding.
For their vine is of the vine of Sodom, and their tendril is of Gomorrah; their grape is a grape of gall, their cluster is bitterness.
Their wine is the venom of serpents, and the incurable venom of asps.
Behold, are not these things gathered with Me, and sealed in My treasuries?
In the day of vengeance I will repay, in the season when their foot shall slip; for the day of their destruction is near, and the things prepared for you are at hand.
For the Lord shall judge His people, and be moved concerning His servants; for He saw them weakened, and failing under assault, and exhausted.
And the Lord said, Where are their gods, in whom they trusted,
whose sacrifices’ fat you ate, and whose drink offerings’ wine you drank? Let them arise and help you, and become your protectors.
See, see that I am, and there is no god beside Me. I will put to death, and make alive; I will smite, and I will heal; and there is none that shall deliver out of My hands.
For I will lift My hand unto heaven, and swear by My right hand, and say, I live for ever.
For I will sharpen My sword as lightning, and My hand shall lay hold of judgment; and I will repay a penalty unto the enemies, and unto them that hate Me will I repay.
I will make My arrows drunk with blood, and My sword shall devour flesh, from the blood of the slain and of captives, from the head of the rulers of the enemies.

Rejoice, O heavens, together with Him, and let all the sons of God worship Him; rejoice, O nations, with His people, and let all the angels of God give Him strength; for He avenges the blood of His sons, and shall avenge and repay a penalty unto the enemies, and unto them that hate Him shall He repay; and the Lord shall thoroughly cleanse the land of His people.
And Moses wrote this song in that day, and taught it unto the sons of Israel. And Moses came in and spoke all the words of this law in the hearing of the people, he and Joshua the son of Nun.
And Moses finished speaking unto all Israel,
and said unto them, Give heed in your heart unto all these words which I testify unto you this day, which you shall command your sons to keep and to do, even all the words of this law.
For this is no empty word unto you; for this is your life, and by this word you shall prolong your days upon the land into which you are crossing the Jordan to inherit it.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses in that day, saying,
Go up into this mountain of Abarim, Mount Nebo, which is in the land of Moab over against Jericho, and behold the land of Canaan, which I give unto the sons of Israel for a possession.
And die in the mountain whither you go up, and be gathered unto your people, as Aaron your brother died in Mount Hor, and was gathered unto his people;
because you disobeyed My word among the sons of Israel at the water of dispute at Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin, because you did not sanctify Me among the sons of Israel.
For you shall see the land from over against it, but you shall not go in thither.

verses.text: And Moses went up from Araboth of Moab unto Mount Nebo, unto the summit of Pisgah, which is over against Jericho; and the Lord showed him all the land of Gilead unto Dan,
and all the land of Naphtali, and all the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, and all the land of Judah unto the farthest sea,
and the wilderness, and the country round about Jericho, the city of palms, unto Zoar.

And the Lord said unto Moses, This is the land which I sware unto Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, saying, I will give it unto your seed. And I have showed it unto your eyes, but you shall not go in thither.
And Moses, the household servant of the Lord, died in the land of Moab by the word of the Lord.
And they buried him in Gai, in the land of Moab, near the house of Peor; and no man knows his burial place unto this day.
And Moses was a hundred and twenty years old when he died; his eyes were not dimmed, neither were his cheeks wasted away.
And the sons of Israel wept for Moses in Araboth of Moab, at the Jordan over against Jericho, thirty days; and the days of mourning and weeping for Moses were ended.
And Joshua the son of Nun was filled with a spirit of understanding; for Moses had laid his hands upon him; and the sons of Israel hearkened unto him, and did as the Lord commanded Moses.
And there arose no more a prophet in Israel like unto Moses, whom the Lord knew face to face,
in all the signs and wonders which the Lord sent him to do in the land of Egypt unto Pharaoh, and unto his servants, and unto all his land,
the great wonders and the mighty hand which Moses wrought before all Israel.
